notes: Merged the two guards in isValidAudioBitrate into a single condition, as the Swift diff does.
Merged the nested allowedSchemes check in isValidUrl into a single if, keeping the same message.
Everything else is unchanged from the previous Kotlin translation.

Swift's synthesised Codable for enums with associated values uses the externally tagged form {"case":{...}}, so each sealed class gets a hand-written KSerializer that reproduces that exact JSON, including {} for payload-less cases.
MoblinkResult has no raw values in Swift but is Codable, so it encodes as {"ok":{}}; it is an enum class with rawValue/fromRawValue plus MoblinkResultSerializer producing that single-key object.
moblinkJson uses explicitNulls = false to match Swift's encodeIfPresent, so nil batteryPercentage/thermalState/data keys are omitted instead of written as null.
Optional payload fields get Kotlin default null so a missing key decodes like Swift's decodeIfPresent.
Swift JSONEncoder writes UUID as an uppercase string; MoblinkUuidSerializer reproduces that and accepts any case when decoding.
UInt16 port is translated to UShort per the wire-format rule; kotlinx.serialization serialises it as a plain unsigned JSON number.

The Swift 'Not a UTF-8 string' / 'Encode failed' guards disappear: Kotlin Strings are already decodable, so fromJson just throws SerializationException on bad input and toJson() on MoblinkMessageToRelay still returns null via runCatching.
Sealed subclass names are capitalised (StartTunnel, Status, Hello, ...) but the JSON keys stay byte-identical to the Swift case names.
[[UInt8]] maps to MutableList<UByteArray>: the 2D grayscale buffer stays byte-oriented and mutates in place like the Swift arrays.
UByte comparisons need toInt() (UByte has no compareTo(Int)), so pixel reads are widened where arithmetic happens.
Swift's ternary threshold becomes a Kotlin if/else; newColor stays Int so the diff arithmetic is unchanged.
Int division by 8 keeps Kotlin's truncate-toward-zero semantics, matching Swift for negative diffs.
guard with multiple conditions becomes an early return with a negated conjunction, preserving the exact bounds check.
min/max clamping becomes coerceIn(0, 255) before converting back with toUByte().
The instance keeps the same mutable state fields (image, width, height) and the same apply/adjustPixel call order.
No Apple frameworks are used, so there is nothing unsupported.
Swift's `extension Bool { var uint8: UInt8 }` becomes a top-level extension property `val Boolean.uint8: UByte` in this file.
UInt8 maps to UByte; Kotlin has no UByte literal syntax, so the values are written as `1u.toUByte()` and `0u.toUByte()`.
The property is a getter-only computed property, matching the Swift read-only computed property.
Swift extends the ExpressibleByIntegerLiteral protocol; Kotlin has no such common supertype for primitives, so `data` is declared once per integer type instead.
Memory layout in Swift's withUnsafeBytes is native byte order, which is little-endian on both Apple and Android platforms; java.nio.ByteBuffer.LITTLE_ENDIAN reproduces it exactly.
Byte.data is a direct byteArrayOf(this) because a single byte needs no buffer.
Unsigned types (UByte/UShort/UInt/ULong) are included so call sites using unsigned literals still compile; UByte reuses the Byte path.
Extension properties are top-level in the file, matching the Swift extension in a separate file.
No top-level types are declared here, only extension properties, so declared_types is empty.
The file-private Swift constant averageSampleCount becomes a private top-level const val; it is only used inside this file.
Both Swift classes are non-final, so they are translated as open class with open functions; the private stored properties stay non-open.
The UInt16 crank revolution and event-time counters are wire values from the CSC characteristic, so they stay UShort and are converted with toInt() (which yields the unsigned value for UShort).

ContinuousClock.now / ContinuousClock.Instant come from com.moblin.android.platform.core; the three second stale timeout is written as .duration(to = now) > 3.seconds with kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.seconds imported.
Swift's values.reduce(0, +) is DoubleArray.sum() and Array(repeating:count:) is DoubleArray(n).
Swift's min(cadence, 10000) is minOf(cadence, 10000.0); Int(averageCadence.averageIgnoreZeros()) is Double.toInt(), which truncates toward zero like Swift.
The Swift shadowed optional bindings inside update(revolutions:time:) are translated with local vals so the assignments to the stored previous* properties stay writes to the properties.
Merged the two guard checks in getStats into a single condition, matching the new Swift guard with comma-separated conditions.
The Swift defer block still runs after the tuple value is built, so the counters are captured into result before being reset, as before.
outputInterval stays a private const in the companion object, referenced as Self.outputInterval does in Swift.
Pixel bytes stay UByte (matching Swift's UInt8) inside MutableList<MutableList<UByte>>; every arithmetic step converts with toInt() first because Kotlin has no implicit unsigned promotion.
The threshold test uses this.image[y][x].toInt() > 127 instead of comparing a UByte with an unsigned literal, avoiding cross-width unsigned comparison ambiguity.
Swift's value semantics are preserved by copying the incoming rows into fresh MutableLists, so the caller's array is not mutated.
Integer division (diff * 7 / 16 etc.) truncates toward zero in both languages, so the error diffusion weights are byte-identical.
clamping uses coerceIn(0, 255).toUByte(), the equivalent of Swift's UInt8(min(255, max(0, value))).
The private state (image, width, height) is kept exactly as in Swift so instances can be reused exactly like the original.
The method name apply is retained for side-by-side reading; it resolves to the member function because the stdlib scope function apply requires a lambda argument.
AVCaptureColorSpace is an AVFoundation type with no Android counterpart, so it is declared in this file as an enum class that keeps the Swift case names, raw values and a companion fromRawValue.
The Swift `description` computed property in the extension becomes a top-level Kotlin extension property on AVCaptureColorSpace in this same package.
CustomStringConvertible has no Kotlin equivalent; toString() is overridden on the enum to delegate to description so string interpolation matches Swift.
Raw values follow AVFoundation (sRGB = 1, P3_D65 = 2, HLG_BT2020 = 3, appleLog = 4); verify against the platform header if these numbers are ever persisted or sent over the wire.
The Swift `default:` branch is kept as `else -> "Unknown"` so values that do not map to a known case keep the same output.
If another Moblin module already declares AVCaptureColorSpace, remove the declaration here and import that one instead.
Kotlin enums are closed, so unknown platform values can only be represented by a null return from fromRawValue or by the else branch of description.
Swift's `Any` maps to Kotlin's `Any?`; the parameter is nullable so callers can pass anything.
Swift `Int` is 64-bit while Kotlin `Int` is 32-bit, so a boxed `Long` value will not match the `is Int` branch; use `Long` at call sites only if that parity is required.
The value is matched with Kotlin `is` checks, which correspond exactly to Swift's conditional `as?` casts, including falling through to `false` for any other type.
No Android or Apple frameworks are used, so the translation is complete and compiles as-is.
CoreAudio is not available on Android, so the `AudioStreamBasicDescription` struct itself is declared here as a Kotlin `data class` with the nine fields used by the Swift extension.

The Swift extension only adds `Equatable`; in Kotlin the data class generates `equals`/`hashCode` over exactly the same nine properties, so the `==` implementation is reproduced without an explicit operator.

Fields are mutable (`var`) to mirror the mutability of the imported Swift C struct, and are declared in the canonical CoreAudio order (`mSampleRate`, `mFormatID`, `mFormatFlags`, `mBytesPerPacket`, `mFramesPerPacket`, `mBytesPerFrame`, `mChannelsPerFrame`, `mBitsPerChannel`, `mReserved`).
The `UInt32` fields are mapped to Kotlin `UInt` because an audio stream format description is wire-format/byte-parsing data, and `mSampleRate` (`Float64`) is mapped to `Double`.
All fields are defaulted to `0u`/`0.0` so a zeroed format description can be built without arguments, matching C's zero-initialised struct.
No `CoreAudio` symbol remains to be stubbed, so no `TODO()` and no unsupported entries are needed.
BitrateStatsInstant is a plain value holder, so it becomes a data class with ULong properties like the Swift UInt64 ones.
BitrateStats mutates its own stored state, so it is translated as a Kotlin class instead of a data class; no copy-on-write value semantics are needed by the algorithm.
private(set) members become public properties with a private setter (totalBytes and latestSpeed).
Swift's default parameter value 100 becomes the ULong default 100uL on the constructor.
add(bytesTransferred:) converts the Int argument with toULong() before adding it to the running total.
The subtraction (100 - speedChangeRate) is kept as unsigned ULong arithmetic, matching the Swift expression exactly.
The smoothing formula uses the same multiplication/addition/division-by-100 ordering as Swift, so results are bit-identical.
The mutating funcs become regular member functions and return BitrateStatsInstant directly, as in the Swift source.
Swift UInt32 bitrate values became Int: this port reserves UByte/UShort/UInt/ULong for wire-format code, and bitrates are never negative.
`weak let delegate` has no Kotlin equivalent; it is stored as a plain nullable reference, so the delegate is not weakly held.
ContinuousClock.Instant mapped to monotonic System.nanoTime() nanoseconds (type Long) so the 15 second expiry test is immune to wall-clock jumps.
swift-collections Deque mapped to kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque (firstOrNull peek, addLast, removeFirst).
DateFormatter mapped to java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter with the system default zone, formatting an Instant.
logger.debug mapped to android.util.Log.d with tag "AdaptiveBitrate".
The Swift method-name typo logAdaptiveAcion is preserved verbatim so both codebases read side by side.
limitByTransportBitrate keeps Swift's integer arithmetic (17 * transportBitrate) / 10 using maxOf/minOf on Long.
The caseless Swift `enum AudioSpecificConfig` used only as a namespace becomes a Kotlin `object` holding three nested `enum class` types, preserving the nesting and declaration order.
UInt8 raw values are mapped to UByte (MPEG-4 ASC values are byte-level wire data); literal values use the `u` suffix.
Each enum gets a `companion object` with `fromRawValue(value: UByte)` to mirror the `init?(rawValue:)` initializer Swift synthesizes for raw-value enums.

Enum case names are kept byte-identical to the Swift names (lowerCamelCase, e.g. `aacLc`, `hz44100`, `frontLeftAndFrontRight`) so the two codebases can be read side by side instead of being renamed to SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.
`SamplingFrequency.sampleRate` (Float64) becomes a computed `val sampleRate: Double` implemented with a `when (this)` expression; the values and their order match the Swift switch.
No imports are required; the file only declares nested enums and one numeric mapping.
No Apple platform frameworks are used, so nothing needed a TODO().
Data is mapped to ByteArray; the private(set) setters become Kotlin 'private set'.
top-level 'let nalUnitEmulationPreventionByte' becomes a top-level const val of type UByte to stay in wire-format semantics.
UInt8 bit-write APIs use UByte and UInt32 uses UInt, matching the wire-format mapping rules.
Swift Data.insert(at:) has no ByteArray counterpart, so insertEmulationPreventionByteIfNeeded reallocates the buffer and copies both segments with ByteArray.copyInto.
Swift '|=' on a Data byte is expressed as an explicit toInt() or mask then toByte().
The emulation-prevention toggle is kept as a private val field declared after data/bitOffset to preserve the Swift declaration order.
writeRawBytes keeps 'self.data += data' as an explicit this.data = this.data + data assignment.
URL extension becomes a java.net.URI extension because this file parses URL components, not a stored string.

absoluteWithoutAuthenticationString rebuilds the URI with the 7-argument java.net.URI constructor passing a null userInfo, which drops both user and password; java.net.URISyntaxException is caught with runCatching.
When the URI has no user info the original toString() is returned verbatim, so URIs are not needlessly re-normalised.
dictionaryFromQuery works on rawQuery and percent-decodes names and values itself; the '+' character is kept literal, matching Foundation's URLComponents.
Query items without '=' are skipped, matching the Swift `if let value` check.
The helper percentDecode is a private top-level function used only by dictionaryFromQuery.
Malformed percent escapes are decoded leniently instead of yielding an empty map as URLComponents would.
File-scope `let defaultStunServer` becomes a top-level `const val defaultStunServer` with the identical name and value.
`setupWebrtcDebugLogging()` keeps its signature but its body only calls `rtcInitLogger`, which comes from the libdatachannel C library; no Kotlin binding exists in this port, so the body is a TODO().
The debug-log callback would have been translated to `android.util.Log.i` with the class name as tag, but it is unreachable because the registration call is a TODO().
No Apple-only framework is used here; the only missing piece is the native WebRTC logger bridge.
When a JNI wrapper for libdatachannel is added, `setupWebrtcDebugLogging()` should register a callback that forwards the C string to `Log.i("WebrtcCommon", "webrtc: $message")`.
Two top-level Swift functions become top-level Kotlin functions in com.moblin.android.streamingplatforms.twitch.
The Swift switch with implicit case values becomes a Kotlin `when` expression returning Int, with the same 1/2/3/default mapping.
The Swift tuple (moving:still:) has no Kotlin equivalent, so it is modelled by a small data class TwitchEmoteUrls with properties in the same order.
URL is translated to String because these URLs are only built and passed on for image loading, never parsed.
The Swift optional return survives a failing URL(string:) call; Kotlin string concatenation cannot fail, so the nullable return type is kept only for call-site fidelity.
No Apple framework is used, so the unsupported list is empty.
Crc32 remains a class with a private constructor and a companion object holding the single `mpeg2` instance, mirroring Swift's `static let mpeg2`.
Swift `Data` becomes `ByteArray`; CRC arithmetic keeps unsigned semantics with `UInt`/`UIntArray` since this is wire-format bit math.
Kotlin's infix bitwise functions (`and`, `shl`, `xor`) are all left-associative and bind looser than `==`, so the Swift expressions were parenthesised to keep the exact same evaluation order.
The Swift constructor parameter `polynomial` is kept as a constructor parameter, not a property, and is only used while building the lookup table.
The table build loop, the 0xFFFFFFFF seed and the byte-sequential update loop are translated literally, including the wrap-around `shl 24` for indices 128..255.
`data[i].toUInt() and 0xFFu` reproduces Swift's `UInt32(data[i]) & 0xFF`, so negative bytes cannot sign-extend into the index.
No Apple platform framework is used in this file, so nothing is stubbed with TODO().
@MainActor is translated to a CoroutineScope bound to Dispatchers.Main, so both handlers run on the main thread exactly like the main-queue DispatchSourceTimer in Swift.

DispatchSourceTimer single-shot and repeating schedules become coroutine Jobs driven by delay(): the single shot delays 'timeout' then runs, the periodic timer delays 'initial ?? interval', runs, then loops with 'interval' delays.
Double seconds are converted to Long milliseconds for delay(); sub-millisecond precision is lost.

The Swift 'isolated deinit { stop() }' has no deterministic Kotlin counterpart because Kotlin objects are not deinitialized eagerly; callers must call stop() (the timer Job keeps the scope alive otherwise).
The stored 'timer' property keeps its Swift name and now holds a Job? instead of an optional DispatchSourceTimer.
stop() cancels the Job and resets the property to null, matching timer?.cancel(); timer = nil.
The 'initial: Double? = nil' optional parameter is preserved as a Kotlin nullable parameter with a default value.
The `handler` closure becomes a nullable `(String) -> Unit` property; call it with `handler?.invoke(line)`.
The `@autoclosure` parameter of `debug` is translated to a `() -> String` lambda so the message is only evaluated when `debugEnabled` is true.
Swift's `DateFormatter` is replaced by a thread-safe `java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter` held in the companion object; `Instant.now()` is converted with the system default zone before formatting.

The compile-time `#if DEBUG` print is replaced by an unconditional `android.util.Log.d` with tag `EasyLogger`; R8/ProGuard or a `BuildConfig.DEBUG` check can be added if release stripping is required.
The global `nonisolated(unsafe) let logger` becomes a top-level `val logger`, initialised once when the file's class is loaded.
`makeTimestamp` and `log` stay `private` instance members and the timestamp prefix format `HH:mm:ss.SSS` is preserved byte-for-byte.
`nonisolated(unsafe)` has no Kotlin counterpart; the singleton is a plain top-level property whose mutable state is not synchronised (same as the Swift original).
Swift enums used purely as namespaces of static constants become Kotlin objects.
UInt16 port constants are translated to Int (const val) because java.net Socket/ServerSocket/DatagramSocket APIs take Int ports and the values fit comfortably.
Values are compile-time constants so they use const val, mirroring Swift 'static let' semantics.
Names and declaration order are preserved exactly for side-by-side reading.
No Apple frameworks, so the unsupported list is empty.
OSAllocatedUnfairLock has no Android counterpart and is replaced by java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock (non-fair, like the Swift lock) used through kotlin.concurrent.withLock.
The Swift Sendable constraints are dropped: Kotlin generics are unconstrained, so Atomic<A> and mutate<R> are plain generics.
Swift's inout A cannot be expressed in Kotlin, so mutate hands the transform a nested mutable holder MutableRef<A>; callers read and write ref.value instead of using $0.
Atomic is a class rather than a data class because instances own a lock and mutable state; value semantics would copy the lock.
value stays a read-only property whose getter reads the state under the lock, mirroring Swift's computed var.
mutate executes the transform while holding the lock and returns R unchanged; the primary constructor parameter is named initialValue to avoid shadowing the value property.
Call sites such as atomic.mutate { $0.count += 1 } become atomic.mutate { it.value.count += 1 }.
No Apple-only framework is used, so the unsupported list is empty.
Swift Data becomes ByteArray; the private(set) data property stays publicly readable but is mutated through local copies, matching Swift value semantics.
UInt8/UInt16/UInt32/UInt64 map to UByte/UShort/UInt/ULong because this is wire-format byte handling; Int32 maps to Int.
The Data.bigEndian.data and Double.data.reversed() extensions from the HaishinKit extensions file are inlined with java.nio.ByteBuffer using BIG_ENDIAN order.
writeBytes(UnsafeRawBufferPointer) is translated to an overload taking java.nio.ByteBuffer, consuming its remaining bytes via duplicate() so the caller's position is untouched.
In sequence(_:lambda:) the trailing `data.advanced(by: data.endIndex - r)` is treated as the remainder slice data[count-r ..< count] and wrapped in a new ByteWriter.
UInt32(data:) used by toUInt32() is reimplemented inline reading 4 bytes big-endian from the region starting at position.
Both Swift initialisers are kept as Kotlin secondary constructors.
The subscript is translated to operator get/set with UByte values, writing into the backing signed ByteArray.
Data maps to ByteArray and the private(set) var data becomes a var with a private setter; the Swift init(data:) becomes the primary constructor in the class header.
The private Swift.Error enum is translated to a private sealed class Error with the nested objects eof and utf8 so thrown failures keep the same names.

readUInt16 and readUInt32 no longer use the UnsafeRawBufferPointer helpers (which do not exist in Kotlin) and assemble the bytes explicitly big-endian, matching the high/low ordering of readUInt64 and the separate readUInt16Le/readUInt32Le variants.

readDouble keeps the Swift semantics verbatim: it consumes 8 bytes, reverses them and decodes them as a little-endian double, which is identical to decoding the untouched bytes big-endian as AMF0 requires.
defer { position += n } became an explicit increment placed after the read value has been captured.
readUtf8Bytes uses a strict UTF-8 decoder with CodingErrorAction.REPORT so malformed input throws Error.utf8 exactly like Swift's String(data:encoding:).
Unsigned wire values use UByte, UShort, UInt and ULong; callers outside this file therefore see Kotlin unsigned types.
skipBytes and readBytes keep the length >= 0 precondition and throw Error.eof on short buffers.
DispatchSourceTimer + DispatchQueue are replaced by a CoroutineScope backed by the given CoroutineDispatcher; the timer field holds the running Job.
Double seconds are converted to Long milliseconds for kotlinx.coroutines delay.
Swift's deinit calling stop() becomes AutoCloseable.close(), which calls stop(); callers should call close() when done.
The handler is a plain () -> Unit lambda; @Sendable has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped.
startPeriodic fires the first handler invocation after `initial ?: interval` and then repeats every interval, matching the Swift schedule.
startSingleShot and startPeriodic still call stop() first, so a previously running timer is always cancelled.

Swift's Data byte-reading extension methods (getUInt16Be/getUInt32Be) are not declared in this file and no shared byte-reader package was provided, so they are re-implemented here as file-private helpers readUInt16Be/readUInt32Be on ByteArray.
16-bit and 32-bit wire values are kept as UShort/UInt as prescribed for byte-parsing code; callers using the packet type should use SrtPacketType.fromRawValue(type).
packet[0] is a signed Byte in Kotlin, so the Swift UInt8 mask test became (packet[0].toInt() and 0x80) == 0.
SRT sequence numbers rely on wrapping unsigned arithmetic; Kotlin's UInt operators already wrap, so Swift's &- is no longer needed in processSrtNak.
SrtPacketType keeps the Swift lowerCamelCase entry names so both files can be read side by side; rawValue stays a UShort with identical raw values.
Swift's guard offset <= packet.count - 4 else { return } became an early return; the guard ... else { continue } became if (upToNakSn - fromNakSn >= 100_000u) continue.
The Swift closed range fromNakSn ... upToNakSn maps to fromNakSn..upToNakSn; a descending range is empty in Kotlin instead of trapping as it does in Swift (only reachable in a wrap-around edge case).
srtControlTypeSize is a const val Int and srtControlPacketTypeBit stays a top-level val UShort, matching the file-scope lets in Swift.
Keychain is backed by androidx.security:security-crypto EncryptedSharedPreferences (1.1.x) with a MasterKey using AES256_GCM; keys use AES256_SIV and values AES256_GCM.

The Swift version got the security context implicitly; here the application Context must be assigned to Keychain.appContext at app start, otherwise store/load/remove log and no-op and loadStreamIds returns an empty list.

Each server maps to its own encrypted preferences file named 'moblin_keychain_' + SHA-256 hex of the server, so that the static loadStreamIds(server) can enumerate all account names (streamIds) belonging to that server, like the kSecAttrServer query did.
Each streamId is the SharedPreferences key inside its server's file, matching kSecAttrAccount.

update/add use commit() instead of apply() so the Swift success/failure logging semantics are preserved; SharedPreferences has no separate update vs add, so update() only succeeds when the key already exists and store() falls back to add().
logger.info is replaced by android.util.Log.i with the tag "Keychain" (the class name).
The Swift guard on value.data(using: .utf8) is dropped since Kotlin String -> UTF-8 conversion cannot fail.
SharedPreferences files are cached per server in a synchronized map, and creation failures (GeneralSecurityException/IOException) are caught and logged like the original keychain status errors.
CMVideoDimensions is a CoreMedia struct with no Android counterpart, so it is mapped to android.util.Size; the Swift extension methods become top-level Kotlin extension functions on Size.
The @retroactive Equatable conformance needs no Kotlin code: android.util.Size already implements equals()/hashCode().
toSize() returns android.util.SizeF, the Float width/height analogue of CGSize (CoreGraphics CGFloat -> Float per the port rules).
convertTo(dimension:) keeps the Swift optional return type (Size?) and the odd-size rounding: the derived dimension is incremented when it is odd; it never actually returns null.
Int32 arithmetic maps to Kotlin Int; Swift traps on overflow while Kotlin wraps, which is unreachable for realistic video dimensions.
`public import AVFoundation` has no Kotlin equivalent; only android.util.Size and android.util.SizeF are imported.
Function names, parameter names and body order follow the Swift source; visibility is Kotlin's default public so other port files can call them.
ObservableObject with @Published became a private MutableStateFlow backing field plus a public read-only StateFlow named followUser / followHeading, matching the _name/name convention.

Because Swift hand-writes encode(to:) and init(from:) over @Published properties, the class uses @Serializable(with = SettingsNavigationSerializer::class) and a hand-written KSerializer that mirrors the Swift container encode/decode calls.
The Swift decoder defaults were false for both keys; deserialize() starts both locals at false so a missing key keeps the Swift behaviour.
The nested CodingKeys enum kept its name and nesting and stores the serialized key string in stringValue (the CodingKey.stringValue counterpart).
The Swift no-argument init() is preserved as a secondary constructor that delegates to the internal primary constructor with false/false.
The primary constructor is internal so the serializer in the same package can build an instance, matching the Swift required init(from:) role.
No Apple-only frameworks are used in this file, so nothing was replaced with TODO().
No comments were added; the full file is a single Kotlin file in com.moblin.android.various.settings.
Swift Character (grapheme cluster) indexing is translated to Kotlin UTF-16 Char indexing, so matches can differ for strings containing combining marks or non-BMP emoji.
The Swift `for shift in minShift ... maxShift` closed range can never be empty here because minShift <= 0 <= maxShift, so Kotlin's `minShift..maxShift` is safe.
Swift `func update(text newText: String)` becomes `fun update(newText: String)`; the external label is dropped as Kotlin has no argument labels.
`String.index(_:offsetBy:)` calls are replaced by direct Char indexing, with the same bounds guarantees (endOffset keeps offset + shift within oldText).
`abs`, `minOf` and `maxOf` come from kotlin.math and the Kotlin stdlib and preserve the original comparison semantics exactly.
Exactly one edit remains: there is no edit, as the source is pure logic with no Apple frameworks.
The `text` property stays private and is only mutated inside `update`; `position` remains a public var so callers keep the same API.
No coroutines, serialization or platform APIs are needed; the file is a self-contained class.
Subtitles is a plain class; the Swift `let length` computed in init becomes a Kotlin `val length` assigned once in an init block.
String length/indexing uses Kotlin UTF-16 offsets (`text.length`, `substring`) instead of Swift Character-based indices, so offsets differ for text containing surrogate pairs such as emoji.
`max(lastLinePosition, 0)` becomes `maxOf(lastLinePosition, 0)` since `max` is removed from Kotlin stdlib.
`.trim()` maps to Kotlin's built-in `String.trim()`, which trims whitespace like Moblin's String.trim() extension, so no extra extension is declared here.
The inner `offset` that shadows the outer one in updateSubtitles is kept with the same name for side-by-side readability (Kotlin emits a shadowing warning only).
`var lines: [String]` becomes `MutableList<String>` and array literals become `mutableListOf(...)` since `lines` is reassigned.
The `guard` statements become early returns, including the `offset < text.count` guard inside the firstLinePosition branch.
ObservableObject with @Published properties became private MutableStateFlow backing fields with public StateFlow exposure; setEnabled/setMicId replace direct assignment from outside.
The hand-written encode(to:)/init(from:) pair is realised by SettingsTalkbackSerializer, attached with @Serializable(with = ...), so the class itself keeps no serialization boilerplate.

Persisted JSON keys remain exactly "enabled" and "micId"; the private surrogate EncodedSettings carries @SerialName for both and gives them the Swift defaults (false / ""), so missing keys decode to the same values kotlinx.serialization fallback gave in Swift.
The nested CodingKeys enum is kept as an enum class with a rawValue property and a companion fromRawValue, matching the Swift coding keys byte for byte.
The empty Swift init() is the implicit no-arg Kotlin constructor; SettingsTalkback() is used by the deserializer to build the instance before applying decoded values.
EncodedSettings is an internal implementation detail of the port and has no counterpart in the Swift source.
any Encoder / any Decoder maps to kotlinx.serialization Encoder / Decoder.
CMVideoDimensions is not given a mapping in the port spec; it is translated to android.util.Size, which has the same width/height shape and value equality.
convertTo(dimension:) is assumed to be a top-level extension function on Size declared in this same package (com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.extension), so it needs no import here.
Swift Testing struct becomes a JUnit 4 class; @Test func becomes @Test fun with org.junit.Test.
#expect(a == b) becomes assertEquals(b, a) with kotlin.test, keeping the argument order of the Swift expectation.
There is no suite-level init in the Swift struct, so no @Before fun setUp() is generated.
All width/height literals are kept byte-identical to the Swift suite.

Swift's custom init that divides by the reference image size is kept as a companion operator invoke; the primary constructor is private so call sites keep the swift spelling AlertsEffectBackgroundLandmarkRectangle(topLeftX = 40.0, ...).
The two file-level size constants stay private top-level const vals, matching Swift's private file scope.
AlertsEffectBackgroundLandmarkRectangle maps to a data class with val fields so equality and copy() behave like the Swift struct.
width() and height() stay functions (not properties) so the two codebases read side by side.
AlertsEffectFaceLandmark is an enum class; the Swift case order is preserved.
AlertsEffectLandmarkSettings is a data class with the same four val fields.
The four global rectangles are top-level vals initialised with named arguments, exactly as in Swift.
No platform frameworks are used, so there are no TODO markers.
Swift struct became a Kotlin class because it holds mutable state and methods, not a data class.
static let fixedSectionSize is exposed via a companion object property; instance code reads it as fixedSectionSize.
Data is mapped to ByteArray; Data(repeating:count:) became ByteArray(size) { 0xFF.toByte() }.
UInt8 wire values are kept as UByte as required by the byte-parsing rule; arithmetic is done in Int and converted back with toInt()/toUByte().
Swift truncatingIfNeeded conversions map directly to Int.toUByte() truncation.
reader.position is read through .toInt() so the code compiles whether the ByteReader exposes an Int or Long position.
The throwing initializer just lets ByteReader/ByteWriter exceptions propagate, matching Swift's throws.
readUInt8() is normalized to Int for bit-flag tests to avoid Kotlin unsigned bitwise pitfalls.

Adds the shoutout-create event models, delegate method, subscription type and handler exactly where the Swift diff places them.

The authError-only branch of the Swift switch has no Boolean counterpart and is folded into the failure branch.
sessionId is now reset in stopInternal() and the reconnect delay is reset in start(), matching the Swift change.
min(reconnectDelay * 2, 120) is written as minOf(reconnectDelay * 2, 120.0) because reconnectDelay is a Double.
initialReconnectDelay became a private const val so the field initialiser can use it.
Subscription is a private data class built positionally in makeSubscriptions(), its property names type/version/condition match the Swift struct.
The new public event type carries @Serializable like the other Decodable structs; the payload and message wrappers stay private.
Added the four makeChannelMap tests as list equality assertions.
convertMonoToStereo uses makePcmFormat and the AVAudioConverter/AVAudioPCMBuffer shims instead of AVAudioFormat.
PCM data is written and read through the ShortBuffer returned by int16ChannelData.

Extension imports for frameLength and int16ChannelData were added.
Existing audio-level tests left byte-identical.
Added the new modelOsmoAction6 test before modelOsmoPocket4Pro, matching the Swift order.
modelOsmoPocket4Pro now uses a `var data` local and asserts twice, once per manufacturer-data sample.
Byte literals with the high bit set keep the explicit `.toByte()` conversion already used in this file.
No new imports were needed; JUnit 4, kotlin.test and Robolectric setup are unchanged.
Swift Testing suite translated to a JUnit 4 class (org.junit.Test) with kotlin.test assertions; helper functions stay private top-level in this file.
DriftTracker calls are written positionally (DriftTracker(""), addMedia(media, fillLevel), setDrift(value), update(media, ...)) because the Kotlin signatures live in DriftTracker.kt.
createTracker() and drive() keep their Swift names and default nullable audio/video lambda parameters.
drive() accumulates into a MutableList<Double> and the tests use `+=` on a `var List<Double>`, which desugars to List.plus plus reassignment.
drift comparisons against integer literals (0, 1) were written as 0.0 so kotlin.test.assertEquals type-checks the Double value.
abs() comes from kotlin.math on the JVM.
The Swift tuple array of (media, closure) pairs becomes a listOf(media to fn) destructured in the for loop, with a `?: continue` guard replacing `guard let`.
DriftTrackerMediaState is not referenced by this file, so it is not imported.
Swift Testing suite translated to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions; each @Test becomes org.junit.Test fun and the struct becomes a plain class.
The private measurement builders keep the exact little-endian wire bytes: 0x02 + UInt16 + UInt16, 0x01 + UInt32 + UInt16 and 0x03 + UInt32 + UInt16 + UInt16 + UInt16.

Wheel revolutions stay unsigned (UInt, UInt.MAX_VALUE for Swift .max) because UInt32.max does not fit an Int; the 16-bit crank wheels and event times use Int with explicit and 0xFF masks inside the helper.
Swift UInt16 overflow 65000 &+ 1024 is written as (65000 + 1024) and 0xFFFF so the helper receives the same wrapped event time 488.
#require(speed) becomes requireNotNull(speed) before calling isEqual(actual, expected, epsilon).
handleMeasurement is called with the declared parameter name value and returns Pair<Double?, Int?> destructured into (speed, cadence).
#expect(throws: (any Error).self) becomes assertFailsWith<Exception>, because the Kotlin translation of the device throws an unchecked exception for a truncated measurement.
No test depends on locale or time zone, so no @Config qualifiers or TimeZone default are needed.
Swift Testing #expect(throws: "msg") { } is translated to kotlin.test assertFailsWith<Exception> plus an equality check on the thrown Throwable's message.
The Swift functions are `throws`; Kotlin has no checked exceptions so the calls are plain (no try/catch needed on the success paths).
@testable import Moblin is dropped because the types under test live in the same package com.moblin.android.media.rtspclient.
Test method names, order and string literals are kept byte-identical to the Swift source.
No suite-level init existed in Swift, so no @Before setUp is emitted.
If the ported error type wraps the text (e.g. prefixes the class name), the assertEquals on error.message must be adjusted to match the ported error's message/description.
Suite struct becomes a JUnit 4 class; kotlin.test assertions replace #expect.
appendTwitchRaidChannel is called with a List of SettingsStreamTwitchRaidChannel and returns the new list, matching the Swift value-semantics helper.
Local `var channels` uses immutable List plus reassignment, mirroring the Swift `var` array.
channels.map(\.channelId) becomes channels.map { it.channelId } since Kotlin has no key-path mapping.
Optional first/last uses firstOrNull()/lastOrNull() so the nil-comparison in test 3 ports directly.
maximumNumberOfTwitchRaidChannels and appendTwitchRaidChannel are imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
String interpolation of the loop index produces the same byte-identical channel ids/names as Swift.

The hand-written Codable (encode(to:) / init(from:)) is translated into a custom KSerializer; the wire format keeps the eight flat Swift coding keys via the private SettingsSelfieStickShape surrogate.

@Published properties become private MutableStateFlow backing fields (_enabled, _function, _functionData) exposed as public StateFlow, per the port's convention; mutation happens through the backing flows inside the class.
Swift's init() maps onto the Kotlin primary constructor's default arguments (enabled = false, function = switchScene, functionData = SettingsControllerFunctionData()).
Assumes SettingsControllerFunctionData exposes mutable properties sceneId, widgetId, gimbalPresetId, gimbalMotion, macroId and streamDeckLayoutId with the Swift defaults.
Assumes SettingsControllerFunction and SettingsGimbalMotion expose a String rawValue plus a companion fromRawValue(String) returning a nullable enum, so persisted raw values stay byte-identical.
UUIDs are stored as strings; a malformed or missing string decodes to null instead of throwing, matching the Swift decoder's fault tolerance.
The nested CodingKeys enum is kept only for side-by-side parity; the actual keys live in SettingsSelfieStickShape's @SerialName values.
Missing keys fall back to the same defaults as the Swift decoder: enabled=false, function=.switchScene, gimbalMotion=.kapow, ids=nil.
Swift Testing suite RistSuite becomes a JUnit 4 class RistSuite with kotlin.test assertions.
The Swift struct has no init, so no @Before setUp() is emitted.

The second Swift argument .hostPort(host: .init("1.2.3.4"), port: .imap) is an NWEndpoint; since Android has no NWEndpoint, it is passed as RistRemotePeer("1.2.3.4", 143), 143 being NWEndpoint.Port.imap.
Assertion argument order follows the contract: assertEquals(expected, actual).
Expected URL strings are kept byte-identical, including the appended weight=1 query item.
If the ported makeRistMoblinkBondingUrl takes (url: String, host: String, port: Int) rather than a RistRemotePeer, only the third test call needs adjusting.
The Swift tuple return of parse() is translated as Pair<Boolean, HttpConnectRequest?>; tests destructure it with (done, result).
Top-level setup is not needed, so no @Before method is generated.
The destination comparison assumes the ported parser exposes Connection.Endpoint.HostPort(host, port) for the Swift .hostPort(host:port:) endpoint case.
The suite therefore imports nothing from the glossary packages because the test lives in the same package com.moblin.android.various.network.
Swift's .utf8Data extension becomes Kotlin's String.encodeToByteArray().
Swift's destructuring reassignment in connectParserSplitAcrossChunks is rewritten with two mutable locals because Kotlin has no multiple assignment.
assertNotEquals and assertFailsWith are not required by this suite, so those imports are omitted.

Added the two new tests notificationActionSurvivesEncodeAndDecode and notificationActionDefaultsWhenMissingFromSettings after ifActionDefaultsWhenMissingFromSettings, matching the Swift diff position.

The new tests refer to SettingsMacrosActionFunction.NOTIFICATION and SettingsMacrosAction.notificationMessage, which the Swift change introduces; the SettingsMacros port must expose those two members for these tests to compile.
Swift .notification maps to the Kotlin enum entry NOTIFICATION following the UpperCamelCase to UPPER_SNAKE convention used by every other case in this enum.
decode/encode still go through kotlinx Json.decodeFromString/encodeToString with the Swift property names, as in the unchanged tests.
Data("{}".utf8) becomes the string literal "{}" passed to Json.decodeFromString, as in the existing default-value tests.
No other line of the file was touched; imports, formatting and declaration order are byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.
No iOS API is used in the added code, so there is no TODO marker.

HttpResponseParser.parse() returning the Swift tuple (done, data) is translated as Pair<Boolean, ByteArray?>; each call is destructured, and the second parse in a test uses done2/data2 because Kotlin has no destructuring reassignment.
Byte arrays are compared with assertContentEquals rather than assertEquals because Kotlin ByteArray equality is reference based, unlike Swift Data.
String.utf8Data becomes Kotlin String.encodeToByteArray(), Data() becomes ByteArray(0), and Data.count becomes ByteArray.size.
Data slices body[0 ..< 5] and body[5...] become ByteArray.copyOfRange(0, 5) and copyOfRange(5, body.size).
The AVFoundation import is dropped because it was unused in this suite.
The class is a JUnit 4 test class using kotlin.test assertions; @Test comes from org.junit.Test and there is no setUp because the Swift struct has no init.
#expect(data == nil) is written as assertNull(data).
Assumes HttpResponseParser exposes append(data: ByteArray) and parse(): Pair<Boolean, ByteArray?>.

The hand-written Codable conformance is translated with kotlinx.serialization surrogate classes plus custom KSerializers, keeping the flat CodingKeys (id, key, function, sceneId, widgetId, gimbalPresetId, gimbalMotion, macroId, streamDeckLayoutId).
@Published properties become private MutableStateFlow fields (private _name, public name) exposed through public var accessors so the values stay mutable for decoding and UI edits.
ObservableObject and Identifiable have no Kotlin counterpart; the id property is kept as a plain property.
UUIDs are persisted as strings via UUID.toString()/UUID.fromString(), matching JSONEncoder's treatment of UUID.
Enum raw values are persisted as strings through rawValue.toString() and resolved by scanning the enum entries, so the code does not depend on the raw value's static type.
Missing keys fall back to exactly the same defaults as the Swift container.decode helper: new UUID, empty string, unused, kapow and nulls.
With the default Json configuration (encodeDefaults = false) surrogate fields equal to their defaults are omitted when writing, but decoding always restores them.
SettingsKeyboardKeyData and SettingsKeyboardData are private file-local serialization helpers, not part of the Swift API.
Swift Testing struct RtmpStreamInfoSuite became a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions.
#expect(a == b) was rewritten as assertEquals(b, a), i.e. the Swift right-hand side is the expected value.
info.bitrateStats.mutate { $0.add(...) } is kept as info.bitrateStats.mutate { it.add(...) }, assuming the ported stats holder exposes value and mutate (e.g. a MutableStateFlow wrapper).
RTMP acknowledgement sequence numbers are wire format, so onAck takes UInt and its literals carry the u suffix (UInt32 -> UInt, Int32.max -> Int.MAX_VALUE).
onWritten takes Long, so sequence literals are plain integer literals typed by the parameter.
Counter fields (totalBytes, latestSpeed, rttMs, packetsInFlight) are asserted as Int, matching the untouched Int usage in the Swift suite.
The async onAckUpdatesRtt test is wrapped in runBlocking and calls the suspend sleep(milliSeconds:) helper from com.moblin.android.common.various positionally.
Assertions come from kotlin.test, the @Test annotation from org.junit.
Swift Testing @Test methods became JUnit 4 @Test functions with kotlin.test assertions (kotlin.test.Test aliases org.junit.Test on the JVM).
#expect(a == b) -> assertEquals(b, a); boolean expectations -> assertTrue/assertFalse, keeping the original order of cases.

Swift's try #require(URL(string:)) has no Kotlin equivalent: java.net.URI parses the same ws/wss strings and throws URISyntaxException on malformed input, which fails the test just like #require returning nil would.
The isLoopback extension is not listed in the glossary, so this file assumes NetworkUtils.kt declares URI.isLoopback() in this same package; no import is needed for a same-package extension.
Dollar signs inside expected/input string literals are escaped as \$ so Kotlin does not treat them as string templates (e.g. "a's\$b 6" and "#\$%^").
The empty Swift tuple array [] maps to emptyList(), whose element type is inferred from the makeUrl parameter type List<Pair<String, String>>.
makeUrl parameters are passed as Kotlin pairs, e.g. listOf("foo" to "bar").
The Swift suite had no init/setUp, so no @Before method is required.
JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions, matching the Swift Testing suite one-to-one.
#expect(optional/boolean) maps to assertTrue, #expect(==) maps to assertEquals with expected first and actual second.
Subtitles lives in this same package, so no import is needed for the type under test.
The Swift multiline string literals using a trailing backslash line continuation were flattened into single Kotlin string literals, preserving the trailing space before each continuation.
Subtitles(languageIdentifier: nil) becomes Subtitles(null).
updateSubtitles(position:text:) becomes updateSubtitles(position, text) as a positional call.
There is no Swift init in the suite, so no @Before setUp is emitted.
Expected line arrays keep the exact byte content, including the intentionally truncated final chunks.

CMTime has no Android counterpart in this port, so every CMTime becomes a Long number of microseconds; a private helper cmTime(value, timescale) in this file reproduces the Swift CMTime(value:timescale:) expressions.
CMTime(seconds:) values are converted with truncation: 0.02 s -> 20000L and 1/71 s -> 1_000_000L / 71 (14084 us, which formats back to 1/71).
CMTime.invalid is represented by the private sentinel invalidExposure = Long.MIN_VALUE and CMTime.zero by 0L; these must match the sentinels used by the implementation in this package.

Assumed signatures of the types under test: factorToExposure(List<Long>, Double): Long, factorFromExposure(List<Long>, Long): Double, exposureFactorStep(List<Long>): Double, formatExposure(Long): String.
Swift Testing struct + @Test func became a JUnit 4 class with org.junit.Test methods and kotlin.test assertions; assertEquals(expected, actual) keeps the Swift operand order.
#expect(a == b) became assertEquals(b, a) so the literal under test stays the expected value, including the empty-string cases in exposureIsFormattedAsFractionOfSecond.
Because exposures are integer microseconds, 1/60 s is 16666 us; the round-trip test still compares against exact list elements so it is unaffected.
The suite has no init/setup, so no @Before method was generated; test data helpers (cmTime, invalidExposure) live as private top-level declarations in this file.
UIGraphicsImageRenderer + CALayer.render(in:) are translated to android.graphics.Bitmap + Canvas + PNG compression with Bitmap.CompressFormat.PNG.
@MainActor is dropped: this is a plain JVM JUnit 4 test, no main-looper hopping is expressed here.
Swift associated-value case ChatLineItem.text(_:_:) becomes ChatLineItem.Text(...) from the sealed class in com.moblin.android.view.utils.
UIColor.white becomes android.graphics.Color.WHITE so ChatLineTextStyle keeps its Int color.
view.layer.render(in:) is mirrored by view.draw(canvas); running it in src/test requires a Robolectric-style android.graphics implementation (or an androidTest source set).
view.layoutIfNeeded() has no Android counterpart: setSize applies the frame with view.layout(0, 0, w, h), which keeps the 'restore the frame without remeasuring' scenario of the test.
view.bounds.size / CGSize is represented as android.util.Size built from View.width / View.height.
Assumes the ported ChatLineUiView is an android.view.View with a no-argument constructor and size(availableWidth: Float) returning android.util.Size.
Added the two new tests as @Test methods at the end of UtilsSuite, matching the Swift declaration order.
sortedBySearchPrefix lives in the same package com.moblin.android.various.utils, so no new import is needed.
The closure { $0 } becomes the trailing lambda { it }.
List literals keep their Swift element order, including the case-sensitive ordering asserted in the first test.
No locale/time-zone dependency, so no assumeTrue guard is added.
All pre-existing lines were kept byte-identical.

JUnit 4 (org.junit.Test) with kotlin.test assertions; the two @Test(arguments: [24, 25, 30, 50, 60]) cases become loops over the same values inside a single @Test method, with the fps included in failure messages.
CMTime maps to Long microseconds, so presentationTimeStamp(frameNumber, fps) returns frameNumber * 1_000_000 / fps (frameNumber/fps seconds).

CMTime.invalid for the decode timestamp is modelled by the file-local sentinel invalidTimeStamp = Long.MIN_VALUE; if MpegTsTimecodeGenerator uses another sentinel (e.g. -1L or a nullable Long?) this constant is the only place to change.

setReference(now:presentationTimeStamp:) kept the Swift units (seconds for 'now' and seconds for the reference timestamp, as required by referenceIsPresentationTimeStampBaseNotTheFirstFrame), so its second argument is written as a bare numeric literal that fits Double/Long/Int.
MpegTsTimecode.clock is java.time.Instant; the private Instant.timeIntervalSince1970 extension restores the Swift accessor (epochSecond + nano/1e9) used all over this suite.

timeOfDay uses the shared top-level 'calendar' from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg.hevc, assumed to be a UTC java.util.Calendar, reading HOUR_OF_DAY/MINUTE/SECOND (Swift .hour/.minute/.second, hence the 'InUtc' test).
MpegTsTimecode.frame is accessed through toLong() so the helpers compile whether the port declared it UInt (as in the Swift UInt32) or Int; frame is only used numerically.
Double.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy:) is Kotlin's % operator on Double.
Removed the wheelOfLuckWidgetId field from SettingsRemoteControlStreamer in constructor, property, encode and decode.
Everything else is byte-identical to the previous port.
Old persisted JSON containing wheelOfLuckWidgetId now silently drops it, matching the new Swift decoder.
BufferedVideoSuite becomes a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions; #expect(a == b) is translated to assertEquals(b, a).
createVideoSampleBuffer returns a com.moblin.android.media.MediaSample instead of a CVPixelBuffer-backed CMSampleBuffer: 1x1 BGRA (4 bytes of data), format = null, key frame = false.
CMTime(seconds: x) maps to presentationTimeUs = (x * 1_000_000).toLong() as the MediaSample carries microseconds.
The Swift precondition checks on CVPixelBufferCreate / CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateForImageBuffer are dropped because no pixel buffer is allocated in the port.
BufferedVideo constructor is called with the same labelled arguments; cameraId: .init() was translated to java.util.UUID.randomUUID(), assuming the port keeps a UUID camera id.
updateSampleBuffer(_:) is assumed to still take seconds as a Double, matching the Swift call site updateSampleBuffer(1.5).
processor: nil becomes processor = null.
The helpers stay private top-level functions in the same file as required for test data helpers.
RtmpChunkType is assumed to be a Kotlin enum class with entries ZERO/ONE/TWO/THREE, a UByte rawValue and a companion fromRawValue; RtmpMessageType is assumed to use fromRawValue(UByte) as well.

ByteReader is expected to expose position: Int (var), bytesAvailable: Int, readUInt8(): UByte, readUInt16Le(): UShort, readUInt24(): UInt, readUInt32(): UInt, readUInt32Le(): UInt and a throwing readBytes(count: Int): ByteArray.
messageHeaderSize() is kept as a function call on RtmpChunkType, mirroring the Swift declaration.

RtmpChunkStream in Swift is a struct copied in and out of the dictionary; in Kotlin it is a data class held by reference, so mutations apply to the stored instance. The observable behaviour is identical because every re-entry re-reads the same bytes from the same offset.
Swift's UInt32 timestamps map to Kotlin UInt, chunk stream ids to UShort, in line with the wire-format rule.
Swift's &+ / &+= wrapping arithmetic is preserved implicitly: Kotlin unsigned operators are implemented over signed Int arithmetic and wrap on overflow.
data.subdata(in:) becomes ByteArray.copyOfRange(offset, size); try! becomes a plain call to a throwing ByteReader method.
The private file-level types RtmpBasicHeader and RtmpChunkStream stay private to this file, as in the Swift source.
DjiStartStreamingMessagePayload lost payload1/payload2 and the oa5 flag; its fields now follow the Swift order rtmpUrl, resolution, fps, bitrateKbps.
encode() in both streaming payloads now builds a body ByteWriter and prefixes a length-prefixed header byte 0x00 / 0x01.
DjiStartStreamingMessagePayload2 dropped the header property, its two header constants and the header constructor parameter.
ByteWriter.writeUInt8 takes a UByte, so the literal header bytes are written as 0x00.toUByte() and 0x01.toUByte().
UInt16(truncatingIfNeeded: count) stays data.size.toUShort() as in the current Kotlin file.
The hand-written "/" -> "\/" JSON escaping used for the Codable payload was kept.
@Published properties become private MutableStateFlow backing fields plus public read-only StateFlow, as required by the porting rules.

kotlinx.serialization cannot serialize StateFlow fields, so SettingsMoblinkStreamer and SettingsMoblinkRelay use hand-written nested KSerializer objects that read/write the backing flows and always emit every key like Swift's encode(to:).
Swift's custom container.decode(_:_:_:isValid:) fallback is reproduced inside the custom deserializers: a missing key (or a url that fails isValidWebSocketUrl) yields the Swift default value.

CodingKeys server/client of SettingsMoblink do not match its property names, so @SerialName maps streamer->server and relay->client; the nested serializers use the Swift key names directly as descriptor element names.
The Swift UInt16 port is translated to Int because DefaultTcpPorts.moblinkStreamer and the rest of the ported code treat ports as Int; this file is not wire-format code.
SettingsMoblink itself stays a plain @Serializable class since it has no published properties; its nested types are resolved through their @Serializable(with = ...) serializers.
The explicit Swift init() initializers are implicit no-arg constructors in Kotlin; Swift's required init(from:) becomes the nested serialize/deserialize pair.
Swift Testing struct suite translated to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions.
JSONDecoder().decode(T.self, from:) becomes Json.decodeFromString<T>(string) with a Json instance configured with ignoreUnknownKeys = true to mirror Swift's default tolerance of extra keys.
Swift raw string #"..."# maps to a Kotlin triple-quoted raw string; the payloads contain no '$' so no escaping is needed.
`throws` test methods become plain @Test methods; decode failures propagate and fail the test as JUnit would.
SettingsMoblinkRelay lives in the same package com.moblin.android.various.settings, so no import is required.
CheermotesSuite is a plain JUnit 4 class; the Swift @MainActor annotation and the throws clauses have no Kotlin counterpart and were dropped.
The Cheermotes.getUrlAndBits(word:) signature is unresolved in this file; it is assumed to return Pair<java.net.URI, Int>? based on the Swift URL return value.
URL.absoluteString maps to URI.toString() and URL.lastPathComponent maps to uri.path.substringAfterLast("/") since java.net.URI has no lastPathComponent.
#require(...) maps to kotlin.test.assertNotNull, which returns the non-null value, so destructuring with val (url, bits) keeps working.
Nil comparisons from #expect(... == nil) map to kotlin.test.assertNull.
Twitch API model properties keep their Swift snake_case names (min_bits, static_) to match the ported model declarations.
makeCheermotes takes a Map<String, List<Int>>; linkedMapOf is used where a test builds more than one prefix so iteration order stays deterministic.
Assertion argument order follows kotlin.test.assertEquals(expected, actual), so the literal side of the Swift comparison is passed first.
String.Index cursor arithmetic is translated to Int UTF-16 offsets; identical for the ASCII format templates this file parses.

Foundation's Measurement unit types UnitSpeed, UnitTemperature and UnitLength do not exist on Android and are declared locally in this file with the same symbol strings, so symbol()/toSystem()/toString() behave exactly as on iOS.
@MainActor is dropped; TextFormatLoader is a plain class driven from the caller's scope.
String(localized:) is translated to localized() imported from com.moblin.android.
Failable enum initializers (init?(_:)) become companion functions fromString(value).
CaseIterable is exposed as companion property allCases backed by the enum entries.
Swift regex literals are translated to Kotlin Regex objects and prefix-matched with find(input, 0) plus a range.first == 0 check.
The Swift custom toString() on the unit enums is translated as override fun toString(): String.
Parameterized `@Test(arguments:)` cases became `@Test fun` bodies that loop over `intArrayOf` rows, because JUnit 4 cannot parameterize individual methods with different data sets in one class.
`Issue.record(...)` followed by `return` is translated to kotlin.test `fail(...)`, which throws and therefore stops the test.

Assumed the failable Swift initializers `HevcSeiPayloadTimeCode(reader:)`, `HevcNalUnit(data:offset:)` and `AvcNalUnit(data:offset:)` were ported as throwing constructors, so `try #require(...)` becomes a direct constructor call; if the port returns nullables instead, an explicit null check must be added here.

Assumed sealed payload case names keep the Swift spelling (`HevcNalUnitPayload.prefixSeiNut`, `HevcNalUnitSeiPayload.timeCode`, `AvcNalUnitPayload.sei`, `AvcNalUnitSeiPayload.pictureTiming`) with an associated-value property of the same name, and that enum entries keep the Swift spelling (`HevcNalUnitType.prefixSeiNut`, `AvcNalUnitType.sei`).
Wire-format integer mapping applied: `hours`/`minutes`/`seconds` are `UByte` and `frame` is `UInt`, so assertions convert the `Int` loop values with `toUByte()`/`toUInt()`.

`clock(...)` takes and returns `java.time.Instant`; the hevc `calendar` global is not used because the test must build the clock in UTC, matching the production `makeClock()` value asserted with `epochSecond % 86400`.
`Data` comparisons use `assertContentEquals` since Kotlin `ByteArray` equality is identity based, and `assertNotEquals`/`assertTrue` were not needed.
Byte literals above 0x7F keep their exact values and are written with `.toByte()` where Kotlin requires it.
The Swift file-private enum `CatPrinterCommandId` is renamed to `CatPrinterCommandsCommandId` so its .class file cannot collide with the private enum of the same name in CatPrinterCommandsMxw01.kt.
`logger.info(...)` became `Log.i("CatPrinterCommand", ...)`; the tag is this file's command type name, as on iOS.

`init?(data:)` became `operator fun invoke(data:)` returning `CatPrinterCommand?`; the do/catch that returned nil is `runCatching { unpack(data) }.getOrNull()` and the thrown Swift strings are IllegalStateException.
Image rows are UByteArray (`[[UInt8]]` -> `List<UByteArray>`), matching catPrinterEncodeImageRow and catPrinterPackPrintImageCommandsMxw01.
Data literals became byteArrayOf with `.toByte()` on values >= 0x80 so the bytes stay identical.
`reader.readUInt8() == 0x51` uses `0x51.toUByte()` because ByteReader returns UByte and bare hex literals are Int.
The case values SetEnergy/FeedPaper keep UShort and SetQuality keeps UByte, written through ByteWriter.writeUInt16Le/writeUInt8.
DrawRow and Lattice are data classes holding arrays, so their generated equals/hashCode compare references; no code in this file compares two commands by value.
Swift Testing's @Test(arguments:) has no JUnit 4 equivalent here, so bool(), decodeIntNotRepresentable() and the other parameterised cases run as one @Test that loops over the argument list.
Swift's `func null()` and `func object()` are hard keywords in Kotlin and had to be declared with backticks so the method names stay identical.
A private top-level `bytes(vararg Int)` helper was added so every Data([...]) byte literal stays byte-identical while producing a ByteArray; Data comparisons use kotlin.test.assertContentEquals.
Assumes Amf0Type is a sealed class with PascalCase subclasses (Number, Bool, String, Object, TypedObject, Null, Undefined, EcmaArray, StrictArray, Date) and that each payload is exposed as `value`.
Assumes AsValue is a sealed class with String/Number/Bool/EcmaArray subclasses and that AsObject is a Map<String, AsValue> (dictionary literals become mapOf).
Assumes AmfError is a sealed Throwable hierarchy with NotNumber and TooDeep objects, so assertFailsWith<AmfError.NotNumber> / <AmfError.TooDeep> is used for #expect(throws:).
RtmpCommandName is imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.rtmp.message and used through RtmpCommandName.fromRawValue(...) / RtmpCommandName.Result per the enum mapping convention.
Swift Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 15) becomes Instant.ofEpochSecond(15); ecmaArray.get(key:) becomes get(...) and swiftArray decoding yields a List<AsValue>.
Added shoutoutCreates list, delegate override twitchEventSubChannelShoutoutCreate and the shoutoutCreate test, matching the Swift diff.

The mock's url() returns a String ("ws://127.0.0.1:port") rather than a URL/URI, since the value is only built and handed to a client.
deinit { listener.cancel() } is dropped; Kotlin has no destructors, so the ServerSocket/coroutine scope is only released when the mock is garbage collected or the socket is closed via disconnect().

filterMetalPetal.inputBackgroundImage = .transparent -> MTIImage.transparent; both `?? image` fallbacks kept.

URL paths are plain String paths backed by java.io.File; FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory.appendingPathComponent is File(System.getProperty("java.io.tmpdir"), name) and attributesOfItem/.size is File.length() after File.exists().

The async tests run through runMainTest { } and loadTrackDuration/loadToneTime/loadVideoFullRange are suspend functions.

model.appendChatMessage is called with named arguments matching the Swift labels, and the chat platform case is assumed to be ChatPlatform.openStreamingPlatform from com.moblin.android.various.model.
private top-level Swift structs become file-private (private) top-level Kotlin declarations in the same file, preserving declaration order.

Swift multi-line string literals with trailing-backslash line continuations are rewritten as Kotlin string concatenation so the IRC wire text stays byte-identical.
try? X becomes runCatching { X }.getOrNull(); try #require(x) becomes a direct x.first() access with kotlin.test assertions.

This is SwiftProtobuf generated code: the message model is translated to plain Kotlin classes, and the runtime encode/decode plumbing (SwiftProtobuf.Decoder / SwiftProtobuf.Visitor) has no counterpart in this port's stack, so those two methods keep their names but take Any parameters and are TODO().
UnknownStorage is represented as ByteArray, and equality uses contentEquals/contentHashCode.
Protobuf field presence is preserved exactly: nullable private backing field, computed property falling back to the proto default, a hasX property and a clearX() function.
The Swift enum init() (which selects .resultUnknown) cannot be an enum constructor in Kotlin, so it becomes the companion function defaultValue().
The bytecode-encoded _protobuf_nameMap is translated into an explicit Map of enum/proto name to field number, keeping the same property name.
static func == is expressed as equals()/hashCode() overrides since Kotlin has no static operator.
Sendable conformance has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped.
SwiftProtobuf.ProtobufAPIVersionCheck is kept as private marker interfaces plus a private object, since Kotlin has no nested typealias.

The Swift diff only merged nested `if let` chains into single comma-separated conditions in decodeEvent and makeHighlight; the Kotlin translation already used the equivalent flat null checks, so no Kotlin line changes.
decodeEvent keeps its hand-written kotlinx.serialization implementation instead of Foundation JSONSerialization.
makeHighlight keeps the existing early-`if (message.type == "reply")` guard with local val extraction, which is semantically identical to the new Swift form.
Every other declaration, import and comment-free body is returned byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.
DispatchQueue is replaced by a CoroutineDispatcher constructor parameter plus an internal CoroutineScope; queue.async -> scope.launch and queue.asyncAfter -> scope.launch { delay(...) }.

AVFoundation types are mapped as follows: AVAudioFormat and CMFormatDescription -> android.media.MediaFormat, AVAudioCompressedBuffer -> ByteArray, CMTime -> Long microseconds, CMSampleBuffer -> MediaSample, so presentationTimeStamp.seconds becomes presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0.

Because AVAudioCompressedBuffer carries no AudioStreamBasicDescription, the audio codec is remembered in the new audioMime field set by audioEncoderOutputFormatInternal and checked with the literal "audio/opus".

The delegate overrides assume the port's AudioEncoderDelegate/VideoEncoderDelegate take (MediaFormat), (ByteArray, Long) and (VideoEncoder, MediaFormat)/(VideoEncoder, MediaSample, Long); adjust if the codec files chose other Android types.
RtmpConnection, RtmpChunk, RtmpChunkType, RtmpStreamInfo and RtmpStreamStats live in this same package, so they are used without imports; processorPipelineQueue is treated as a CoroutineScope.

info.bitrateStats.mutate { it.add(bytesTransferred = length) } is kept as-is, assuming RtmpStreamStats exposes the same mutate helper as the Swift version.

File returned byte-identical to the current Kotlin version.

The Swift diff only merges three sequential guards into one in processGimbalPresetQueue(); behaviour is unchanged, so the Kotlin guard chain stays as it is.
No Kotlin lines needed to change; the file is returned byte-identical.

Only the four guard blocks named in the diff changed; every other line is byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.

Generated SwiftProtobuf file: every Swift enum became an enum class with rawValue plus a companion fromRawValue; the message structs became mutable Kotlin classes.

No Swift API in this file is Apple-only; nothing was replaced by TODO().

Added the new VideoSources class between CameraShow and CameraState, with @Published properties as MutableStateFlow<List<Camera>> and all() reading them via .value.

Swift's import Network is unnecessary on Android and is dropped; no Network.framework API from this file survives the port.
CryptoKit Insecure.MD5 is replaced by java.security.MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5") over the UTF-8 bytes.

The three Swift overloads become three Kotlin top-level functions with the same names and order; the String/ByteArray overloads stay unambiguous.
The java.util.Base64 MIME encoder pads with '=' and wraps at 64 characters, matching the Swift line-length option; callers that need an unwrapped token should strip the line breaks.
No Moblin-internal extension (utf8Data) is imported or redeclared, so this file has no dependency on other Moblin files.
MD5 is cryptographically broken but is kept unchanged because the HaishinKit protocol path depends on those exact digests.
No permission handling is needed for digest calculation.

CBytePerfMon is a libsrt C struct with no Kotlin binding in this port, so a mirror data class named CBytePerfMon is declared in this file with the same field names and C types (int32_t -> Int, double -> Double); SrtNative is expected to populate it.
The Swift memberwise init is the Kotlin primary constructor; the init(mon:) becomes a secondary constructor so both call shapes stay identical.
static let zero maps to val zero in the companion object.
Int32 in Swift maps to Int in Kotlin; Double stays Double.
The Swift mon.pktRecvNAKTotal is exposed as pktRecvNakTotal to match the existing Swift property spelling.
No native (JNI) symbols are called in this file, so no System.loadLibrary call is needed here.
Kotlin data class equality, hashCode and toString are generated, which the Swift struct got for free.
Moblin keeps these counters as plain values, so no state flow or observable wrapper is required.

NEHotspotNetwork.fetchCurrent comes from the NetworkExtension shim (platform/networkextension/NEHotspotNetwork.kt): WifiInfo from the ConnectivityManager transport info on Android 12 and later, WifiManager before that, and null without WiFi or location permission, like iOS.

DispatchQueue.main.async becomes mainScope.launch on a private file-level CoroutineScope on Dispatchers.Main.
The macCatalyst CoreWLAN dynamic-lookup helper is preserved as a private function of the same name returning null.
No types are declared by this file, only top-level functions, so declared_types is empty.
BluetoothScanner is an ObservableObject but not a settings class, so @Published discoveredPeripherals became MutableStateFlow<List<CBPeripheral>>; views collect it with collectAsState().
The Swift class is non-final, so it is declared open class with open val discoveredPeripherals and open funs.

The Swift extension that conforms to CBCentralManagerDelegate is folded into the class header, and the delegate methods use override because the shim interface provides default bodies.
CBCentralManager(delegate: self, queue: .main) maps to CBCentralManager(delegate = this, queue = null): the main queue is the default.
discoveredPeripherals.append(peripheral) becomes a value assignment on the flow (value = value + peripheral), and the duplicate check reads .value.
The delegate methods are declared with all four parameter names even though the Swift code ignores advertisementData and rssi.
CMMotionManager, CMAccelerometerData and OperationQueue.main come from the CoreMotion shim (platform/coremotion/CoreMotion.kt), so the constructor keeps the Swift parameter motionManager.

data.acceleration is a CMAcceleration in g on iOS axes with gravity included, so the magnitude is about 1 at rest, as on iOS.
guard let data, error == nil else { return } becomes an early return@startAccelerometerUpdates.
GForce is a @Serializable data class; its property names match the Swift coding keys exactly, so no @SerialName is needed.

NSObject is dropped; ObservableObject with @Published array becomes MutableStateFlow<List<GoProDiscoveredDevice>> per the scanner rule, so readers use discoveredDevices.collectAsState().
centralManager is a stored optional CBCentralManager backed by CBCentralManager.holder(); assigning null releases it like ARC (scan stops, no more delegate calls).
The Swift extension conformance is merged into the class header, so both delegate methods are override fun of CBCentralManagerDelegate.
CBCentralManager(delegate:self, queue:.main) uses queue = null because .main, DispatchQueue.main and nil all map to the main queue in the shim.

goProControlServiceId is not declared in this file: it is expected as a top-level CBUUID val in package com.moblin.android.integrations.gopro (GoProDevice.kt); no import is needed since it is the same package.

discoveredDevices.append(.init(...)) becomes a value reassignment with a new list plus a GoProDiscoveredDevice, and the duplicate check uses any { it.peripheral.identifier == peripheral.identifier }.
The whole class stays main-actor-less: the shim delivers every central delegate call on the queue given to the manager (here the main queue), in order.
NWPathMonitor is replaced with ConnectivityManager.registerDefaultNetworkCallback, so a Context parameter was added to the constructor because Android needs it.
NWInterface.InterfaceType has no Android counterpart and is replaced by a local InterfaceType enum keeping the same case names (cellular, wifi, wiredEthernet, other).
