@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin equivalent and was dropped.
Collections.Deque is replaced with kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque.
pathUpdateHandler is mapped to onCapabilitiesChanged; since only the default network is observed, .other is used when the network exposes none of the wifi/cellular/ethernet transports.
The `if self.cellular` guard is expressed as `this@NetworkInterfaceTypeSelector.cellular` inside the anonymous NetworkCallback.
The registration is never unregistered because the Swift file exposes no cancel path; the owner must call unregisterNetworkCallback if needed.
Only the delegate body changed: the three early-return guards are now one combined condition.
The wholeMatch regex check keeps Regex("S[0-9a-f]{16}C").matches(localName) as before.
Everything else (class, state flow, central manager holder, companion) is unchanged.

CoreBluetooth ids stay CBUUID, as required for BLE device protocol files: workoutDeviceHeartRateServiceId and workoutDeviceHeartRateMeasurementCharacteristicId are top-level vals built with CBUUID(string = ...).
HeartRateMeasurement keeps its Swift shape as a file-private class with a secondary constructor taking the value bytes, since a data class cannot hold the parsing init.
Swift throws/try disappear: ByteReader's readUInt8/readUInt16Le are non-throwing in Kotlin, so handleMeasurement is a plain function and the init needs no try.
UShort is used for the 16-bit heart-rate field because this is BLE wire parsing; Int(measurement.heartRate) becomes measurement.heartRate.toInt().
UInt16(reader.readUInt8()) is a widening conversion, written readUInt8().toUShort().
flags.isBitSet(index:) comes from com.moblin.android.common.various and takes the UByte flags of the measurement byte.
Data parameters become ByteArray and the class is open because the Swift class is non-final, so its members are open too.
The private top-level format-index constant stays private in this file.

Swift's throwing `init(value:)` on the file-private struct becomes the companion factory `CyclingSpeedCadenceMeasurement.parse(value)`; ByteReader throws naturally, so Kotlin needs no `throws` clause.
The 32-bit wheel-revolution delta is widened to Long so the `+ 4294967296` wraparound cannot overflow Kotlin's Int.
`flags.isBitSet(index:)` comes from com.moblin.android.common.various and is imported explicitly.
`ContinuousClock.now` and `ContinuousClock.Instant` come from com.moblin.android.platform.core; the 3-second guard uses `3.seconds` from kotlin.time.
UInt/UShort values are value-preserving converted with `toLong()`/`toInt()` and never reinterpreted as bytes.
`measurementCharacteristic` is stored but only tested by `isAnyCharacteristicDiscovered()`, exactly as in Swift.
The class stays `open` with `open` members because the Swift class is not final; all stored state stays `private`.
Average calculator and crank cadence come from the same Kotlin package, so no imports are needed for them.
ByteReader's Kotlin methods do not throw, so the Swift `throws` on RscMeasurement's init and on handleMeasurement is dropped; callers that wrap the call in try still compile.
The throwing Swift init of RscMeasurement became `RscMeasurement.create(value)` on a private data class, because a Kotlin constructor cannot parse with several statements.
`flags.isBitSet(index:)` is the extension from com.moblin.android.common.various, imported and called with the named argument as on the shim contract.
`lastRscUpdateTime.duration(to: now).seconds` becomes `duration(to = now).toDouble(DurationUnit.SECONDS)` from com.moblin.android.platform.core.ContinuousClock.
WorkoutDeviceRunningMetrics is a synthesized-Codable struct, so it is an @Serializable data class with the Swift property names and null defaults so absent JSON keys decode like Swift.
WorkoutDeviceRunning is a non-final Swift class, so it becomes an open class with open members and private backing properties.
The two CoreBluetooth UUID constants are top-level vals built with CBUUID(string = "..."), matching the shim constructor.
The two flag indices stay file-private constants with their Swift names.
A Context is now a constructor parameter because ConnectivityManager cannot be obtained without one; pass the application context.
NWPathMonitor is replaced by ConnectivityManager.registerDefaultNetworkCallback with a main-Looper Handler, so callbacks arrive on the main thread like the Swift @MainActor code.
NWInterface.InterfaceType became the local InterfaceType enum, mapped from NetworkCapabilities transports (wifi/cellular/ethernet, otherwise other).
The ifaddrs walk is replaced by ConnectivityManager.allNetworks for the interface list and java.net.NetworkInterface.getByName(name).inetAddresses for the addresses.
IPv6 scope suffixes such as %wlan0 are stripped from hostAddress before the address is reported.
start() needs ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE on the manifest; the permission request stays in the Activity layer.
Swift's init only installed monitor.pathUpdateHandler; that handler is now the NetworkCallback overrides, so init just builds the callback object.
Swift URL is stored only, so pushUrl/stopUrl are plain String fields built from baseUrl and pushKey.
The failable init? becomes a regular primary constructor because there is no URL parsing failure path once URL is a String; call sites get a non-null RealtimeIrl.
CLLocation maps to android.location.Location: coordinate.latitude/longitude -> latitude/longitude, speed -> speed, altitude -> altitude, timestamp.timeIntervalSince1970 -> location.time / 1000.0.
The POST body is built as a plain JSON string like the Swift version; content type application/json is set via OkHttp MediaType.
httpRequest is expected to take an okhttp3.Request; the JSON body is sent with toRequestBody().
stop() sends an empty POST body because OkHttp rejects a POST with a null body.
Location permission requests are left to the Activity layer.
Network.framework NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket; reads happen on a Dispatchers.IO coroutine and writes are fire-and-forget coroutines, matching .idempotent send semantics.
ContinuousClock.Instant is represented as monotonic Long nanoseconds from System.nanoTime(); isActive compares the delta against removeTimeoutNanos.
The Swift connection.batch / receiveMessage batch-of-100 pattern becomes a single blocking InputStream.read loop; connectionReceiveBatchSize is kept but unused.
A private ByteArray.setUInt32Be extension is added locally because the common package only guarantees createSrtlaPacket, srtControlTypeSize and the packet parsers.
logger.info/debug map to Log.i/Log.d with tag SrtlaServerClientConnection.
SrtlaServerClientConnectionDelegate protocol becomes a Kotlin interface; AckPacket struct becomes a mutable class.
isSrtDataPacket, getSrtControlPacketType and getSrtSequenceNumber from the common package are used as ByteArray member extensions.
connection.cancel() maps to Socket.close(); stop() also cancels the receive coroutine.
Swift's `nonisolated(unsafe) let ... = CBUUID(string:)` globals become top-level vals calling the CBUUID shim with `string =`.

The private PowerMeasurement/PowerVector structs keep their throwing `init(value:)` as a Kotlin class whose `init` block parses through ByteReader; call sites stay `PowerMeasurement(value)` / `PowerVector(value)`.
`try` disappears: ByteReader's reads throw on their own, so the parsing code is a plain sequence of calls.
UInt8 flags use ByteReader.readUInt8() -> UByte; the direction mask is a private UByte val because a UByte literal cannot be a `const val`, and the shift goes through toInt() since UByte has no shr.
The private raw-value enum gets a `rawValue` property and a companion `fromRawValue` returning null for unknown values, matching the Swift failable `init?(rawValue:)`.
`isBitSet(index:)` comes from com.moblin.android.common.various; WorkoutDeviceAverageCalculator/WorkoutDeviceCrankCadence are in this same package so they need no import.
Crank data is read with readUInt16Le (little-endian) exactly as in Swift, and the tuple result of handleMeasurement becomes Pair<Int, Int?>.
`now: .now` becomes ContinuousClock.now from com.moblin.android.platform.core.
CoreLocation maps to android.location: CLLocation -> Location, CLPlacemark -> Address, CLGeocoder -> android.location.Geocoder.
The class gains a Context constructor parameter because Geocoder needs one; every other member keeps its Swift name and signature.
@MainActor becomes a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main), and Task<Void, any Error> becomes kotlinx.coroutines.Job; the geocoding call is moved to Dispatchers.IO via withContext.
Task.isCancelled becomes isActive of the launch scope, so the polling loop still exits after cancellation.
sleep(seconds:) is assumed to be the suspend function sleep(seconds: Int) from com.moblin.android.common.various; the delay variable stays an Int number of seconds.
The do/catch around the sleep and geocode becomes runCatching { ... } so a failed lookup keeps the loop alive, exactly like the Swift catch.
Geocoder.getFromLocation is blocking, so it must not run on the main dispatcher.
Location.distanceTo returns Float while Swift returned CLLocationDistance (Double); the 1001/1000 literal fallback and threshold stay the same numbers.
The Swift `extension Model: CBCentralManagerDelegate` becomes a top-level extension function `fun Model.centralManagerDidUpdateState` in this package, since Model itself is declared in Model.kt.
`Model.bluetoothAllowed` is a `MutableStateFlow<Boolean>`, so the assignment writes `bluetoothAllowed.value = ...`.
`CBCentralManager.authorization == .allowedAlways` maps to `CBManagerAuthorization.allowedAlways` from the CoreBluetooth shim.
The `@MainActor` attribute is dropped; when a CBCentralManager is created it is given `delegate = { model.centralManagerDidUpdateState(it) }` and its queue, and that queue defines the thread.
`let bluetoothNotAllowedMessage` is a global String constant and becomes a top-level `const val`.
The unused `_: CBCentralManager` parameter is named `central` in Kotlin.
CLLocation maps to android.location.Location, the same type the WeatherService shim accepts.
The Swift Task<Void, any Error>? loop becomes a Job launched from a main-dispatched CoroutineScope; Task.isCancelled is checked with the coroutine scope's isActive.
try await sleep(seconds: delay) is sleepSeconds(seconds = delay) from com.moblin.android.common.various.
weatherService.weather(for: location) is called with the backticked keyword parameter `for` exactly as the shim declares.
logger.debug is android.util.Log.d with "WeatherManager" as the tag.
The non-final Swift class keeps open members so subclasses can override, matching Swift.
The private stored properties stay private, so they are never marked open.

The Swift diff only merges two guard clauses; the merged `guard let nameData = metadata["name"], let name = String(...)` becomes a single `metadata["name"]?.let { ... } ?: continue` line in `discoveredStreamersUpdated`.
The second merged guard is inside `getAddressInfo`, which is hand-written for Android with java.net.InetAddress instead of getnameinfo, so that function stays byte-identical.
Kotlin's `String(ByteArray, Charset)` never fails, so the UTF-8 decode failure branch of the Swift guard has no Kotlin counterpart.
NsdManager discovery, resolve and address handling are unchanged; only the TXT record name lookup line was touched.
The Swift diff only merges two guard statements in getQueryItems; behaviour is identical, so no Kotlin change is needed.
Kotlin getQueryItems keeps its hand-written query parsing over URI.rawQuery with Uri.decode, matching URLComponents.queryItems semantics.
SrtSocketOption stays an enum class with a String rawValue and a companion fromRawValue, as before.
The socket-option constants still come from SrtNative; nothing in this diff touches them.

The three separate Swift guards are merged into one Kotlin condition using smart-cast-free null handling: the manufacturer data is read without a trailing `?: return`, then a single `if` checks null, isDjiDevice and duplicate detection.
`discoveredDevices` stays a `MutableStateFlow<List<DjiDiscoveredDevice>>` and is appended with `discoveredDevices.value = discoveredDevices.value + ...`, unchanged from before.
`@MainActor` and `NSObject` have no Kotlin counterpart; the delegate queue is the main queue (`queue = null` on the shim).
The `centralManager` property still uses `CBCentralManager.holder()` so assigning null releases the manager like ARC does.
Only handleLocationUpdate changed: the two guards are merged into one if with a disjunction.
Everything else in the file stays byte-identical, including the Android-specific Location calls.

Kotlin cannot add protocol conformance from an extension, so Model's HttpProxyServerDelegate conformance is kept as the extension function httpProxyServerPortReady plus an anonymous adapter object assigned to HttpProxyServer.delegate.
NWEndpoint.hostPort is represented as java.net.InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", port) and NWEndpoint.Port as Int, so getHttpProxyServerEndpoint returns InetSocketAddress?.
Model must already declare httpProxyServer: HttpProxyServer?, httpProxyPort: Int? and database whose httpProxy exposes enabled, localNetwork and port.
setWebBrowserProxy() and setBrowserEffectsProxyServer() are resolved as Model members or extension functions in com.moblin.android.various.model.
DispatchQueue.main.async is replaced by a file-private mainScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) plus launch.
All functions are top-level extension functions on Model in this package, matching the Swift extension.
The Swift diff merges two guards in sendRtcp; the existing Kotlin already performs both checks (rtcpChannel null check and 0xFFFF length check) in sequence, so the file stays byte-identical.
No behavioural change is required: the port keeps java.net Socket/DatagramSocket based transport from earlier hand-written Android work rather than NWConnection.
All log calls keep using the Android TAG/Log shim.
Delegate callbacks are dispatched on rtspClientQueue via deliver().

The file-private serial DispatchQueue becomes a single-thread CoroutineScope(Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor().asCoroutineDispatcher()); start/stop/setWheelCircumference keep hopping onto it with launch.
centralManager is stored through CBCentralManager.holder() so assigning null releases the previous manager and its connections exactly like ARC.
delegate stays a plain nullable var (Swift weak); no WeakReference is used.
The @MainActor global workoutDeviceScanner becomes a top-level val constructed from the four service ids.
WorkoutDevice implements CBCentralManagerDelegate (fun interface) and CBPeripheralDelegate in the class header; only the delegate methods the Swift file uses are overridden.
In peripheralDidDiscoverCharacteristicsFor the CBPeripheral parameter is named peripheralArg because the body uses the stored peripheral property.
Swift's try around the delegate calls is dropped (the Kotlin delegate methods and handleMeasurement do not throw); the do/catch around characteristic handling stays as try/catch.
logger.debug/info become Log.d/Log.i with tag "WorkoutDevice"; CBUUID interpolation uses uuidString.
Network.framework NWConnection/NWListener are replaced with java.net.Socket/ServerSocket on Dispatchers.IO; the callback-driven receive loops became blocking read loops inside coroutines.
NWEndpoint is replaced by a host String plus a port Int, so HttpConnectRequestParser.Result carries destinationHost/destinationPort instead of an NWEndpoint.

The file-level serial DispatchQueue is a CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO); Swift's serial execution guarantee is lost, so the shared `connections` list and `stopping` flag would need extra synchronization in production.
logger.info calls become android.util.Log.i with tag "HttpProxyServer".
HttpParser.getLine is assumed to return Pair<String, Int>? and HttpParser.data a ByteArray; both live in this same package so nothing is imported.
NWInterface/NWInterface.InterfaceType map to android.net.Network: NetworkInterfaceTypeSelector.getType() returns Network? and markBad takes it.
NWListener state updates are collapsed into handleStateUpdate(error: Exception?), where null means the ready state and a non-null value the failed state.
The body byte range is stored before connectToDestination runs (Swift sets it after the async connect) so the tunneling socket can flush it.
Only HttpParser.getLine changed: the two Swift guards are now one guard, so the Kotlin line lookup and the strict UTF-8 decode are folded into a single elvis return.
Everything else (InterfaceTypeHttpClient, httpCall, httpCallUrlSession, parseIntStrict, decodeUtf8Strict) is untouched and byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.
InterfaceTypeHttpClient still binds NWConnection to NWParameters.requiredInterfaceType and falls through cellular, wifi, wiredEthernet, keeping the chosen transport first for later calls.
The OkHttp fallback in httpCallUrlSession attaches the body with toRequestBody() before calling httpRequest(), matching Swift's uploadTask(from:).
MainActor.assumeIsolated is dropped: NWConnection handlers already run on the Dispatchers.Main coroutine dispatcher passed to start(queue =).
Global `logger` becomes android.util.Log with tag "ObsWebSocket"; `logger.debugEnabled` maps to Log.isLoggable(TAG, Log.DEBUG).

The untyped JSON envelope (op/d/eventType/...) is parsed with org.json (the Android counterpart of JSONSerialization); typed payloads use kotlinx.serialization with ignoreUnknownKeys = true so unknown keys are skipped like Swift's JSONDecoder.
Swift's `throw "some string"` became IllegalStateException("..."), and `try?` became runCatching { ... }.getOrNull(); `try { } catch {}` became runCatching { }.onSuccess { }.
`weak let delegate` has no Kotlin equivalent: delegate is a strongly referenced constructor property, so the caller must drop the ObsWebSocket instance to break the cycle.

@MainActor is emulated with a private mainScope (CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main)) used only inside the WebSocketClientDelegate callbacks; all public methods must be called from the main dispatcher as before.
The UInt64 event-subscription bitmask is kept as ULong (wire format) and serialized by kotlinx.serialization's built-in unsigned serializer.

Assumed WebSocketClient API (from com.moblin.android.various.network): constructor WebSocketClient(url: String, loopback: Boolean), var delegate: WebSocketClientDelegate?, start(), stop(), send(string) -- verify against the Kotlin port of WebSocketClient.kt.

`URL` is stored as String and `url.isLoopback()` (not present in the glossary) is replaced by a private isLoopback(String) helper using java.net.URI; request bodies are pre-encoded with Json.encodeToString at the call site because Kotlin cannot encode an `any Encodable`.
The private Voice sealed class is gone; utterance dispatch now switches on TextToSpeechVoice (Apple/TtsMonster/ElevenLabs) returned by TextToSpeechVoice.find(voices, language).
Added the elevenLabs field, setElevenLabsApiKey and utterElevenLabs, mirroring setTtsMonsterApiToken.
playGeneratedAudio is shared by the TTS Monster and ElevenLabs paths and posts the player setup onto the serial textToSpeech queue via scope.launch, as Swift hops to textToSpeechDispatchQueue.

Natural language detection is still stubbed (dominantLanguage returns null, languageProbability 0.0), so the 0.7 probability filter never fires and the detected language always falls back to defaultLanguage/Locale.
The unused SettingsVoiceType import was removed together with the old voice-selection code.
Assumes TextToSpeechVoice exposes Apple(voice), TtsMonster(voiceId), ElevenLabs(voiceId) and a companion find(voices, language).

WiFiAware (Wi-Fi Aware listener/connection) and Network.framework's declarative NetworkListener/NetworkConnection have no counterpart in this port, so listen() keeps its signature and its body is TODO("no Android counterpart for WiFiAware").
actor WiFiAwareReceiver -> plain class with suspend members; the Swift 'static let shared' singleton becomes 'val shared' in the companion object.
private struct Sender -> file-private data class Sender; Swift Task<Void, Never> -> kotlinx.coroutines.Job, cancelled with task.cancel().
NetworkConnection<UDP> has no Kotlin type equivalent here, so 'connection' is typed Any; the Android realization of the UDP data path would be a java.net.DatagramSocket driven on Dispatchers.IO.
The 'connections' array is exposed as a file-private MutableList<Sender> of the class; actor isolation must be provided by a Mutex if the list is later mutated concurrently.
Swift 'async throws' becomes a suspend function; errors surface as thrown exceptions rather than a checked error type.
The '#if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst)' compile guard and '@available(iOS 26, *)' annotations are dropped since they have no Kotlin meaning.
logger.info(...) lines disappear with the stubbed body; when the body is implemented use android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag.
apple_only: WiFiAware framework (Wi-Fi Aware listening, publishable/subscribable service pairing)
Network.framework declarative NetworkListener / NetworkConnection API

notes: NWListener/NWConnection (UDP) are replaced by one loopback DatagramSocket. The 'connection' is the remote InetSocketAddress of the first peer that sends a packet, and packets are sent back over that same socket so the local source port stays stable for the SRT peer.
onReady passes the port as Int because Android exposes ports as Int; UInt16 is only used for wire formats in this port.

srtlaClientQueue is assumed to be a CoroutineDispatcher/CoroutineContext, so the class builds CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + srtlaClientQueue). If it is declared as a CoroutineScope instead, replace this with srtlaClientQueue.launch { }.
NWListener.State is replaced by a private nested enum ListenerState(setup, ready, failed); setup is a no-op and every other failure maps to the same 'bad network state' error message as in Swift.
The receive loop drains incoming datagrams so the peer endpoint can be detected; the payload is discarded because the Swift file exposes no receive handler on its connection.
stop() closes the socket, which also unblocks the blocking DatagramSocket.receive; the scope itself is not cancelled so the listener can be started again.
DatagramSocket.send is blocking and therefore dispatched onto srtlaClientQueue from the non-suspend sendPacket().
All logging uses android.util.Log.i with tag LocalListener and the same message text as the Swift logger calls.
CoreBluetooth ids stay top-level CBUUID vals built with CBUUID(string = ...), and the UInt8 protocol ids stay top-level UByte vals.
Data becomes ByteArray: Data([a, b]) -> byteArrayOf(a.toByte(), b.toByte()), concatenation uses ByteArray.plus, and Data() -> ByteArray(0).
Byte parsing uses (x.toInt() and mask) then .toByte(), so the UInt8 masks and header shifts keep Swift's unsigned semantics.
Protobuf requests use the ported types with the same property names (result, phoneName, scanID, maxEntries, bypassEulaCheck, ...); Int32 maps to Int and UInt32 to UInt.
The file-private SwiftProtobuf.Message.encoded() extension becomes a file-private fun Message.encoded() using runCatching { serializedData() }.getOrNull() ?: ByteArray(0).
The two toProtobuf() extensions are kept, one file-private for SettingsGoProLaunchLiveStreamResolution and one public for SettingsGoProLens returning a nullable OpenGopro_EnumLens.
GoProBleMessageAccumulator keeps its switch as a when expression so headerLength is definitely assigned, and reset() reassigns payload to ByteArray(0).
The ScanEntry helpers test the flags with Int bitwise and against OpenGopro_EnumScanEntryFlags rawValue.
MoblinkStreamer gains a Context constructor parameter (first position) because the Bonjour advertisement now uses android.net.nsd.NsdManager; port/password/name keep the Swift names and order.
NWListener/NWConnection are replaced by java.net.ServerSocket plus a file-private WebSocketConnection that performs the RFC 6455 HTTP upgrade and frame coding on Dispatchers.IO.
NWConnection.start(queue:) has no equivalent and its call site was dropped: the Kotlin connection is usable as soon as the handshake helper returns it.
NWEndpoint is represented as host String + port Int, so MoblinkStreamerDelegate takes host/port instead of an endpoint object and Relay stores tunnelEndpointHost/tunnelEndpointPort.
moblinkBonjourDomain has no NsdManager counterpart, so only name/type/TXT attributes are registered.
@MainActor is modelled with CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main): all relay bookkeeping and delegate callbacks are dispatched there, so the mutable relay list needs no locks.
MainTimer, SimpleStringStorage(key:) and randomString() call sites assume the Kotlin ports kept the Swift labels; MainTimer intervals are passed as Double seconds per the TimeInterval mapping.

MoblinkRequest/MoblinkResponse/MoblinkMessageToRelay/MoblinkMessageToStreamer are matched with `is` checks and property names taken from the Swift case labels (id, result, data, apiVersion, authentication).
NWConnection is replaced by java.net.Socket; connect, read and write run as coroutines on Dispatchers.IO and all blocking calls stay off the caller thread.
NWProtocolTLS.Options is mapped to javax.net.ssl.SSLContext? (null keeps plain TCP); an RTMPS caller passes an SSLContext whose socket factory creates the SSLSocket.

The DispatchQueue constructor argument became a CoroutineDispatcher named queue, still used for the delayed close and the too-much-buffered disconnect; short latency trickles stay on the caller side otherwise.
NWConnection.viabilityUpdateHandler has no Android counterpart, so viabilityDidChange is kept intact but must be driven by the caller (e.g. a ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback).
NWConnection.State has no Android counterpart; it is modelled by the private sealed class RtmpSocketConnectionState (Ready/Failed/Cancelled) declared in this file and fed from connect().
weak var delegate cannot be expressed in Kotlin; delegate is a plain nullable property and the owner must clear it when the socket is released.
RtmpChunk.split, RtmpMessage.length, RtmpHandshake.sigSize, RtmpHandshake.createC0C1Packet/createC2Packet and RtmpConnectionCode.eventData() are assumed from the sibling files of the same package.
logger.info is replaced by android.util.Log.i with the tag "RtmpSocket".
The Swift diff only merges an availability check into an optional binding in BackgroundActivity.stop(); the Kotlin port already used a null-safe call, so no Kotlin change was required.

The view takes no model objects, so only the kind string is a parameter.
An extra Modifier parameter with a default value was added, as is conventional for Compose composables.
The copy is kept inline rather than moved to strings.xml so the Swift and Kotlin sources stay readable side by side; it can be extracted later with stringResource.
Only the tick() tail changed: the nested emptiness check is now folded into the 5 second condition, as in the Swift source.
Everything else, including the Android-specific SystemClock nanoseconds timestamps, mainScope and Log calls, is left byte-identical.
The @Binding selectedRotation becomes a plain Double parameter plus an onSelectedRotationChange lambda, per the ui tier convention.
Picker is rendered as a Material 3 ExposedDropdownMenuBox with a read-only OutlinedTextField anchor.
The ForEach over the literal rotation list is a Kotlin loop over listOf(0.0, 90.0, 180.0, 270.0); the degree labels use Int conversion to match "\(Int(rotation))°".
No navigation callback is needed because the Swift view has no NavigationLink.

The Swift diff only merges two guard statements into one; the Kotlin kernel initializer already short-circuits with `?: return@lazy null` on both lookups, so the generated code is functionally identical and unchanged.
No Kotlin lines needed to change: Bundle.url is still read through java.io.File and wrapped in runCatching, matching the merged Swift guard.
The Swift diff only merges two sequential guards into one; the Kotlin file already returns early for both conditions in the same order, so its statements stay byte-identical.
No behavioural change: takeSnapshotComplete is still read before the makeCopy call, so a copy is only made when a snapshot callback is pending.
All existing Android-specific lease handling (retainLease/retainLeases/releaseLeases), Dispatchers.Main.immediate callbacks and Bitmap helpers are preserved untouched.
VideoToolbox has no Android counterpart, so the extension receiver is android.media.MediaCodec (per the media tier mapping); the Swift receiver name VTCompressionSession is therefore not preserved.
OSStatus -> Int, CMTime -> Long microseconds, CVPixelBuffer -> android.media.Image, CMSampleBuffer -> MediaSample (com.moblin.android.media).
VTCompressionOutputHandler -> (status: Int, flags: Int, sampleBuffer: MediaSample?) -> Unit.

All four bodies are TODO(): MediaCodec is configured/started/stopped/released rather than prepared/invalidated, the async output callback must be registered at configure time, and there is no VTSessionSetProperties equivalent.
setProperties keeps the pure dictionary-building logic unchanged; it assumes VTSessionPropertyKey.value is a String (port of CFString) so it can key a MutableMap<String, Any?>.
@inline(__always) has no Kotlin counterpart and was dropped.
The Swift `duration _: CMTime` parameter is kept as an unused `duration: Long` to match the signature; only `.invalid` was ever passed.
No top-level Kotlin type is declared in this file; only extension functions.
Swift struct -> Kotlin class: it has mutable stored bytes plus parsing constructors, so a data class is not applicable.
Kotlin has no failable initialiser, so init?(formatDescription:) became the companion factory fromFormatDescription(formatDescription:) returning null when no avcC is available.
getAvcC() depends on CMFormatDescription atoms, which have no Android counterpart, so its body is TODO(); fromFormatDescription() therefore throws until an Android avcC source is supplied.

makeFormatDescription() cannot take an out-pointer, it returns MediaFormat? and uses csd-0/csd-1 ByteBuffers (MediaCodec parameter-set representation), null replacing kCMFormatDescriptionBridgeError_InvalidParameter.
reserveNumOfSequenceParameterSets stays a UByte and the mask arithmetic is kept identical to Swift (UByte.inv() + and).
Parsing is wrapped in runCatching/onFailure instead of do/catch, logging via Log.i with the class name as tag, matching the Swift catch branch.
ByteReader is imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.util and assumed to expose readBytes(count)/readUInt8()/readUInt16() that throw on underflow.
MediaFormat.MIMETYPE_VIDEO_AVC is set because CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateFromH264ParameterSets is H.264-specific and an Android MediaFormat needs a mime type.
stroke is implemented as a Modifier extension using drawWithContent to replicate SwiftUI's shadow-based stroke.
The four shadow layers are drawn with BlurMaskFilter and PorterDuffColorFilter, offset by the stroke width.
Values are scaled by density to convert dp to pixels, matching SwiftUI's point-based coordinates.
compositingGroup() is emulated by the saveLayer compositing in drawWithContent.
The @ViewBuilder conditional is translated to an if expression returning the original modifier when width <= 0.
ElementaryStreamType and ElementaryStreamDescriptiorTag became enum classes with a UByte rawValue plus a companion fromRawValue, mirroring the Swift raw-value initializer (nullable result).
ElementaryStreamDescriptiorRegistration is an object; the String.utf8Data extension has no Kotlin counterpart so opus uses "Opus".toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8).
ElementaryStreamSpecificData is a data class; Swift's init(reader:) became a secondary constructor because ByteReader parses the wire format synchronously.
esDescriptors stays a private property declared in the class body (not a constructor parameter), matching Swift's private stored property being excluded from the memberwise initializer.
Kotlin ByteArray has no append, so += (ByteArray.plus) is used; each appendDescriptor call allocates a new array, which matches Swift Data semantics but is O(n).

ByteReader/ByteWriter are assumed to expose readUInt8(): UByte, readUInt16(): UShort, readBytes(Int): ByteArray, skipBytes(Int), writeUInt8(UByte), writeUInt16(UShort), writeBytes(ByteArray) and a data: ByteArray property, per the wire-format unsigned convention.
getDescriptor's do { while true } catch {} was translated to try/catch(Exception) returning null, so any reader failure yields null exactly like the Swift version.
The Swift name typo 'Descriptior' is preserved so both codebases stay readable side by side.
KickWebView's nested Coordinator becomes a top-level class KickWebViewCoordinator because Kotlin cannot nest a class inside the KickWebView composable function.

WKWebView is translated to androidx AndroidView with android.webkit.WebView; the per-cookie httpCookieStore API has no Android equivalent, so periodicallyCheckForAccessTokenCookie polls CookieManager.getCookie(loginUrl) and parses the session_token pair.

WKWebViewConfiguration.websiteDataStore = .nonPersistent() is approximated with CookieManager.getInstance().removeAllCookies(null) when the WebView is created; Android has no per-WebView ephemeral store.
allowsInlineMediaPlayback has no WebSettings counterpart; only mediaPlaybackRequiresUserGesture (matching mediaTypesRequiringUserActionForPlayback = .all) is applied.

Keychain call sites keep the Swift member names (store(value = ...), load(), remove(), Keychain.loadStreamIds(server = ...)); adjust the parameter names if com.moblin.android.various.Keychain differs.
MainTimer was replaced by a coroutine loop with delay(1000) on Dispatchers.Main, per the periodic-timer mapping rule.
ignoresSafeArea(.keyboard) has no direct Compose counterpart and was dropped; use Modifier.imePadding()/WindowInsets if keyboard behaviour matters.
@Binding var presenting became a value parameter presenting plus an onPresentingChange lambda; the value itself is never read in the Swift body either.
Added AudioPlayer.duration() translated from AVAudioPlayer.duration; MediaPlayer reports milliseconds so the value is divided by 1000.0 to keep TimeInterval seconds.
Everything else in the file is unchanged, including the hand-written AudioPlayerDataSource and the MediaPlayer-based constructors.
SwiftUI struct StreamOverlayTextView becomes a single @Composable function taking text as a parameter.
.foregroundStyle(.white) maps to the Text color parameter with Color.White.
.padding(.horizontal, 2) becomes Modifier.padding(horizontal = 2.dp).
.cornerRadius(5) becomes Modifier.clip(RoundedCornerShape(5.dp)).
backgroundColor is imported from com.moblin.android.common.various and used unchanged as the Modifier.background color.
Swift struct MuteIntent becomes a Kotlin class implementing AppIntent, with the static constants moved into a companion object of the same names.
@MainActor func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult becomes override suspend fun perform(): IntentResult, returning IntentResult.result().
@Dependency private var model becomes private val model: Model by Dependency<Model>().
model.setQuickButton(type: .mute, isOn: true) maps the Swift enum case .mute to SettingsQuickButtonType.mute from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
LocalizedStringResource is the platform typealias for String, so title and description keep their Swift literals.
No Android-side permission or UI is needed: the intent runs when its launcher shortcut is used.

AVAudioPCMBuffer has no Android type; per the media mapping it becomes a ShortArray extension function, with sampleRate and channels passed as extra parameters because they were properties of the Swift buffer.

CMAudioSampleBufferCreateWithPacketDescriptions and CMSampleBufferSetDataBufferFromAudioBufferList are replaced by building a MediaSample directly (data + presentationTimeUs + MediaFormat), which is the Android-side equivalent of a non-data-ready audio sample buffer plus attached block buffer.
CMTime presentationTimeStamp becomes Long microseconds, matching MediaSample.presentationTimeUs.
frameLength is recomputed as size / channels to mirror AVAudioPCMBuffer.frameLength (sample frames, not samples).
PCM samples are written little-endian 16-bit into a ByteArray, which is the native PCM layout expected by Android audio codecs.
The format is audio/raw with KEY_PCM_ENCODING = ENCODING_PCM_16BIT (API 24+, fine for minSdk 26).
null is returned when the buffer is empty or channels <= 0, keeping the Swift guard-let behaviour.
MediaSample is constructed with named arguments data/presentationTimeUs/isKeyFrame/format as listed in the project mapping; isKeyFrame is always true because raw PCM has no key frames.
Swift struct UnmuteIntent becomes a Kotlin class implementing AppIntent; it stays constructed with no arguments, as MoblinShortcuts does.
The three Swift static lets move into the companion object; the AppIntent interface does not declare them, so they are plain vals without override.
@MainActor func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult becomes override suspend fun perform(): IntentResult and returns IntentResult.result().
@Dependency private var model: Model becomes a property delegated by Dependency<Model>(), resolved through AppDependencyManager.

model.setMuted(value = false) and model.setQuickButton(type = SettingsQuickButtonType.mute, isOn = false) are Model members, so no import is needed for them; SettingsQuickButtonType comes from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
The two LocalizedStringResource literals are wrapped in localized() from package com.moblin.android, as every localizable String literal in this port.
perform() runs when the Android launcher shortcut for this intent is used; the body is fully ported, no TODO().
Only the perform() call site changed: takeSnapshot now receives age, isChatBot and message, matching the new Swift call with Kotlin named arguments.
Everything else in the file is unchanged.

CMVideoFormatDescription is a CoreMedia value type; on Android it maps to android.media.MediaFormat, so the Swift extension becomes a static-only object named CMVideoFormatDescription holding the factory.
The Swift static func create(imageBuffer:) becomes CMVideoFormatDescription.create(imageBuffer) taking an android.media.Image (the CVPixelBuffer counterpart), preserving the call site shape.

There is no Android API that derives a MediaFormat from an Image: MediaFormat instances come from MediaCodec (getOutputFormat) or MediaExtractor (getTrackFormat), so the creation call and its return value are TODO().
The noErr status check and its logger.info failure message are kept as a Log.i call with tag "CMVideoFormatDescription", as required by the Logger mapping.
CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateForImageBuffer is a CoreVideo/CoreMedia function with no counterpart; nothing here is pure logic, the entire body is hardware/vendor bound.
No other Moblin types from the glossary are referenced by this file, so no cross-package imports beyond the Android framework are needed.
The Swift diff merges two guards in next(); in Kotlin the bounds check was already implicit in AdtsHeader(data, cursor) returning null, so the redundant cursor compare is simply dropped.
Everything else in the file is unchanged and kept byte-identical.
makeFormatDescription keeps the MediaFormat/AAC profile translation of CMAudioFormatDescriptionCreate from the previous port.

UInt8/UInt16 stay UByte/UShort because this file parses and serialises MPEG-TS wire bytes; the shared constants live in the companion object with their Swift names (size, fixedHeaderSize, syncByte, programAssociationTableId).
The Swift throwing initialiser init(reader:) becomes a secondary constructor delegating to the primary one; Kotlin has no checked exceptions, so the read calls are simply invoked.
Swift's `throw "Invalid sync byte"` (String as Error) is mapped to IllegalStateException("Invalid sync byte") because Kotlin has no String-Error conformance.
encodeFixedHeaderInto(pointer:) took an UnsafeMutableRawBufferPointer; it now writes into a ByteArray at an explicit offset (default 0), same byte layout.
Data is ByteArray; concatenation uses the explicit form `data = data + ...` so no plus/plusAssign ambiguity is involved.
TSTimestamp and TSProgramClockReference are caseless Swift enums used as namespaces, so they become Kotlin objects; resolution stays 90 kHz and the 33-bit PTS/DTS mask 0x1_FFFF_FFFF is preserved.
decode still masks each byte with 0xFF before widening, since Kotlin's Byte is signed and would otherwise sign-extend.
The zero check `if (length > 0u)` mirrors the Swift `length > 0`; MpegTsAdaptationField(reader, length) is assumed to be the ported initialiser of the sibling type.
The Swift diff only merges two consecutive `guard let` statements into one in createSilent and foreachAudioSample; behaviour is identical, so the Kotlin file is unchanged.

createSilent and foreachAudioSample in Kotlin are hand-written Android versions (MediaFormat/AudioFormat PCM encoding plus ByteArray payload) rather than literal translations of the AVAudioPCMBuffer/CMBlockBuffer code; those are kept as is.
Null checks equivalent to the merged guards already exist: createSilent always allocates the PCM byte array, and foreachAudioSample early-returns on a null format.
Everything else (setIsSync, getIsSync, muted, withGain, replacePresentationTimeStamp, deepCopyAudioSampleBuffer) is untouched by the diff.
AVFoundation import had no used symbols and was dropped; no Kotlin import is required.
UInt32 maps to UInt and Data maps to ByteArray.
The two Swift initializers become Kotlin secondary constructors, both delegating to super with RtmpMessageType.audio.
Swift 'final class' maps to a plain Kotlin 'class' (final by default).
streamId, timestamp and encoded are assigned, so they are assumed to be mutable properties inherited from RtmpMessage in the same package.
No Android APIs are involved, so the bodies are translated in full without TODO().
RtmpMessage and RtmpMessageType are declared in the same package, so no import lines are needed.
Swift UInt32 fields stay as Kotlin UInt because this is RTMP wire-format code; RtmpMessage.streamId and RtmpMessage.timestamp must use UInt in the parent class for these assignments to compile.
payload: Data maps to encoded: ByteArray, matching the RtmpMessage property name used by the second initializer.
The two Swift designated initializers become two Kotlin secondary constructors delegating to the RtmpMessage(type) superclass constructor.
The AVFoundation import is unused in the Swift source and has no counterpart here.
CMTime is represented as Long microseconds; CMTime.invalid is mapped to the new constant OptionalHeader.invalidTimestamp (Long.MIN_VALUE).
The 90kHz TSTimestamp.resolution is used to convert between microseconds and PES timestamp ticks.
OptionalHeader is a plain class with a no-arg constructor and a ByteArray constructor; Swift's implicit struct memberwise init is not reproduced.
MpegTsPacket is a reference type (class) in Kotlin, so the Swift loop that reuses a single 'packet' var now instantiates a fresh MpegTsPacket per iteration to preserve struct value semantics.
The inout Int payloadOffset buffers of the private append* helpers are replaced by passing the offset in and returning the updated value.
Swift's 'throw "Bad PES start code"' (throwing a String) becomes IllegalStateException("Bad PES start code").
Bit operations on UByte values are done through Int masks/shifts since Kotlin's UByte has no bitwise operators.
MpegTsPacket.payload slices (Data subscripts) become ByteArray.copyOfRange.
Merged the two early-return guards into one condition to mirror the Swift diff.
Kept the Android lease retain/release hooks and the jpegData readback path byte-identical.
Everything else is unchanged from the current Kotlin file.
Swift extension on Model becomes a top-level extension function fun Model.setupAppIntents() in the same package.
AppDependencyManager.shared.add(dependency: self) maps to the AppIntent shim call with the explicit parameter name dependency.
No new types are declared; the extension is an import-only helper so nothing else in the file needs translating.

UIView with an AVSampleBufferDisplayLayer is replaced by android.view.TextureView: its SurfaceTexture is the target a MediaCodec decoder renders into, and it is the only Android view exposing a real Matrix transform.
Both Swift initialisers collapse into one primary constructor (context + AttributeSet); the NSCoder initialiser is dropped because Android views are inflated by the framework.
The overridden layerClass/layer members have no Android counterpart, so PreviewView simply extends TextureView.
AVLayerVideoGravity becomes a VideoGravity enum with identical raw values; the property only stores the value because Android applies scaling in the renderer, not on the view.
render() and flushAndRemoveImage() are TODO("OpenGL ES port") because turning a MediaSample into a displayed frame needs MediaCodec plus an OpenGL ES/SurfaceTexture pipeline.
CGAffineTransformMakeScale(isMirrored ? -1 : 1, 1) is translated with android.graphics.Matrix#setScale about the view centre via TextureView.setTransform, matching the CALayer anchor-point behaviour.
DispatchQueue.main.async becomes CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main).launch.
enqueue takes MediaSample instead of CMSampleBuffer.
The generic SwiftUI view SwiftUI View with Content/Content2 builders becomes a single @Composable CacheAsyncImage taking two slot lambdas (content, placeholder).
URL maps to java.net.URI: it is both the cache key and the source for the OkHttp request.
SwiftUI's AsyncImage is not part of Compose, so loading is done with OkHttp + BitmapFactory on Dispatchers.IO; no third-party image library was assumed.
The @MainActor global cache becomes a file-private val with @Synchronized get/set, keeping the in-memory, process-lifetime semantics.
The cache stores androidx.compose.ui.graphics.ImageBitmap instead of SwiftUI.Image; callers draw it with Image(bitmap = it).
The scale parameter is kept for signature parity but has no effect because content is a composable slot.
The placeholder slot is rendered while the download is in flight and when it fails, matching AsyncImage's placeholder behaviour.
The load runs in LaunchedEffect(url) so re-composition with the same URL does not refetch, and a successful load is stored into the shared cache.

The Swift rewrite drives NWConnection directly with NWProtocolWebSocket.Metadata; the Android platform layer only exposes the WebSocket shim (NWWebSocket/NWProtocolWebSocket.Options/CloseCode), so the transport stays NWWebSocket and the connection state/viability/message/pong handling maps onto the WebSocketConnectionDelegate callbacks.

The new private helpers handleStateUpdate/handleViabilityUpdate/handleMessage/receiveMessage/send/handleSendError/sendPing have no separate Kotlin counterpart because the shim delivers those events through the delegate; their logic lives in the matching override bodies.

stop(closeCode:) now takes the close code with the same default (.protocolCode(.normalClosure)) and forwards it to webSocket.disconnect(closeCode) so the close frame is sent like Swift's NWProtocolWebSocket.Metadata(opcode: .close).
handleDisconnected() is added: it remembers connected, restarts the connect timer and only notifies the delegate when the socket had been connected, matching the new Swift behaviour.
The ping timer now logs 'websocket: Pong not received' and only reports a disconnect when the client was connected before restarting.
Swift's deinit { connection?.cancel() } has no Kotlin equivalent; stopInternal() cancels the shim socket and there is no finalizer to keep.
The Context constructor parameter stays because NetworkInterfaceTypeSelector needs it; the Swift init never had one.
swift's `.url(url)` endpoint and `defaultProtocolStack.applicationProtocols` are handled inside the NWWebSocket shim (ws -> tcp, wss -> tls, subprotocols, autoReplyPing).
URL.documentsDirectory.appending(component:) becomes a File under AppDelegate.context.filesDir, stored as a String path in the global faceBackgroundImagePath.
Model is an ObservableObject, so the @Published faceBackgroundImage is read and written as a MutableStateFlow: faceBackgroundImage.value = ...
try? Data(contentsOf:) and try? data.write(to:) become runCatching { File(...).readBytes() }.getOrNull() and runCatching { File(...).writeBytes(data) }.
UIImage(data:) is the platform shim from com.moblin.android.platform.uikit and returns a Bitmap?, whose .cgImage identity extension feeds CIImage(cgImage = ...).
The nonisolated keyword is dropped; Kotlin has no actor isolation.
The Swift extension on Model becomes top-level extension functions in the same package, so Model itself needs no import.
updateFaceFilterSettings() is expected to exist as a Model extension in another file of this package and is called unchanged.

The Swift change merges two guard statements into one with no behavioural difference; the Kotlin guard already short-circuits in the same order, so the file stays semantically and literally identical.
Swift CIImage(data:) maps to BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray on Android; the check that data is present and the HTTP response is successful is kept before decoding.
Delegate callbacks are dispatched on Dispatchers.Main to mirror the @MainActor annotation on FaxReceiverDelegate and FaxReceiver.
The weak delegate has no Kotlin counterpart; it is a plain nullable var, so the caller must clear it.
The Swift diff only merges three guards into one; the merged Kotlin condition keeps the same short-circuit behaviour and the same lookups.
UIPress/UIPress.key remain translated as android.view.KeyEvent with the existing unicodeChar helper, which was hand-written for Android and is kept.
The keyboardKey lookup now happens before the emptiness/modifier checks, matching the single combined guard; the null check inside the same `if` still lets the val smart-cast afterwards.
DispatchQueue.main.async stays mainScope.launch as before.
Class name typo "RtmpAbortMessge" (missing 'a' in Message) is preserved verbatim from Swift.
`Data` maps to `ByteArray`; array equality uses `contentEquals` because ByteArray has no `==`.
`chunkStreamId` stays an unsigned `UInt` since it is a 32-bit wire-format field.
The Swift `UInt32.bigEndian.data` and `UInt32(data:)` extension helpers are not in the glossary, so they are inlined as explicit big-endian read/write of the first 4 bytes.
`override var encoded` reads and writes `super.encoded`, i.e. the base class accessors, avoiding recursion.
Swift `init()` calling `super.init(type: .abort)` becomes a secondary constructor `constructor() : super(RtmpMessageType.abort)`.
No apple-only APIs are used here, so nothing is replaced with TODO().
The Swift `extension Model` becomes top-level Kotlin extension functions on Model in the same package; no type is redeclared.

`URL.documentsDirectory.appending(component:)` has no context-free Android equivalent, so the top-level `stealthModeImagePath` getter is TODO() that resolves to File(context.filesDir, "stealthModeImage.img").
`Data` becomes ByteArray; `try? data.write(to:)` becomes runCatching { file.writeBytes(data) } so a failed write is silently ignored as in Swift.
`loadStealthModeImage` decodes the stored bytes with android.graphics.BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray and assigns null when the file is missing, matching the guard-let early return.
`UIImage` is mapped to android.graphics.Bitmap, which is the expected type of StealthMode.image in this port.
`FileManager.default.removeItem(at:)` becomes File.delete(), which also reports failure via its Boolean result instead of throwing.
RemoteControlState is not part of the provided glossary, so it is referenced by name from the same package as Model without being redeclared.
This file contains no SwiftUI views, so no @Composable functions are produced despite the ui tier.
Kotlin has no `super.property` access, so the overridden `encoded` uses a private `_encoded` backing field; the base class stores nothing else for this property, so it is equivalent.
`size` is kept as `UInt` because `UInt32` is wire-format data.
Added file-private helpers `uint32ToBigEndianBytes` and `readUInt32BigEndian` to replace the HaishinKit `UInt32.bigEndian.data` and `UInt32(data:)` conversions.
Assumes `RtmpMessage` exposes `open var encoded: ByteArray` and a constructor taking `RtmpMessageType`; the override follows Android's `: View { constructor() : super(...) }` delegation pattern.
The two Swift initializers become two secondary Kotlin constructors, since the base constructor requires an argument.
The `import AVFoundation` line is dropped: no AVFoundation API is actually used in this file.
Getter returns the existing bytes when non-empty, otherwise encodes `size`; setter early-returns on equal bytes and decodes `size` from the first four big-endian bytes.
CMFormatDescription maps to android.media.MediaFormat; the HEVC parameter sets are carried in the "csd-0" byte buffer as the ISO/IEC 14496-15 hvcC box.
getHvcC() reads csd-0 and strips the 8-byte hvcC box header (size + 'hvcC' type) when it is present, returning the raw configuration record the parser expects.
init?(formatDescription:) becomes the companion factory create(formatDescription:) because Kotlin has no failable constructors; callers must null-check the result.
The raw hvcC record is kept in an extra private property (hvcC) so makeFormatDescription() can rebuild the complete hvcC box for csd-0.
kCMFormatDescriptionBridgeError_InvalidParameter is kept as a private Int placeholder; on Android any non-zero return value means the format could not be created.
logger.info maps to android.util.Log.i with the class name as tag.
ByteReader is assumed to throw on truncated input, matching the Swift do/catch around the whole loop.
The exact csd-0 hvcC box layout should be verified against the target MediaCodec HEVC decoder during device integration.

AVPictureInPictureController, its ContentSource, AVPictureInPictureSampleBufferPlaybackDelegate and CMVideoDimensions come from the AVKit shim (platform/avkit), which shows the stream preview in an Activity picture-in-picture window: auto-enter on API 31+, enterPictureInPictureMode on user leave before.
setupPictureInPicture(), updatePictureInPicture() and pictureInPictureEnabled() are top-level extension functions on Model reading pipController, stream, isLive and isRecording like Swift.

Kotlin extensions cannot add interface conformance, so the delegate methods are Model extensions and the private ModelPictureInPicturePlaybackDelegate forwards to them; it is passed as playbackDelegate where Swift passes self.
CMTimeRange is the avfoundation shim's CMTimeRange with Long microseconds, Long.MIN_VALUE/Long.MAX_VALUE for negative/positive infinity; skipByInterval is Long microseconds.
The no-op delegate callbacks keep empty bodies and skipByInterval invokes the completion callback, preserving the Swift behaviour.
StoreKit has no Android counterpart; every function that touches StoreKit products or transactions got the body TODO("no Android counterpart for StoreKit").
struct Icon -> data class Icon(name, id, price) keeping both helper functions imageNoBackground() and image(); Swift's Identifiable has no Kotlin equivalent, equals/hashCode come from the data class.
The Model extension becomes top-level extension functions on Model in com.moblin.android.various.model, matching the original declaration order.
listenForAppStoreTransactions() returned Task<Void, any Error>; it now takes a CoroutineScope and returns the Job of the launched coroutine.
checkVerified(result:) used Swift's opaque VerificationResult<StoreKit.Transaction>; its parameter and return type are Any? because those StoreKit types do not exist in the port.
purchaseProduct(id:) and restorePurchases() were async throws; Kotlin has no checked exceptions, so they stay plain suspend functions (their bodies are TODO).
The global logger is replaced by a file-private Log tag constant named TAG with value "Model".
updateIcons(myProductIds:) keeps its full loop and store bookkeeping; only the Icon built from StoreKit product metadata (displayName/displayPrice/id) is a TODO.
needs_user: StoreKit: Product.products(for:), Transaction.updates, VerificationResult, AppStore.sync(), Product.purchase(), Transaction.currentEntitlements, Transaction.finish() (needs Google Play Billing and the icon products in the Play Console)

notes: WebBrowserState keeps its name; @Published isSmall becomes a MutableStateFlow exposed as StateFlow plus setIsSmall(value) for the views that toggle it.
The Model extension becomes top-level extension functions on Model in this package (loadWebBrowserUrl, loadWebBrowserHome, loadWebBrowserPage, getWebBrowser, setWebBrowserProxy).
WKWebView maps to android.webkit.WebView, so webBrowserUrl becomes a String and getWebBrowserUrl returns String? (WebView.loadUrl takes a String, not a URL object).
URL scheme detection uses java.net.URI with runCatching, matching Swift's URL(string:) leniency; the search fallback is built by string interpolation as in Swift.
The WKNavigationDelegate method becomes Model.webViewDidStartProvisionalNavigation and is wired in through a WebViewClient.onPageStarted override installed by getWebBrowser().
getWebBrowser() needs a Context to build android.webkit.WebView; Model does not expose one in this file, so the Context argument is a TODO that must be filled in.
mainScope is a file-private CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main) used for the DispatchQueue.main.async call.
WKWebViewConfiguration.setHttpProxy and WKUIDelegate have no Android counterpart and are TODO placeholders.
CrtEffect is final in Swift, so the Kotlin class is a plain class extending VideoEffect().
CrtBarrelDistortionFilter.outputImage is declared as Any?, so it is cast back with `as? CIImage` before the Swift `?? image` fallback.
CrtBarrelDistortionFilter.width is a Float while Swift's CGFloat becomes Double, so the width argument is converted with toFloat().
Swift CGFloat values (extent.width, cropRect.height) become Double throughout; Core Image filter scalar properties stay Float as declared by the shims.
CIColor literals are written with Double values (0.0, 0.25) because the shim has no Int constructor overload.
scanlineWidth keeps Swift's Float computation with maxOf(1.0f, ...).
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin equivalent and is dropped.
stripes.center = .zero becomes CGPoint.zero and CGAffineTransform(rotationAngle: .pi / 2) becomes CGAffineTransform(rotationAngle = PI / 2).
Swift final class maps to a plain Kotlin class extending VideoEffect; the @unchecked Sendable conformance is dropped because Kotlin has no Sendable.
The Swift `.init(content:position:size:)` shorthand inside the layers array becomes an explicit MTILayer(...) with named arguments.
`.black` on MTIImage resolves to the MTIImage.black companion value; `CIImage.black` keeps its platform name.
CGRect is built with the (x, y, width, height) labelled constructor using Double values (0.0 instead of the Int literal 0 to avoid overload ambiguity).
`filter.outputImage ?? image` stays as `filter.outputImage ?: image`.
The unused VideoEffectInfo parameters are named `info` to satisfy the platform signature.
TripleEffect is a final Swift class, so it becomes a plain class extending VideoEffect() and keeps its two CIFilter instances as reusable properties.

The project's CIImage.translated(x:y:) helper is not part of the Core Image shim, so both calls are written as transformed(by: CGAffineTransform(translationX = x, y = 0.0)), the exact equivalent of that helper.
Swift's unused second parameter (_) becomes the named parameter info, matching VideoEffect's Kotlin signature.
The MetalPetal path builds filter.layers from a (0 until 3).map { } range, exactly as the Swift (0 ..< 3).map does.
@unchecked Sendable is dropped; Kotlin has no concurrency annotation counterpart here.
CGSize/CGRect/CGPoint are the platform CoreGraphics shims with Double fields, so width and height stay Double and index + 0.5 promotes to Double.
No TODO() is needed: every call used here exists in the Core Image and MetalPetal shims.

Swift `final class MovieEffect: VideoEffect` becomes a plain `class MovieEffect : VideoEffect()` with `override fun` members; the `@unchecked Sendable` conformance is dropped since Kotlin has no Sendable protocol.

The Swift `execute(_ image: CIImage, _: VideoEffectInfo)` shape is translated to the declared base signature `override fun execute(image: CIImage, info: VideoEffectInfo): CIImage`, keeping the same call sites.
Core Image chain stays as shim calls: `cropped(to:)`, `composited(over:)` and `CIImage.black` are unchanged apart from named arguments.

MTIImage array elements written as `.init(content:position:size:)` become explicit `MTILayer(content = …, position = …, size = …)` constructors, using MetalPetal's defaults for the remaining parameters.
`filter.layers` takes a `List<MTILayer>`, so the Swift array literal is a `listOf(...)`.
`filter.outputImage ?? image` keeps the MetalPetal fallback as the Kotlin elvis operator.
CGRect/CGSize/CGPoint come from com.moblin.android.platform.coregraphics and take Double fields, so the Swift CGFloat arithmetic is unchanged.
Added the @Published photosImageQuality Double property as MutableStateFlow(0.95) after externalCameraVideoRange, matching Swift declaration order.
Added the matching photosImageQuality key to encode() and to decode(), both positioned after externalCameraVideoRange as in the Swift diff.
CodingKeys is not translated; JSON keys are the literal strings passed to encode/decode, so the new key is written as "photosImageQuality".
SwiftUI Text with an empty string and a full-size frame becomes a Box with Modifier.fillMaxSize() wrapping an empty Text.
.background(.black.opacity(0.01)) maps to Modifier.background(Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.01f)).
.onTapGesture(count: 2) maps to Modifier.pointerInput(Unit) { detectTapGestures(onDoubleTap = { ... }) }.
model is passed in as a Compose parameter exactly like the SwiftUI View property; toggleLockScreen() is called directly on it.
No state or navigation is needed, so no remember or onNavigate parameter is introduced.
Snapshot's published properties are modelled as StateFlow and read with collectAsState().
The Swift `if let ... && countdown > 0` guard becomes an early return on the collected nullable job and a countdown check.
`.frame(maxWidth: 300)` maps to Modifier.widthIn(max = 300.dp); `.fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)` has no direct Compose equivalent and is covered by wrapping content sizing.
`.font(.title)` becomes MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge.
`.multilineTextAlignment(.center)` becomes textAlign = TextAlign.Center.
`.background(.black.opacity(0.75))` becomes Modifier.background(Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.75f)).
`.cornerRadius(10)` becomes Modifier.clip(RoundedCornerShape(10.dp)).
@MainActor on getOrientation/isPhone/isPad/getWindow/getRootViewController/screenScale is dropped; the Kotlin functions are plain and are called from the main thread.
getOrientation's body starts at the interface orientation, as specified: the port's platform hook prepends the com.moblin.android.platform.uikit.UIDevice.current.orientation check before it.
This file declares object UIDevice (vibration only), which shadows the UIKit UIDevice, so the UIKit one is referenced fully qualified as com.moblin.android.platform.uikit.UIDevice.

DeviceOrientation mirrors UIDeviceOrientation with UPPER_SNAKE entries; UIInterfaceOrientation.landscapeLeft maps to LANDSCAPE_RIGHT and landscapeRight to LANDSCAPE_LEFT, exactly as the Swift switch does.
interface Identifiable<ID> { val id: ID } is declared here because Kotlin has no standard-library equivalent, and makeOffsets is generic over it.
makeOffsets returns Int? (the index) instead of IndexSet?, matching the shape its callers use.
UIImage.resize(height:) becomes Bitmap.resize(height: Float) with Bitmap.createScaledBitmap at 1x instead of UIGraphicsImageRenderer, as the port specifies.
screenScale() returns Float and keeps the UIScreen.main.scale fallback; isMac() is always false and ProcessInfo is not instantiated.

Swift's CIImage `translated(x:y:)` and `scaled(x:y:)` helpers are not declared in the Kotlin platform layer, so both are written with the declared `transformed(by = CGAffineTransform(...))`, which produces the identical matrices.
`@unchecked Sendable` is dropped; the effect is executed on the pipeline thread only, as in Swift.
The private `CIFilter.sourceOverCompositing()` instance is reused across frames, exactly like the Swift stored `filter` property (it is only mutated on the pipeline thread).
`CGRect`, `CGSize` and `CGPoint` come from com.moblin.android.platform.coregraphics and hold Double values, so `width` and `height` are Double and feed `CGAffineTransform` directly.

MTILayers are built with the Kotlin constructor's named parameters `content`, `contentRegion`, `contentFlipOptions`, `position`, `size`, and `contentFlipOptions` uses `MTILayer.FlipOptions.flipHorizontally` instead of `.flipHorizontally`.
`filter.outputImage ?? image` becomes `filter.outputImage ?: image`, keeping the Core Image / MetalPetal fallback.
NavigationLink destinations become an onNavigate: (String) -> Unit callback using the destination view name as the route string.

Form and ScrollView both map to LazyColumn; ForEach maps to LazyListScope.items with the attribution name as key.
.font(.title2) maps to MaterialTheme.typography.headlineSmall.
Purely layout-driving Spacer() views from the SwiftUI HStack/LazyVStack were dropped since LazyColumn already fills the screen.
The Swift `private let` attribution tables are kept as private top-level vals so they stay file-scoped, matching the Swift visibility.
The Attribution struct has only stored properties and became a private data class.
The trailing space in "Credit Richie Velasquez " is preserved verbatim.

Material 3 ListItem replaces the plain Form row plus its chevron.

ReplaysStorage now owns a `storage` and a `directory`; the constructor takes a nullable `directory: File?` like the Swift `init(directory: URL? = nil)`, creating `<directory>/Database` and `<directory>/Replays`, or falling back to the module-level `defaultStorage` and Documents/Replays.
The top-level `getReplaysDirectory()` helper was deleted, as in Swift; every use is now the instance `directory` (ReplaySettings.url() is gone too, replaced by ReplaysStorage.url(replay)).

`database.replays` stays the Android `MutableStateFlow<List<ReplaySettings>>` with `setReplays(...)`; the Kotlin list ops stand in for the Swift in-place mutations (popLast/removeLast -> dropLast(1), insert at 0 -> listOf(replay) + ...).

cleanup() now filters with `url(it).exists()` and walks the directory on a background coroutine: DispatchQueue.global(qos: .utility).async -> CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO).launch (a concurrent global queue, not a serial one).
The background walk captures the `knownNames` Set and the `directory` built before launching, and logs with Log.d plus File.remove(), matching Swift's logger.debug and fileUrl.remove().
Declaration order follows the new Swift file: url(replay:) then the private cleanup(), tryLoadAndMigrate(settings:) and migrateFromOlderVersions() at the end.
AddButtonView is a stateless view, so it becomes a @Composable function taking the Swift closure as a Kotlin lambda.

CIFilter.sepiaTone() keeps its name and the CISepiaTone shim's inputImage/intensity members; intensity 0.9 is written as 0.9f.
execute and executeMetalPetal keep the ?? image fallbacks on outputImage.
MTIColorMatrixFilter is a MetalPetal shim class, so no MetalPetal context or TODO is needed.
The 'nonisolated(unsafe)' attribute and '@unchecked Sendable' conformance have no Kotlin counterpart and are dropped.
CloseToolbarButtonView becomes a @Composable taking the @Binding as a Boolean value plus an onPresentingChange lambda.
The SwiftUI Button with an Image label maps to IconButton with Icon for tap target sizing.
Image(systemName: "xmark") maps to Icons.Default.Close with contentDescription = null.
CloseToolbar (a ToolbarContent) becomes a @Composable that emits the button; place its call inside a Material 3 TopAppBar actions slot.

Both declarations are top-level composable functions, so no Kotlin types are declared in this file.
No coroutines, state holders or serialization are needed here; the boolean owner lives in the calling screen.
Localization note for the Swift file: no user-facing strings, so no localized() calls are required.
Both SwiftUI structs became @Composable functions with the same names, per the ui tier contract.
ShareLink(item = text) and SystemImage come from com.moblin.android.platform.swiftui and com.moblin.android.platform.
The label tint uses LocalTint.current, as required for Image(systemName:).font(.system(size:)).

No SwiftUI view is present in this file, so no @Composable function was generated.

@EnvironmentObject Model becomes a plain Composable parameter; model.sendSettingsToWatch() is invoked from the LaunchedEffect blocks.

No iOS-only APIs are used in this file, so no TODO markers were introduced.

No iOS-only API is used, so there is nothing in the unsupported list.

No SwiftUI preview/dialog features were present, so no member needed a TODO.

Swift's generic `Content: View` parameter is unnecessary in Compose: HCenter becomes a @Composable function taking a `@Composable () -> Unit` content lambda, as required by the tier rules.
HCenter's HStack with leading/trailing Spacer maps to a Row with Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f)) on both sides.

The `View.hCenter(_:)` extension cannot be a composable wrapper, so it becomes `Modifier.hCenter(center: Boolean): Modifier`, implemented with fillMaxWidth() + wrapContentWidth(Alignment.CenterHorizontally) when centering is requested and returned unchanged otherwise.
The private HCenterModifier ViewModifier is kept as a private @Composable wrapper function that branches on `center` exactly like the Swift body.

There is no Compose counterpart to ViewModifier, so HCenterModifier is only callable from Compose code (it is retained for side-by-side readability; the Modifier extension is the practical entry point).
No iOS-only APIs are used in this file, so nothing is stubbed with TODO().
The view is a single conditional Text; it becomes one @Composable function with an if/else branch.

No @State, sheets, alerts or navigation are used in this file, so no Compose state or navigation handling is needed.
submit returns the clamped value as a String exactly like the Swift implementation.

layoutLayers() centralises hiding/showing the device layers and the selection transform, then calls layoutWidgets(); onLayout now just calls layoutLayers().

The SwiftUI body's if/else is a plain Kotlin if inside the @Composable function.

No View state, modifiers or navigation exist in the source, so the Composable stays a bare Text with no Modifier parameter.
