scanner is TeslaVehicleScanner.shared; discoveredPeripherals is collected with collectAsState() next to bluetoothAllowed.
.onAppear/.onDisappear become DisposableEffect(Unit) calling startScanningForDevices()/stopScanningForDevices().
The nested SwiftUI List is dropped: its ForEach rows are plain Section rows of the Form, keyed by the InlinePickerItem id.
ProgressView has no platform shim, so it is a Material 3 CircularProgressIndicator with the iOS gray tint and a 20dp size.
peripheral.identifier.uuidString becomes peripheral.identifier.toString().
dismiss comes from rememberDismiss(), so the view takes no dismiss parameter; onChange stays a normal parameter.
The Section footer string is passed to Section(footer = ...) instead of a footerContent Text closure.
AvcNalUnitType becomes an enum class with a UByte rawValue plus a companion fromRawValue(); the static isPicture(type:) lives in the companion object.
AvcNalUnit.init?(data:offset:) has no Kotlin equivalent, so it becomes companion create(data, offset) returning AvcNalUnit?; init(type:payload:) is a secondary constructor.
AvcNalUnitHeader.init(reader:) becomes companion from(reader) because a delegating constructor cannot read bits; the primary constructor keeps (refIdc, type) exactly like the Swift memberwise one.
AvcNalUnitPayload's associated values became nested classes Pps/Sps/Sei plus object Unspec; encode(writer:) switches over them.

makeFormatDescription() returns android.media.MediaFormat with csd-0/csd-1 instead of CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateFromH264ParameterSets; the Swift format description carried no dimensions, so createVideoFormat is called with 0,0 and the real width/height must be filled in from the SPS when decoding.
The csd-0 (SPS) and csd-1 (PPS) buffers are prefixed with the 4-byte start code, which MediaCodec requires for H.264, while the Swift parameter-set API wanted the bare NAL units.
The translation assumes the ported NalUnit interface declares encode(): ByteArray and that NalUnitWriter exposes a data: ByteArray property and writeBit(Boolean)/writeBits(UByte, Int) methods.
The commented-out logger.debug call is dropped; no logging is emitted on parse failure.
Form with a single Section becomes a LazyColumn; the section has no header in Swift so only the row item is emitted.
webBrowser.home is read with collectAsState() because DeepLinkCreatorWebBrowser publishes it as a StateFlow; submitHome writes through webBrowser.home.value.
submitHome is kept as a private file-level function taking the model plus the value, since Compose composables have no member functions.
.navigationTitle("Web browser") becomes the title of a Scaffold TopAppBar, so this screen owns its own top bar until the parent navigation host supplies one.
String(localized:) calls map to the top-level localized() from package com.moblin.android.
TextEditNavigationView is imported from com.moblin.android.view.utils and called with title/value/onSubmit/capitalize, matching the original argument labels.
No navigation-compose dependency is pulled in here; the title is the only navigation affordance.
No top-level Kotlin type is declared in this file, only the composable function.
The file contains no SwiftUI views, so no Compose composables are produced; it is a static-only class and therefore becomes a Kotlin object named GoPro.
UIImage? is mapped to android.graphics.Bitmap?, the Android equivalent for a generated QR code image.
The Swift switch expression over SettingsGoProLaunchLiveStreamResolution becomes a Kotlin when expression returning the same suffixes (!GL, !GM, !GS) byte-for-byte.

The Kotlin enum constants of SettingsGoProLaunchLiveStreamResolution are assumed to be R1080P, R720P and R480P following Kotlin naming conventions; adjust if the settings package uses different names.
generateQrCode from com.moblin.android.various.utils is called positionally with the payload string, mirroring generateQrCode(from:).
Interpolated Swift string literals are preserved exactly (quotes and leading ! are significant for the GoPro QR payload).
No shared state, coroutines or IO are involved, so the object stays synchronous.
UIKeyboardType is mapped to androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType and applied through androidx.compose.foundation.text.KeyboardOptions.

The outer view's @State value/errorMessage/submittedValue become remember { mutableStateOf } holders; because TextEditNavigationViewInner is a separate screen the state must be hoisted/re-created by whoever builds the destination route.

NavigationLink is replaced by Modifier.clickable plus onNavigate("TextEditNavigationViewInner"); the destination composable has to be instantiated by the navigation host with the same parameters (no navigation-compose is pulled in here).
onChange(of: value) -> LaunchedEffect(value), which (unlike SwiftUI) also runs on first composition, so onChange is invoked once with the initial value.
keyboardType / textInputAutocapitalization / disableAutocorrection / submitLabel are merged into a single KeyboardOptions (capitalization, autoCorrectEnabled, imeAction).

onSubmit { submit(); dismiss() } -> KeyboardActions(onDone = { submit(); onDismiss() }) and .onDisappear -> DisposableEffect(Unit) { onDispose { submit() } }, which captures the first-composition closure.
Form/Section -> Column + LazyColumn, .navigationTitle -> Material 3 TopAppBar (requires the ExperimentalMaterial3Api opt-in).

TextItemView is called with name/value/sensitive exactly as in the Swift call site; its Kotlin signature lives in this same package - verify the parameter names and add an onClick/Modifier parameter if it exposes one.
The Swift diff is purely cosmetic: an if/available block was joined into a single condition and the filter/optional-binding chain was reflowed. No behaviour changes, so the Kotlin file is unchanged.
removeNalUnitStartCodes keeps the Android hand-written copy-then-move implementation (System.arraycopy into a new array) that stands in for Data.moveSubranges, which needs iOS 18.
readNalUnits keeps its extra create lambda parameter because Kotlin has no generic failable initializer on the NalUnit interface.
Byte comparisons stay unsigned via toInt() and 0xFF, matching Swift UInt8 indexing.
SwiftUI Views become @Composable top-level functions with the same names, so TextButtonView, ExternalButtonView and ExternalUrlButtonView exist as composables in this file.

TextButtonView's two Swift initialisers (LocalizedStringKey and String) collapse into a single composable because Kotlin has only one String type; call localized(title) at the call site when the title is localised.
.buttonStyle(.borderless) maps to TextButton instead of Button.
Spacers inside the Button label Row use Modifier.weight(1f) as the layout rule requires.
ExternalButtonView and ExternalUrlButtonView take their Swift @ViewBuilder content as a @Composable () -> Unit parameter.
Section { } has no direct Compose container here, so the wrapped content is emitted as a Column.
Image(systemName: "arrow.turn.up.right") maps to Icon(Icons.Default.ArrowForward, contentDescription = null).
openUrl is imported from com.moblin.android.various.utils and called with the url argument.

The only Swift change is URLSession.shared -> httpUrlSession() in fetchTwitchProfilePicture; the Kotlin hand-written OkHttpClient profilePictureHttpClient was replaced by the shared com.moblin.android.various.network.httpUrlSession() client for both calls.

The unused java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit and okhttp3.OkHttpClient imports and the private profilePictureHttpClient declaration were removed together with that change; the 10 second timeout now comes from the shared session.
Message.truncate(length: 500) stays message.take(500) (Kotlin String length is UTF-16 while Swift counts graphemes; the API limit is a byte/character budget and this matches the previous port).
TwitchApi is a plain class here, not a @MainActor class: callbacks run on mainScope, preserving the MainActor delivery of the Swift callbacks.
serialize() keeps the org.json JSONObject.wrap path so nested dictionaries and lists encode as on iOS.
Decoding uses kotlinx.serialization with ignoreUnknownKeys, matching JSONDecoder's tolerance of extra Twitch fields, and @SerialName for the "2" and "static" CodingKeys.
httpRequest's completion delivers okhttp3 Response; forbiddenIsAuthError maps to response.code == 403 and unauthorized to 401, as before.
fetchTwitchProfilePicture still runs on Dispatchers.IO and decodes the avatar bytes with BitmapFactory into an ImageBitmap (UIImage(data:) equivalent).
UIImage/CGContext/CALayer rendering is replaced by android.graphics.Bitmap + Canvas, and SDWebImage loading by OkHttp + BitmapFactory.
android.graphics.Movie exposes no per-frame timing, so animated emote frames are sampled at 15 fps across the clip's total duration (animatedFrameRate).
EmotesPlayer.shared is a companion getter that requires EmotesPlayer.initialize(context) before first use, so it can resolve bundled drawables.
CADisplayLink is replaced by a coroutine loop on Dispatchers.Main ticking every ~66 ms.
sizesVersion is exposed as a StateFlow of Int and incremented by the load callbacks.
EmoteUiView is a plain state-holder class; layoutSubviews became onSizeChanged, while the sibling @Composable EmoteUiView(...) draws the frame and drives register/unregister.
EmoteBorder and EmoteKey are internal instead of private because EmotesPlayer's internal members expose them in their signatures.
ChatImageSource.Symbol cannot resolve a dynamic icon name on Android, so its render branch is TODO().
HevcNalUnitType keeps its Swift raw values as UByte and gains a companion fromRawValue plus the static isPicture helper.
Swift's enum-with-associated-values HevcNalUnitPayload became a sealed class; vps/sps/pps/prefixSeiNut are nested classes holding their value in a `payload` property, unspec is an object.

The failable Swift init?(data:offset:) has no Kotlin constructor counterpart, so it is a companion operator fun invoke(data, offset): HevcNalUnit? which keeps the HevcNalUnit(data, offset) call shape.
HevcNalUnitHeader's throwing reader initialiser is a companion operator fun invoke(reader) so HevcNalUnitHeader(reader) keeps the same call shape.

NalUnitReader.readBits/skipBits and NalUnitWriter.writeBit/writeBits/bitOffset/data are assumed to come from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.mpeg with UByte bit values, mirroring the Swift UInt8 parameters.

The [HevcNalUnit] extension became a top-level extension on List<HevcNalUnit>; CMVideoFormatDescriptionCreateFromHEVCParameterSets has no Android equivalent so the format description creation is TODO().
The file-global 'calendar' maps to a java.util.Calendar pinned to UTC (Swift Calendar(identifier: .iso8601) with UTC time zone).
writeRbspTrailingBits and writeMoreDataInPayload are unchanged top-level functions.
Removed createSpeechSynthesizer(), the Android TextToSpeech equivalent of the deleted AVSpeechSynthesizer factory.
The now unused android.speech.tts.TextToSpeech import is kept so every untouched line stays byte-identical, as the incremental rules require.
No other Kotlin declaration in Utils.kt maps to a line in the diff, so everything else is unchanged.
SwiftUI Form/Section with footer becomes a LazyColumn whose last item is the footer Text.
navigationTitle is rendered as a Material 3 TopAppBar inside a Scaffold.
The Swift trailing-closure argument of ExternalUrlButtonView is passed as the trailing @Composable content lambda.
The multi-line Swift string literal (joined with a backslash) is written as a single concatenated localised string.
@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class) is required for TopAppBar.
The view takes no parameters, matching the Swift struct's empty property list.
Added constructor parameter colorRange: SettingsStreamColorRange between softwareDecoding and delegate, matching the new Swift init order.
Added a private colorRange property on SrtClient (constructor val) and a matching import of SettingsStreamColorRange.
Passed colorRange = colorRange to both MpegTsReader constructions, the one in init and the one rebuilt in main().
All other Kotlin lines, including the hand-written reader.stop() calls and the socket/URI handling, are unchanged.
Added the colorRange constructor parameter and forwarded it to MpegTsReader's colorRange argument.
Added the SettingsStreamColorRange import from com.moblin.android.various.settings.
Everything else, including the hand-written ristServerDispatcher helper and the server property, stays byte-identical.
RistServerDelegate.ristServerOnConnected now takes cameraId, name and latency instead of a port; ristServerOnDisconnected takes cameraId and name instead of port and reason.
Added private notifyDisconnected(virtualDestinationPort: Int) that resolves the stream by virtual destination port, mirroring the Swift guard-let.
stopInternal and peerDisconnected now call notifyDisconnected, so the disconnect callback is only sent for known virtual destination ports.
peerConnected reports the stream's id, camera() name and latencySeconds() through the new connected signature.
UInt16 virtual destination ports stay Int in Kotlin, as in the rest of the port.
This file exists only for macCatalyst; Android has no status-item bridge, so the helper entry points keep their signatures with TODO() bodies.
The MoblinMac plugin types MacStatusItem and MacStatusItemDelegate have no counterpart and no glossary entry, so minimal Kotlin interfaces are declared in this file.
macStatusItem is a stored Model property in Swift (extensions cannot store properties); here it is a top-level extension property on Model backed by a WeakHashMap.
makeMacStatusItemStatusTitle() is translated in full because it only joins localized strings.
String(localized:) maps to localized() imported from com.moblin.android.
logger.info maps to Log.i with the tag "Model".
The Swift #else branch (empty stubs) is represented by the same three function names; their bodies are TODO because the macCatalyst plugin bundle cannot be loaded on Android.
apple_only: NSBundle.main.builtInPlugInsURL / Bundle(url:) / principalClass plugin bundle loading (MoblinMac.bundle)
macCatalyst NSStatusItem bridge (MacStatusItem helper object)
UIImage(named:)?.pngData() icon encoding
MacStatusItemDelegate conformance declared from an extension

notes: ThermalStateView is a SwiftUI struct: it becomes a @Composable function with the same name, an extra trailing Modifier parameter and thermalState kept first.
Image(systemName: "flame") with .font(.system(size: 11)) and .foregroundStyle(...) is the platform SystemImage composable with fontSize = 11.sp and tint = thermalState.color().
ProcessInfo.ThermalState comes from com.moblin.android.platform.core and keeps its Swift case names (nominal, fair, serious, critical).
thermalState.color() is the existing Kotlin extension fun ProcessInfo.ThermalState.color(): Color; it is imported from the same com.moblin.android.common.view package as this view.
compactAudioLevelColors returns Pair<Color, Color> because Kotlin has no tuples; callers use .first/.second (Swift callers destructure the tuple).
Image(systemName:) is resolved by the private helper compactAudioLevelIcon, mapping the SF Symbol speaker/mic names to Material Icons.Filled.VolumeUp/VolumeDown/VolumeOff/VolumeMute.
.foregroundStyle(foregroundColor) becomes the Icon tint parameter.
.font(smallFont) has no effect on a Material Icon, which is sized purely by Modifier.size(17.dp); it is therefore not applied.
.contentShape(Rectangle()) only widens the hit-test region and has no Compose counterpart; it is dropped (no gesture is attached in this file).
.padding(20) followed by .padding(-20) only expands the tap area in SwiftUI; Compose rejects negative padding, so both are dropped and the wrapped layout is unchanged.
clippingThresholdDb/redThresholdDb/yellowThresholdDb/zeroThresholdDb/defaultAudioLevel stay top-level Float vals in the same package so other files keep the same names.
The composable parameter backgroundColor intentionally shadows the package-level backgroundColor color, exactly as in the Swift struct.
Enum cases beforeIcon/afterIcon/hide became PascalCase entries BeforeIcon/AfterIcon/Hide; comparison kept identical.
The row is Compose Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(1.dp)) with vertical centering, matching HStack(spacing: 1).
Image(systemName: icon) uses a dynamic SF Symbol name, so there is no Material icon to substitute; the painter is TODO() and listed as unsupported.
.font(smallFont) applied to StreamOverlayTextView is passed as the child composable's style parameter; smallFont is imported from com.moblin.android.common.various.
color has default Color.White and iconBackgroundColor defaults to the imported top-level backgroundColor val from com.moblin.android.common.various.

Icon sizing chain maps to Modifier.size(17.dp, 17.dp).padding(horizontal = 2.dp).clip(RoundedCornerShape(5.dp)).background(iconBackgroundColor) so the background is clipped like Swift's .cornerRadius(5).
Swift's .contentShape(Rectangle()) plus .padding(-20) hit-area expansion has no Compose counterpart (negative padding is not supported); it is left as TODO().
enum case names differ in casing only, so the Swift and Kotlin sources can still be read side by side.

The four private enums with associated values (PublishMessage, SubscribeTopic, Message, MessageToMoblin, MessageToBrowser) became private sealed classes with hand-written JsonObject encode/decode that match Swift's synthesized Codable shape ({"caseName":{...}}, optional associated values omitted).
ChatPostSegment/ChatPostUrl are encoded by hand into id/text/url/bigGifUrl (url: {moving, still}) instead of relying on a serializer, because their Kotlin ports are not shown as @Serializable.
JSON is parsed and printed with codableJson; MessageToBrowser.toJson returns null when encoding fails, like Swift's try?.
moblinScript() calls loadStringResource("moblin", "js") from com.moblin.android.various.utils in place of Bundle.main url+Data.
NSObject, weak and @MainActor are dropped; the delegate is a plain nullable property.
DispatchQueue.main.async became CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main.immediate).launch.
logger.info/debug became Log.i/Log.d with the tag "BrowserEffectServer".
The class implements WKScriptMessageHandler in its header (the Swift extension) and is open with open members because the Swift class is not final.

The Swift diff merges two guards in layoutSubviews; Kotlin cannot combine two nullable unwraps in one elvis chain, so onLayout keeps two consecutive `?: return` lines, which are behaviourally identical to the merged guard.
No other Kotlin line changes: the rest of the file is kept byte-identical, including the Android hand-written measurement, drawing and AndroidView hookup.
ChatLineUiView keeps its own onMeasure/onLayout override in place of Swift's layoutSubviews plus sizeThatFits.
CMTime is ported to Long microseconds: `.invalid` becomes the sentinel Long.MIN_VALUE and `.zero` becomes 0L.

AVAudioPCMBuffer is replaced by the new PcmBuffer type (ByteArray + frameLength) because the original does raw memcpy of int16/int32/float32 samples, interleaved or planar; ShortArray alone could not express all three sample formats.
The AVAudioFormat stored in `format` is replaced by the new PcmAudioFormat type which carries sampleRate, channels, isInterleaved and commonFormat plus derived bytesPerSample/bytesPerFrame.
AudioStreamBasicDescription/`kAudioFormatLinearPCM` become android.media.MediaFormat with KEY_PCM_ENCODING; the guard still returns null for non 16-bit linear PCM.
AudioEncoder.makeAudioFormat is expected to exist in this package and to return PcmAudioFormat? for a MediaFormat argument.
Swift `init?` becomes a companion `operator fun invoke` returning AudioEncoderRingBuffer?, with the primary constructor kept private.
`defer` inside createOutputBuffer is translated by capturing the tuple first, then resetting latestPresentationTimeStamp/outputIndex before returning.
setWorkingSampleBuffer no longer wraps an AudioBufferList without copying; it wraps the supplied PCM bytes into a PcmBuffer view and derives frameLength from the byte size.
Added the new top-level createColorProperties(colorAttachments) helper right after createDataRateLimits, translating the optional lookups with ?.let and NSMutableArray-style append calls.
properties() now appends the HDR metadata insertion mode and then adds the three color properties produced from hlgColorAttachments instead of the inline ITU_R_2020 list.
hlgColorAttachments is imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.extension and typed as Map<String, String> (the Swift [String: String] color attachment dictionary).

The attachment dictionary keys kCVImageBufferColorPrimariesKey, kCVImageBufferTransferFunctionKey and kCVImageBufferYCbCrMatrixKey come from com.moblin.android.platform.video, so three new imports were added.

The per-format constants kCVImageBufferColorPrimaries_ITU_R_2020, kCVImageBufferTransferFunction_ITU_R_2100_HLG and kCVImageBufferYCbCrMatrix_ITU_R_2020 stay declared in this file because other files use them.
Everything outside the changed block (rate-control constants, Format, RateControl, thresholds, shouldInvalidateSession, bitrateProperties) is untouched.

The Swift file is wrapped in #if targetEnvironment(macCatalyst); the whole capture pipeline is Apple-only, so the three ScreenCaptureKit call sites are TODO() while the rest of the structure (delegate, latency constant, sample-buffer rewriting) is translated.
SCStream has no Kotlin type, so the private 'stream' property is kept as an Any? placeholder.
makeContentFilter returned (SCContentFilter, SCDisplay); those types do not exist here, so it returns Pair<Any, Any> with a TODO body.
CMSampleBuffer -> MediaSample; presentationTimeStamp (CMTime) -> presentationTimeUs (Long microseconds) and the 0.15 s latency becomes +150000 us.
sampleBuffer.imageBuffer != nil is mapped to MediaSample.data.isNotEmpty(), because MediaSample carries the pixels in data.
weak var delegate has no Kotlin equivalent; it is kept as a plain nullable reference (strong).
logger.info is translated to Log.i with tag "MacScreenCapture"; the start log cannot reproduce the SCStream width/height pixels, so it logs the filter/display/scale instead.
TODO() throws NotImplementedError (not an Exception), so startInternal/stopInternal short-circuit before the delegate callbacks run; the TS-adjustment callback logic is still fully translated.
apple_only: no Android counterpart for ScreenCaptureKit SCStream
no Android counterpart for ScreenCaptureKit SCStream.stopCapture
no Android counterpart for ScreenCaptureKit SCShareableContent

notes: CMSampleBuffer maps to MediaSample, so every presentationTimeStamp.seconds becomes presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0 and CMTime is kept as Long microseconds (deltaLimit arithmetic unchanged).

CMSampleBuffer.numSamples has no MediaSample counterpart, so frameLength is TODO(); startOutput, makePresentationTimeStamp and the whole periodic output path depend on it being supplied by the platform capture side.
formatDescription.audioStreamBasicDescription?.mSampleRate maps to MediaSample.format (android.media.MediaFormat) + KEY_SAMPLE_RATE; sampleRate is only touched when a format is present, as in Swift.

CMSampleBuffer.replacePresentationTimeStamp is emulated by building a new MediaSample with the same data/isKeyFrame/format and the corrected presentationTimeUs (MediaSample is assumed to have those constructor parameters).
CMBlockBuffer data pointer zeroing becomes latest.data.fill(0) because MediaSample.data is a mutable ByteArray.
consumeBuffer's inout Int parameter becomes a returned Int (Kotlin has no inout); the call sites assign the result.

Assumes the ported SimpleTimer takes the queue in its constructor and exposes startPeriodic(interval, initial) { } and stop(), that DriftTrackerMedia's entry is Audio and DriftTracker.update/addMedia keep the Swift parameter order, and that currentPresentationTimeStamp() returns microseconds.
logger.info/debug become android.util.Log with tag "BufferedAudio"; logger.debugEnabled becomes Log.isLoggable(tag, Log.DEBUG).
Deque<CMSampleBuffer> became kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque<MediaSample>; CMTime comparisons use presentationTimeUs and 'seconds' became presentationTimeSeconds (presentationTimeUs / 1e6).
The Swift 'weak let processor' is stored as a plain nullable reference because Kotlin has no weak stored properties; a WeakReference would have changed every call site.
deinit has no JVM counterpart, so it is exposed as close() and must be called by the owner when the BufferedVideo is discarded.
logger.debugEnabled maps to Log.isLoggable(TAG, Log.DEBUG) and the stats.getStats() call stays inside that guard so its short-circuit side effects match Swift exactly.
Assumes DriftTrackerMedia.Video and BufferedStats.getStats() returning Pair<Int, Int>? so the Swift tuple destructuring still compiles; adjust if the sibling Kotlin files name these differently.
replacePresentationTimeStamp is provided as a file-private MediaSample extension using copy(); if the sibling file declares the same helper, delete this one.
The inout 'numberOfBuffersConsumed' parameter of consumeBuffer became a returned Int because Kotlin has no inout.
processor.delegate is reached with safe calls (processor?.delegate?.streamVideoBufferedVideoReady/Removed) to avoid depending on its nullability.
Added the colorRange: SettingsStreamColorRange constructor parameter after softwareDecoding and forwarded it to WebrtcIngestClient, matching the Swift diff.
SettingsStreamColorRange is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings.

The dependency declaration listed for WebrtcIngestClient does not yet show a colorRange parameter; the call follows the Swift change, so WebrtcIngestClient's constructor must expose colorRange: SettingsStreamColorRange.
Everything else in the file (delegate interface, handleOffer, stop and the delegate overrides) is unchanged.
Only the three merged-guard hunks changed: tryPrintNext, handleMessageMxw01 and handleMessageDefault.
Swift's `guard a, b else` has no single Kotlin form; the merged conditions are written as one if-expression/let plus one early return.
In tryPrintNext the job is popped only when currentJob is nil, exactly as the merged Swift guard does.
handleMessageMxw01 and handleMessageDefault parse the characteristic value with `?.let { Command(it) } ?: return`, combining the value and command guards.
Everything else, including the Android hooks (Bundle.url, SimpleTimer, CBCentralManager holder, Log) and the JobState @JvmName workaround, is kept byte-identical.
startRunning now resets oldBitrateVideoSize to a zero Size, matching the new Swift line CMVideoDimensions(width: 0, height: 0).
CMVideoDimensions maps to android.util.Size in this port, so the reset is Size(0, 0), the same value used for the oldBitrateVideoSize field initialiser.
Everything else in the file is unchanged; the Android-specific launch/atomic/lockQueue handling and the Size-based adaptive resolution logic are preserved byte-identically.
No SwiftUI views are declared here; the file only provides data models and a formatter, so no @Composable functions were added.
Swift UInt64 usage/percentage values are mapped to Long, matching the Android side which does not use unsigned types for these counters.
The Swift tuple return of format(_:) becomes Triple<String, String, List<BondingPercentage>>; callers read .first/.second/.third.
Identifiable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped; BondingPercentage keeps its id property for LazyColumn keys.
RgbColor(red:green:blue:).color() is assumed to exist as a member call on RgbColor from com.moblin.android.common.various with Int red/green/blue arguments.
The file-private top-level `colors` array keeps its name and file-privacy; nothing outside this file can see it.
getNameColor uses indexOfFirst (-1 when absent) instead of Optional firstIndex, preserving the same colour selection order (Cellular, WiFi, then interface names offset by 2).
percentages is a MutableList so the last entry's usage can be normalised to 100 minus the sum of the earlier entries, exactly as in Swift.
RtmpServer gains the colorRange: SettingsStreamColorRange property, constructor parameter and init assignment exactly as the Swift diff adds them.
colorRange is forwarded to RtmpServerClient in handleNewListenerConnection; RtmpServerClient's constructor must accept that fourth parameter.
Everything else, including the ServerSocket-based listener, SimpleTimer periodic work and Atomic<BitrateStats> usage, stays byte-identical to the previous Kotlin revision.
Swift positionPort .init(rawValue:) with a fallback is already handled by the port range check plus DefaultTcpPorts.rtmpServer fallback; unchanged.

The Swift diff only merges availability and optional-unwrap guards; Android has no ASWebAuthenticationSession, so startSession() already returns false and the Kotlin guards already short-circuit in the same order. No Kotlin code needed to change.
Kept the hand-written WebView auth flow (getWebBrowser(context), WebViewClient.onPageStarted calling webView(view, null)) byte-identical, including the WebSettings.LOAD_NO_CACHE fix.
twitchMoblinAppClientId reads com.moblin.android.platform.loxen.Loxen.twitchClientId instead of the hard-coded test client id; preserved.
extractAccessToken keeps Uri.parse on the fragment plus getQueryParameter("access_token"), which is equivalent to the merged URLComponents guard.
isCanceledByUser stays a stub returning false: ASWebAuthenticationSessionError has no Android counterpart.
The UI still uses AndroidView hosting the shared TwitchAuth WebView inside a verticalScroll Column with CloseButtonTopRightView.
unsupported: ASWebAuthenticationSession and ASWebAuthenticationSessionPresentationContextProviding (startSession and presentationAnchor return false/null)

notes: The Swift extension on Model becomes top-level Kotlin extension functions on Model in the same package, so the two files can be read side by side.
`database.appMode == .chatPhone` assumes the port keeps an enum `AppMode` in this package with a `chatPhone` entry; `AppMode` is not declared here and must already exist.
AVAudioPlayer is replaced with android.media.MediaPlayer: numberOfLoops = -1 becomes isLooping = true and play() becomes start().
The member `chatPhoneBackgroundAudioPlayer` is assumed to be declared in the Model file as `var chatPhoneBackgroundAudioPlayer: MediaPlayer? = null`.
Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:) for the Alerts.bundle subdirectory has no direct Android equivalent, so only the asset resolution plus MediaPlayer construction is deferred with TODO().
`resetSelectedScene(changeScene: false)` is called with a Kotlin named argument; the parameter name must be `changeScene` in the Model file.
The long Swift switch lists every SettingsQuickButtonType case explicitly, all returning false, with `default` returning true; the Kotlin `when` mirrors this with `else -> true`.
No new types are declared by this file; it only adds extension functions to Model.
Merged the two guards into one condition with ||, matching the new Swift guard list.
Everything else is unchanged from the previous Kotlin translation.
Despite the ui tier, this file declares no SwiftUI views; it is a Model extension with control bar background image helpers, so no @Composable functions are produced.
UIImage is mapped to android.graphics.Bitmap and UIGraphicsImageRenderer drawing is replaced with android.graphics.Canvas plus android.graphics.Matrix.

URL.documentsDirectory has no equivalent without a Context: a top-level lateinit appContext must be assigned the application context at app startup, and controlBarBackgroundImagePath is derived from appContext.filesDir.
FileManager.removeItem is File.delete and Swift's try? becomes runCatching, matching the silent failure behaviour.
The crop factors (backgroundImageCropX/Y/Width/Height) and backgroundImageOpacity are treated as Float, since CGFloat maps to Float.
image.jpegData(compressionQuality: 0.9) becomes Bitmap.compress(Bitmap.CompressFormat.JPEG, 90, ...).
BitmapFactory returns null on undecodable data, mirroring the optional returned by UIImage(data:).
Crop + scale rendering keeps the same order as Swift: scale by min(1, 1024 / max(width, height)) and translate by -x*scale, -y*scale.

`ristCameras()` was replaced by `updateRistVideoSources()` and `updateRistVideoSourcesAndMics()`; the Swift `videoSources.rist = ...` write becomes `videoSources.rist.value = ...` because it is a MutableStateFlow.
`getRistStream(virtualDestinationPort:)` is deleted; `isRistStreamConnected(port: Int)` and the two id-based lookups stay unchanged.
The port-based `ModelRistServerDelegate` callbacks became cameraId/name/latency based; the delegate class overrides were rewritten to the new RistServerDelegate signatures.

The removed private `ristServerOnConnectedInternal`/`ristServerOnDisconnectedInternal` helpers are gone; the toast and buffered media calls now happen directly inside the callbacks, still on the main scope.
`updateRistMics()` is a Model extension in the same package and is called directly from `updateRistVideoSourcesAndMics()`.
This file is a networking layer despite being flagged ui tier, so there are no Compose views; the translation is a plain Kotlin/Swift-parallel API client.
UIImage is mapped to android.graphics.Bitmap via BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray; fetchKickProfilePicture therefore returns Bitmap?.

Helper signatures are taken as: httpRequest(Request, (ByteArray?, okhttp3.Response?, Throwable?) -> Unit), suspend httpGet(url: String): Pair<ByteArray, okhttp3.Response>, makeUrl(path: String, parameters: List<Pair<String, String>>), all from com.moblin.android.various.network.
OperationResult and NetworkResponse are used as sealed classes with Success(data)/Success(value), AuthError and Error members, as declared in com.moblin.android.various.network.

ChatterRole enum entries and the ChatterInfo constructor parameter names are assumed to be ChatterRole.Owner/Staff/Moderator/Viewer and profilePicture/bio/accountCreated/role/followingSince/subscribedMonths/giftedSubs/followers.

Swift property names are kept byte-identical (snake_case coding keys included) so kotlinx.serialization uses them as JSON keys; Json is configured with ignoreUnknownKeys to match JSONDecoder behaviour.
weak var delegate has no Kotlin equivalent, so it is a plain nullable reference; callers must avoid leaking KickApi instances.
KickApi was @MainActor in Swift: all completion handlers here are invoked on the OkHttp callback thread, so UI code must switch to Dispatchers.Main itself.
Renamed Model.rtspCameras() to Model.updateRtspVideoSources() and changed it to assign into videoSources.rtsp instead of returning a list.
videoSources.rtsp is a MutableStateFlow in the Kotlin port, so the mapped list is written with .value =, matching the other Model source-update helpers.
Everything else in the file is unchanged from the previous Kotlin translation, including the ModelRtspClientDelegate that replaces the Swift extension conformance to RtspClientDelegate.
The Swift diff is whitespace-only (re-indentation of the .first(where:) continuation line), so the Kotlin translation is unchanged.
No functional change, no new members, imports and declaration order kept byte-identical.
Only handleAudioMessageInternal changed: the separate timestamp guard and the data.isEmpty/decoder-state checks are merged into one guard, as in the new Swift code.
The merged check is written as one if (…) return with timestampSeconds == null first, matching the Swift guard order.
Everything else in the file is byte-identical to the current Kotlin, including the Opus decode path, the MediaSample usage and the platform shims.
Added the new setPhotosImageQuality() call in Model.importSucceeded, right after setExternalCameraVideoRange() as in the Swift diff.
Everything else in the Kotlin file is unchanged, including the hand-written Context-taking clipboard and data-import helpers.
takeSnapshot now takes age/isChatBot/message; the estimatedViewerDelay computation moved to the callers.
SnapshotJob no longer stores isChatBot and instead carries the takeSnapshot closure that performs the delayed capture.
takeSnapshotWithCountdown loses its isChatPhone guard and its isChatBot parameter, and takes the takeSnapshot closure.
Added takeSnapshotWebRemoteControl, takeSnapshotHeic and the shared private handleSnapshot, inserted in the same declaration order as the Swift file.
saveSnapshotToPhotos is split in two: the Bitmap overload encodes and then hops to main, the ByteArray overload writes the asset to Photos.
The Discord live-only check moved out of tryUploadSnapshotToDiscord into the call site inside takeSnapshot, as in Swift.
request.timeoutInterval = 15 has no per-request OkHttp counterpart on Request.Builder, so it is dropped; the shared client's default timeouts apply.
URL(string:).appending(path:queryItems:) is built with java.net.URI (scheme/authority/path/query) since there is no direct Kotlin equivalent.

srtClientCameras() was replaced by updateSrtClientVideoSources(), which assigns the mapped cameras to videoSources.srtClient.value, plus updateSrtClientVideoSourcesAndMics() calling updateSrtClientMics().
isSrtClientStreamConnected(id:) was removed from the Swift file and is removed from the Kotlin file as well.
updateSrtClientMics() is a Model extension that lives in the microphone model file; it is called directly with no import because it is in the same package.
Everything else (reloadSrtClient, stopSrtClient, delegate forwarding, toast/buffered media wiring) is unchanged, so those lines stay byte-identical.
The private serial DispatchQueue is a top-level private CoroutineDispatcher from a single-thread executor; every `lockQueue.async` becomes `CoroutineScope(lockQueue).launch`.
`images: Deque<VideoImage>` (swift-collections) maps to `ArrayDeque<VideoImage>`; `images += newImages` becomes `images.addAll(newImages)` and `images.count` becomes `images.size`.
`AVAssetReaderTrackOutput.copyNextSampleBuffer()` blocks and stays on the reader's own (lock) queue, never on processorPipelineQueue.
Sample offsets use `sampleBuffer.presentationTimeUs / 1_000_000.0` (CMTime -> Long microseconds).
`CIImage(cvImageBuffer:)` becomes `CIImage(cvPixelBuffer = imageBuffer)` and `.toEffectImage(isOpaque: true)` comes from com.moblin.android.videoeffects.
`try? AVAssetReader(asset:)` becomes `runCatching { ... }.getOrNull()`; the `guard let trackOutput` after construction is kept as a local nullable read.
The `[weak self]` in the loadTracks completion is dropped; the coroutine launched on lockQueue references the reader directly, as the completion ends with the load.
Pixel buffer output settings use the Map<String, Any> form with the kCVPixelBuffer* keys from com.moblin.android.platform.video.
BeautyEffect is a final Swift class, so it becomes a plain Kotlin class; @unchecked Sendable is dropped.
framesPerFade keeps the Swift declaration order: the stored default 30f plus an init block that assigns 15f * (fps / 30f).
setSmoothnessSettings/setShapeSettings keep the processorPipelineQueue hop, written as processorPipelineQueue.launch { } since the scope is already a CoroutineScope.
VideoEffectDetectionsMode cases are referenced as the nested members VideoEffectDetectionsMode.Now(null) and VideoEffectDetectionsMode.Off, matching the sealed class declared in VideoEffect.kt.
In executeMetalPetal the Swift local `var image` shadows the parameter; Kotlin forbids that, so the running value is named `result` and the parameter keeps its name.
`var detections` in addBeautyShapeMetalPetal shadows the parameter, so the mutated copy is named faceDetections.
guard let image, var detections -> an early return of the nullable image plus a smart cast; points.first/last become firstOrNull/lastOrNull with a continue.
The third parameter of addBeautyShapeMetalPetal is unnamed in Swift and named info in Kotlin; it is unused.
The Swift diff only merges two-statement guards into single guards; the Kotlin version already expresses both as short early-return chains, so no Kotlin line changes.
handleAudioSampleBuffer keeps the hand-written Android shape (sampleBuffer.data plus a size check against audioBuffer) because MediaSample has no CMBlockBuffer dataBuffer.
getOpusFormatDescription keeps the Android MediaFormat.createAudioFormat path; CMAudioFormatDescriptionCreate has no counterpart and never fails there.
The third hunk (CMAudioFormatDescriptionCreate == noErr, let formatDescription) is likewise absorbed by the Android MediaFormat path, which cannot return null.
Everything else, including the decoder release in stop(), createSilent gap filling and readHevcTimecode, is untouched.
Combined the two guard statements in the H.264 and H.265 decodeFrame helpers into a single `if (data.size <= 4 || !isPicture(...))` early return.
No other line changed; the rest of the file is byte-identical to the previous translation.
The Swift enum with associated values is declared here as a sealed class Dewarp360EffectSettings with nested data classes Direct and Animate, keeping Swift's default values.
setSettings posts through processorPipelineQueue.launch, matching the original processorPipelineQueue.async.
info.videoUnit.canvasSize is an android.util.Size, so it is converted with toCGSize() before being stored in Dewarp360Filter.outputSize (a CGSize).
The Swift comment about a physics model in updateParameters is dropped because Kotlin output has no comments.
Smart casts cannot be applied to a mutable property, so updateParameters/applySettings bind the settings value to a local val inside when.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped; the class stays a plain final class.
Dewarp360Filter and graphicsEpsilon are in the same package and need no import.
The Animate branch of updateParameters keeps the Swift placeholders: currentPan/Tilt/FieldOfView are assigned from the case payload as before.
final class CameraManEffect : VideoEffect gets a primary constructor; moveVertically, speed and alwaysMove are private var constructor properties.
highQualityDownsampling is referenced from the ported VideoEffect base class exactly as in Swift; it is not part of the declaration excerpt given in the request.
setSettings uses processorPipelineQueue.launch to stand in for DispatchQueue.async on the serial pipeline queue.
VideoEffectInfo.presentationTimeStamp is Long microseconds, so Swift's .seconds is divided by 1_000_000.0 at both call sites.
calcCropRegion keeps the stateful isStill / previousScale / previousIsRising logic; isStill.toggle() becomes isStill = !isStill.
All geometry stays in CoreGraphics types (CGRect, CGSize, CGPoint, CGAffineTransform) because the effect boundary is CIImage / MTIImage.
executeMetalPetal builds one MTILayer with the crop as contentRegion and yields filter.outputImage ?: image.
@unchecked Sendable is dropped; the class has no Kotlin counterpart.
OpacityEffect keeps its Swift shape: a final class becomes a plain class deriving from VideoEffect, and @unchecked Sendable is dropped.

processorPipelineQueue is a CoroutineScope in Kotlin, so the Swift processorPipelineQueue.async { } becomes processorPipelineQueue.launch { }; this@OpacityEffect.opacity is used because launch's lambda receiver is the CoroutineScope.
CIFilter.colorMatrix() returns the CIColorMatrix shim, whose aVector is a CIVector and inputImage a CIImage?.
The MetalPetal path uses MTIOpacityFilter directly, with opacity as Float and outputImage a nullable MTIImage.
The opacity field has no synchronisation primitive in Swift either, so it stays a plain private var read on the pipeline thread.
Unused parameter info in both overrides is kept so the signatures match VideoEffect.
The Swift private top-level helper makeGrayScaleColorMatrix stays a file-private top-level Kotlin function with the same name and return type.
SIMD4<Float>(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722, 0) * 0.75 becomes SIMD4(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722, 0) * 0.75f using the platform.simd SIMD4 Number constructor and Float times operator.
simd_float4x4(columns: (...)) becomes simd_float4x4(columns = listOf(...)) with the four SIMD4 columns in Swift order.
SWIFT final class GrayScaleEffect: VideoEffect becomes a plain Kotlin class extending the open VideoEffect, since a final Swift class has no open members.
The Swift override init() body is written as a Kotlin init block; property initialisers (CIFilter.colorMonochrome(), MTIColorMatrixFilter()) stay property declarations.
filter.intensity = 1.0 assigns a Float on the Kotlin CIColorMonochrome shim, so it is written 1.0f.
CIColor(red:green:blue:) drops to the positional CIColor(0.75, 0.75, 0.75) call because the shim's alpha parameter defaults to 1.0.
Both execute and executeMetalPetal keep the ?? image fallback as ?: image, since outputImage is nullable on the CIFilter and MTIFilter shims.
PinchEffect is a final Swift class extending VideoEffect, so it becomes a plain Kotlin class extending the open class VideoEffect.
setSettings uses processorPipelineQueue.async; translated to processorPipelineQueue.launch from kotlinx.coroutines.
The MetalPetal filter is created once as a stored property and reused, exactly as in Swift; its center is a SIMD2 so the Swift .init(Float, Float) becomes SIMD2(...).
The Core Image path builds a fresh CIPinchDistortion filter per frame and keeps the ?? image fallback via the elvis operator.
Float(min(w, h) / 2) is preserved by dividing the Double values first and converting to Float afterwards.
CIImage.extent and MTIImage.extent are both CGRect from platform.coregraphics, so min/width/height are Double.
pixellateCalcScale keeps Swift's Float arithmetic; 20/1920/5/1 literals become 20f/1920f/5f/1f and size.maximum() is a CGSize member returning Double, narrowed with toFloat().
final class PixellateEffect: VideoEffect -> plain class with an override of the open VideoEffect members. The private stored strength becomes the primary-constructor property.
The CIFilter.pixellate() companion factory returns the CIPixellate shim, so filter.center takes CGPoint.zero and filter.scale a Float.
execute/executeMetalPetal take the base-class parameter names (image, info); the Swift unnamed second parameter is not reproduced.
filterMetalPetal.scale is the SIMD2 member of MTIPixellateFilter, so .init(scale, scale) becomes SIMD2(scale, scale).
setSettings dispatches onto processorPipelineQueue (a CoroutineScope) with launch and qualifies the property as this@PixellateEffect.strength to avoid shadowing.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped.

ControlBar is an ObservableObject in Swift, so here it is a parameter whose StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState(); backgroundImage is expected to be a StateFlow<android.graphics.Bitmap?> and backgroundImageOpacity a StateFlow<Float>.
Color.black becomes Modifier.background(Color.Black) on a Box that fills the available space with Modifier.fillMaxSize().
Image(uiImage:) becomes Compose Image(bitmap = bitmap.asImageBitmap()) with ContentScale.Crop for .resizable().scaledToFill().
.opacity is applied with Modifier.alpha and .clipped() with Modifier.clipToBounds().
.allowsHitTesting(false) has no direct Compose counterpart and is dropped: the overlay contains no clickable or scrollable content, so it never steals pointer events.
.ignoresSafeArea() is a SwiftUI-only concept; the Box fills its parent's constraints, so the caller decides whether to extend behind the system bars.
No modifier parameter is added so the composable signature stays identical to the Swift view's stored properties.

final class WhirlpoolEffect: VideoEffect becomes `class WhirlpoolEffect(angle: Float) : VideoEffect()`, with the Swift `self.angle = angle` init body expressed as a body property initialised from the constructor parameter (same name).
`private let filterMetalPetal = MTITwirlDistortionFilter()` stays a private val of the MetalPetal shim; the Swift calls (`inputImage`, `angle`, `radius`, `center`, `outputImage`) are kept verbatim.

`processorPipelineQueue.async { ... }` becomes `processorPipelineQueue.launch { ... }` (processorPipelineQueue is a CoroutineScope); the mutation targets `this@WhirlpoolEffect.angle` so the lambda captures the effect, not the shadowed parameter.

CITwirlDistortion values are CGFloat in Swift, i.e. Double in the CoreGraphics shim, so `image.extent.width/height` stay Double and only the `radius` assigned to the filter's Float property is converted with `.toFloat()`.
`.init(Float(x), Float(y))` for the MetalPetal filter's SIMD2 center becomes `SIMD2(x, y)` with both components converted to Float.
`filter.outputImage?.cropped(to: image.extent) ?? image` keeps the `?:` fallback to the input image, as does `filterMetalPetal.outputImage ?? image`.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped; the class is not marked open because Swift declares it final.
A SwiftUI ViewModifier cannot be a Compose Modifier here because it emits a dialog, so QuickButtonChatLinkConfirmationModifier is a @Composable function instead.
@Binding var url: URL? becomes a value parameter url: String? plus an onUrlChange: (String?) -> Unit callback; setting null dismisses the dialog.
confirmationDialog maps to Material 3 AlertDialog with the URL as its title; titleVisibility is always visible in Material 3.
UIApplication.shared.open(url) maps to Context.startActivity(Intent(ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(url))) using LocalContext.current.
URL is only displayed and handed to the system browser, so it is translated as String rather than java.net.URI.
The View extension quickButtonChatLinkConfirmation is kept as a top-level @Composable that delegates to the modifier composable, preserving the call-site name.
The implicit SwiftUI Cancel button is provided by AlertDialog's onDismissRequest, which clears the URL.
Callers should place quickButtonChatLinkConfirmation(url, onUrlChange) alongside the chat content it used to modify.
BatteryView became a @Composable function; Battery and Model are passed in as parameters and are imported from com.moblin.android.various.model.
battery.level is a StateFlow because the Swift @Published property was translated that way, so it is read via collectAsState().
The private Swift methods percentage(level:) and boltColor() became top-level private functions; boltColor takes model explicitly because the Swift method read self.model.
Image(systemName: "bolt.fill") maps to Icons.Default.Bolt, which is only shipped by the material-icons-extended artifact; add that dependency if it is missing.
Circle().trim(from: 0, to: 0.5).rotationEffect(.degrees(-90)) is drawn with Canvas + drawArc(startAngle = -90, sweepAngle = 180) as the right half of a ring.
ZStack with RoundedRectangle + Text becomes a Box(contentAlignment = Alignment.Center) whose background is applied with background(Color.White, RoundedCornerShape(2.dp)).
Text(...).fixedSize() maps to maxLines = 1 with softWrap = false.
SwiftUI colors map as .white -> Color.White, .black -> Color.Black, .gray -> Color.Gray, .clear -> Color.Transparent.

The Swift change replaces @EnvironmentObject with a plain `let model: Model`, so FixedHorizonView now takes model as a required parameter: the Kotlin `LocalModel.current` default was dropped and the now-unused `com.moblin.android.LocalModel` import removed.
The Toggle/onChange body is untouched: the fixed-horizon write and model.sceneUpdated() call stay byte-identical.
@Published properties became private MutableStateFlow backing fields exposed as public StateFlow via asStateFlow().

Swift's hand-written Codable encode(to:)/init(from:) flatten functionData into top-level keys; reproduced with hand-written KSerializer objects (SettingsStreamDeckKeySerializer, SettingsStreamDeckLayoutSerializer, SettingsStreamDecksSerializer) attached via @Serializable(with = ...).
UUIDs are persisted as strings (UUID.toString() / UUID.fromString) because java.util.UUID has no built-in kotlinx serializer here.
Identifiable has no Kotlin counterpart; id is exposed as a plain java.util.UUID property instead.
SettingsStreamDeckLayout conforms to Named; assumed com.moblin.android.various.utils.Named declares 'val name: StateFlow<String>' so the flow-backed property can override it.
Assumes RgbColor, SettingsControllerFunction and SettingsGimbalMotion are @Serializable in their own packages and expose .serializer().
SettingsControllerFunctionData is treated as a mutable class instantiated with SettingsControllerFunctionData().
toString() on SettingsStreamDeckModel is an override of Any.toString() to keep the Swift function name.
Picker with .pickerStyle(.inline) is rendered as a LazyColumn of clickable rows with a RadioButton, one per database.streams entry.
Assumes each stream exposes `id` (matching Model.currentStreamId) and `name`; adjust if the Kotlin settings model names them differently.
onChange(of: model.currentStreamId) is translated to LaunchedEffect(currentStreamId) with a first-composition guard, because LaunchedEffect also runs on entry while Swift onChange does not.
DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 3) becomes delay(3000) inside the LaunchedEffect coroutine, which already runs on the main dispatcher.

Writing the picked stream requires Model.currentStreamId to be assignable from outside (e.g. a var backed by a MutableStateFlow); if the port exposes only a read-only StateFlow, route the write through the model's setter.
.navigationTitle("Switch stream") becomes the TopAppBar title inside a Scaffold.
The Section footer text becomes a trailing item in the LazyColumn.
pickerStyle(.inline) and labelsHidden() have no direct Compose equivalent and are dropped.
Only the onChange callback changed: model.reattachCamera() is now model.attachCamera(); everything else stays byte-identical.
The CallbackSignatureStateManager, the Row/Switch layout and the database write are untouched.
The SwiftUI View body became a @Composable named TapScreenToFocusSettingsView taking the model and database objects as parameters.
@ObservedObject database reads database.tapToFocus via collectAsState() on its StateFlow.

The @Binding write $database.tapToFocus is expressed as database.tapToFocus.value = value, which assumes Database exposes tapToFocus as a MutableStateFlow; swap in the ported setter if Database only exposes a read-only StateFlow.
onChange(of: database.tapToFocus) became LaunchedEffect(tapToFocus), which also fires on first composition, so model.setAutoFocus() can run once at startup when the toggle is already off.
Toggle became a Row containing a Text label with weight(1f) and a Material 3 Switch, matching the platform settings-row layout.
The toggle title goes through the top-level localized() helper from package com.moblin.android.
No navigation, sheet, alert or toolbar is used in this file.
scanner.discoveredPeripherals is a MutableStateFlow, read with collectAsState; the filtered/mapped InlinePickerItem list is rebuilt on each recomposition.
Swift localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("black shark") becomes contains("black shark", ignoreCase = true).
ProgressView() has no iOS shim, so the standard CircularProgressIndicator is used inside HCenter.
@State selectedId is never read in the Swift body; it stays as a required parameter so call sites keep working.
.navigationTitle("Device") is folded into Form(title = "Device"), which supplies the navigation stack.
The List wrapping the ForEach inside the Section is dropped; its rows are rows of the Section.
onAppear/onDisappear become a DisposableEffect(Unit) that starts and stops the BLE scan.
model.bluetoothAllowed is collected as state so the body recomposes when the Bluetooth permission changes.
layoutScale and the private layoutOffset helper are added; layoutPosition and move are rebuilt on top of layoutOffset.
metalPetalLayerPosition is renamed to layoutCenter (layoutPosition + half size) and its old body is dropped.
moveComposited, resizeMirrorMoveComposited and composited now take WidgetShape/WidgetShapePlacement from the same package instead of MetalPetalWidgetShape.

composited gained the resize parameter and reads placement.center/placement.size/placement.borderSize/placement.borderWidth; the border layer wraps cornerRadius/borderColor in MTICornerRadius/MTIColor.
shape.rotationRadians() is converted with .toFloat() and shape.borderColor components with .toFloat() for the Float MTIColor constructor, matching Swift's Float(...) casts.
move now uses alignment.mirrorPositionVertically() and alignment.mirrorPositionHorizontally() instead of the old isTop()/else branch logic.
resizeMirror computes a single layoutScale and scales by (mirror ? -scale : scale, scale).
Imports MTIColor and MTICornerRadius added; shape.placement and shape.cornerRadiusPixels are called positionally because WidgetShape lives in another file of this package.
Form/List become a single LazyColumn; the outer Section has no header so no header Text is emitted.
.navigationTitle("Streams") is rendered as a Material 3 Scaffold TopAppBar; remove the Scaffold if the caller already provides one.

deepLinkCreator.streams is collected with collectAsState() to replace @ObservedObject, and mutations assume DeepLinkCreator exposes it as a public MutableStateFlow<List<DeepLinkCreatorStream>> (assign via .value).
contextMenuDeleteButton has no Compose counterpart; long-press (combinedClickable) on a row opens an AlertDialog that deletes the stream.
onMove (List reordering) has no Compose equivalent without an extra library, so reordering is not implemented; onDelete behaviour is covered by the delete dialog.
CreateButtonView is used with a trailing lambda, matching a Composable that takes an onClick as its last parameter.
All user-facing strings go through localized() from package com.moblin.android.
makeUniqueName and DeepLinkCreatorStream.baseName are called positionally because their Kotlin parameter names are defined in other packages.
ThermalState replaces ProcessInfo.ThermalState with PowerManager thermal status constants (API 29 values, inlined ints); read the live value with PowerManager.getCurrentThermalStatus() on API 29+.
Enum entries are upper case in Kotlin (NOMINAL, FAIR, SERIOUS, CRITICAL); raw values 0-3 are persisted byte-identically via ThermalStateSerializer.

StreamingHistoryDatabase's @Published properties are public MutableStateFlow fields (totalTime, totalBytes, totalStreams, streams) so append() and migrateFromOlderVersions() keep the Swift member shapes; collect them from Compose.

The database itself is serialized through the private StreamingHistoryDatabaseSnapshot class because kotlinx.serialization cannot serialize MutableStateFlow; totalTime is stored as milliseconds and missing keys fall back to the Swift defaults.
UUID and Instant get explicit KSerializers (UuidSerializer, InstantSerializer) as kotlinx.serialization has no built-in ones in the default module.
UInt64 counters (totalBytes, totalStreams) and Int64 highestBitrate became Long; Int64.min stays Long.MIN_VALUE.
Swift's toString() became override fun toString(): String (it overrides Any.toString); fromString() keeps throwing behaviour by letting SerializationException propagate.
logger.info is android.util.Log.i with tag "StreamingHistory".

The Swift change replaces `@EnvironmentObject var model: Model` with `let model: Model`, so the Kotlin `model: Model = LocalModel.current` default is dropped and `model: Model` becomes a required parameter.
The now unused `com.moblin.android.LocalModel` import is removed together with the default value.
The rest of the file is unchanged: Form title, the empty-state Text, the ForEach with onDelete and the ContextMenuDeleteButton wrapper all stay byte-identical.
deleteNetworkInterface keeps its Kotlin shape with a Model parameter, matching model.networkInterfaceNamesUpdated().
Swift struct ExportSettingsView: View becomes a @Composable function taking model, defaulted from LocalModel.
@State URL? becomes remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }; the URL is carried as a String file path.
.onAppear is translated to DisposableEffect(Unit) calling model.exportToFile, with an empty onDispose.
ShareLink(item:label:) maps to the platform ShareLink composable, which shares a file path String as the file.
ProgressView() becomes CircularProgressIndicator with 20.dp size, formPalette().secondaryLabel colour and 2.dp stroke, matching the port's convention.
The HCenter wrapper from com.moblin.android.view.utils replaces the SwiftUI HCenter.
The result of the export callback is read back through the state, exactly like the Swift closure assigning to url.
catPrinterScanner is a shared scanner, so discoveredPeripherals is collected with collectAsState and read inside the Form body.
model.bluetoothAllowed is treated as a MutableStateFlow on the Model port and collected; change to a plain read if the port exposes it as a Boolean.
ProgressView has no shim in com.moblin.android.platform.swiftui, so HCenter holds a CircularProgressIndicator sized to 20.dp with explicit color and stroke width.
The iOS List inside the Section is dropped: the mapped InlinePickerItems are rendered with forEach and key(item.id) directly as rows of the Section.
peripheral.identifier.uuidString becomes peripheral.identifier.toString(), and the missing name falls back to localized("Unknown").
onAppear/onDisappear start and stop the scan in a DisposableEffect(Unit) with onDispose, so the scan is stopped when the view leaves composition.
Form(title = "Device") carries the Swift .navigationTitle and provides the NavigationStack; no Scaffold or TopAppBar is emitted.
selectedId stays a required parameter although the Swift body never reads it, matching the Swift struct's memberwise initializer.
Private helper views HeaderCellView and CellView become private @Composable functions; extra files keep the same names.
UIImage/SwiftUI Rectangle().stroke overlay is drawn with Modifier.border(0.5.dp), and the Swift modifier order is reversed when building the Compose modifier chain.
.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 5 * scale)) becomes Modifier.clip(RoundedCornerShape((5 * scale).dp)).
.foregroundStyle(textColor) has no equivalent environment here, so textColor is passed explicitly to every cell composable.
.minimumScaleFactor(0.5) is implemented by ScorecardShrinkText, which lowers the font size in onTextLayout while hasVisualOverflow, down to half the base size.
ForEach over 0 ..< numberOfHoles becomes a plain for loop; ForEach(golf.players) becomes players.forEach with key(player.id).
The .background modifier applied to a ForEach groups the player rows inside one Column with that background, as SwiftUI does.
The scorecardFontSize text sizes are scaled by `scale` and passed to SwiftUIFonts.system so the rendered scoreboard image matches iOS.
Model and DjiDeviceScanner are treated as state holders, so bluetoothAllowed and discoveredDevices are read with collectAsState().
The Swift singleton `.shared` on DjiDeviceScanner is assumed to be a Kotlin `object`, hence the default value `DjiDeviceScanner = DjiDeviceScanner` on the parameter.
@Environment(\.dismiss) has no Compose counterpart, so the view takes an explicit `onDismiss: () -> Unit` callback.
The nested List/ForEach is flattened into the single outer LazyColumn so there is no nested vertical scrolling.
The Section footer Text becomes a trailing item of the LazyColumn.
onChange and selectedId stay parameters; selectedId is part of the caller contract but is not read by the body, exactly as in the Swift source.
.navigationTitle("Device") is rendered as the title of a Scaffold TopAppBar, hence the @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class).
DjiDiscoveredDevice property accesses (peripheral.identifier.uuidString, peripheral.name) are kept name-for-name from Swift since the Kotlin model is not defined in this file.
SettingsSaveView is translated to a single @Composable function of the same name taking the Model as a parameter.
Swift's @State showSaved becomes remember { mutableStateOf(false) } with delegate read/write.
DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 3) becomes a LaunchedEffect(showSaved) that delays 3000 ms and resets the flag.
model.storeSettings() is invoked inside a rememberCoroutineScope().launch block so the call compiles whether or not the Kotlin port makes it a suspend function.
HCenter from com.moblin.android.view.utils is used as the Compose centering wrapper around the content.
Button label and Text content keep the exact Swift strings, including the emoji.
Swift `@EnvironmentObject var model` became `let model`, so the Kotlin parameter lost its `LocalModel.current` default and is now passed in explicitly.
The now-unused `com.moblin.android.LocalModel` import was removed with the environment object.
The Swift `HCenter { Button(...) }` remains the platform `FormButton(centered = true)`, which is the hand-written Android equivalent; unchanged by this diff.
`confirmationDialog` stays the platform `ConfirmationDialog` with `titleVisibility = Visibility.visible` and a destructive action Button.

ControllerThumbStickView: @Binding function becomes a value parameter plus an onFunctionChange lambda; the SwiftUI Picker + Section + ForEach is rendered as a Row with an ExposedDropdownMenuBox and the section header is dropped.

@ObservedObject anamorphicLens is a parameter whose published `scale` is read with collectAsState(); the handler writes back through the same MutableStateFlow with `.value =`.
Private View methods updateWidget, changeScale and submitScale became private top-level functions so the composable keeps the SwiftUI name and signature shape.
The Swift `valueFormat: { "\($0)x" }` closure maps to the `valueFormat` lambda parameter of TextEditNavigationView and appends the literal 'x'.
Double(String) returning nil maps to String.toDoubleOrNull(); the three guard error strings keep the exact localized keys 'Not a number', 'Too small', 'Too big'.
String(localized:) calls become the shared localized() helper from package com.moblin.android.
widget.setSettings(settings: anamorphicLens.clone()) keeps the clone/setSettings pattern from the Swift source.
Swift changed `@EnvironmentObject var model: Model` to a plain `let model: Model`, so the Kotlin parameter loses its `LocalModel.current` default and is now always supplied by the caller.
The `com.moblin.android.LocalModel` import is removed because nothing else in the file uses it; every other line stays byte-identical.
`httpProxy` is a settings class read directly (no collectAsState) and read through `collectAsState` here for `port`, `enabled` and `localNetwork`, which are MutableStateFlow properties.

The conditional `UrlsView` Section stays inside the Form at the same position as in Swift.

chatEmoteCombo.minimumCombo and chatEmoteCombo.resetAfter are treated as MutableStateFlow<Int> (the @Published mapping); the view reads them with collectAsState() and writes with .value.

.onChange(of:) maps to LaunchedEffect(value); unlike Swift it also runs once on first composition, which just reapplies the same settings.
setEffectSettings() is kept as a private top-level function with model, widget and chatEmoteCombo passed explicitly.
The call chain model.getChatEmoteComboEffect(widget.id)?.setSettings(chatEmoteCombo) is assumed to exist on the Android Model port in com.moblin.android.various.model.

NavigationLink wraps an inline Form destination, so the destination became a separate top-level composable DisconnectProtectionSettingsForm while DisconnectProtectionSettingsView keeps the label and calls onNavigate("Disconnect protection").
Picker with an optional UUID selection is rendered as an ExposedDropdownMenuBox row through the private SceneSelectionPicker composable.

navigationTitle("Disconnect protection") becomes the TopAppBar title of DisconnectProtectionSettingsForm.
SettingsScene is not in the glossary and is imported from com.moblin.android.various.settings; the collapsed picker text uses its name property.
database.scenes and disconnectProtection.liveSceneId/fallbackSceneId are read with collectAsState() and written through the MutableStateFlow .value property.
SceneNameView is reused unchanged inside the dropdown items, matching its use as the picker row content in Swift.
KeyboardSettingsView stays a single @Composable function taking the model objects it needs (Model, SettingsKeyboard); no @StateObject/collect wrapper class is needed.

String(localized:) is mapped to localized(); it is used for the footer kind ("a key") and for the new Delete menu label. CreateButtonView is called with a trailing lambda for the append action.

WidgetEffectWizardSettingsView becomes a @Composable function with the same name; the @Binding presentingCreateWizard is a Boolean parameter plus an onChange lambda, and effect is passed in so its StateFlow properties can be read with collectAsState().
The Form/Section structure is rendered as a LazyColumn with a section header Text, an ExposedDropdownMenuBox for the Type picker and a TextButtonView row for Create.

widget.effects.append(effect) becomes widget.effects.add(effect), so SettingsWidget.effects is assumed to be a MutableList<SettingsVideoEffect>.
model.resetSelectedScene(changeScene: false) keeps its Swift signature as model.resetSelectedScene(changeScene = false).
The toolbar CloseToolbar is rendered as TopAppBar actions calling CloseToolbarButtonView { ... } with a trailing lambda that sets the presentation binding to false.

Swift changed the model from @EnvironmentObject to a plain let property; the Kotlin signature already provides it as a parameter, and its LocalModel.current default keeps the parameter optional so existing callers keep working while new callers can pass model explicitly, as the Swift now does.
No other line of the Swift body changed, so the rest of the Kotlin file is kept byte-identical.
model.reloadLocation() is called only when stream.enabled, exactly as in Swift.
stream is a settings type read directly (no collectAsState), matching how the platform settings classes are observed.
TextEditNavigationView keeps its onChange = { isValidHttpUrl(it) } validation and the sensitive push key field.
`@EnvironmentObject var model: Model` becomes an explicit `model: Model` parameter; `let stream: SettingsStream` becomes `stream: SettingsStream`.
The SwiftUI `Form` with a single header-less `Section` is rendered as a `LazyColumn` holding the two rows.

RemoveBackgroundEffectView keeps its name and becomes a @Composable function that receives model, widget, effect and the observed removeBackground settings object as parameters.
The SwiftUI Section with its header becomes a header Text followed by the two picker rows inside a Column.
The @ObservedObject settings object is passed in as a parameter; its StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState().

RgbColorPickerView is imported from com.moblin.android.view.utils and is called as (title, color, onChange) replacing the Swift color Binding plus trailing closure.
updateWidget mirrors the Swift private method and stays a local function inside the composable; it reads plain values from the settings flows and forwards them to setColorRange.

SegmentedPicker, SegmentedHPicker and SegmentedVPicker keep their generic type parameters T and Content with the same parameter order as the Swift initializers.
Swift's @Binding selectedItem becomes a value parameter plus an onChange callback, matching the tier rules.
@Namespace / matchedGeometryEffect has no Compose equivalent; the selected highlight is drawn directly with a Modifier.background on the selected cell instead.
Global layout constants (zoomSegmentWidth, segmentHeight, cameraButtonWidth, ...) are top-level vals in this package, matching the Swift globals one to one.
Color.gray and Color.black.opacity(0.4) become Color.Gray and Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.4f).
The pickerBorderColor/pickerBackgroundColor globals keep their Swift names as top-level Compose Color vals.

defaultSegmentedPickerSelectedColor.color() is translated as a TODO() because the Settings color helper is not available in this file's glossary; replace it with the real conversion once Settings is ported.
The ForEach with Divider separators becomes a Kotlin for loop emitting each item followed by a HorizontalDivider.
Only submitHeight changed: the null check and the positivity check are now one guard, translated as a single `height == null || height <= 0` early return.
Everything else in the file is unchanged, including the Picker options/nullable id handling and the KeyboardType.Number mapping.
Existing hand-written Android adaptations (model parameter, LocalModel default, top-level private helpers taking model and widget) were kept as is.
Applied the diff: the Chat destination now passes model = model into WatchChatSettingsView; the rest of the file is unchanged.
model keeps its Android default Model = LocalModel.current so existing callers of WatchSettingsView keep compiling; the explicit argument from the Swift init now overrides it.
watch.chat still drives the hand-written conversion into com.moblin.android.view.settings.watch.chat.WatchSettingsChat, which is the type WatchChatSettingsView expects.
No imports, declaration order or formatting changed elsewhere.
@ObservedObject debugOverlay becomes a parameter whose debugLines StateFlow is read with collectAsState().

The VStack spacing of 1 maps to Arrangement.spacedBy(1.dp) on the Column.
smallFont from com.moblin.android.common.various is reused as the Text style parameter.

The conditional rendering of the whole view is a plain if around the Column.

No nav-compose dependency is pulled in; the composable is a plain screen body.

The label width keeps the Swift name `width` and is applied with Modifier.width(width.dp).
format is a lambda parameter `(Float) -> String` exposed as FloatFunction-free plain Kotlin function type.
Slider is imported from androidx.compose.material3 and Text from androidx.compose.material3.
The EmptyView label of the Swift slider has no Compose counterpart and is dropped, which is behaviour preserving.
No iOS-only API is used, so there is nothing to replace with TODO().
UIImage is translated to androidx.compose.ui.graphics.ImageBitmap so the QR code can be drawn with Compose Image.
The View body became a single @Composable function QrCodeImageView(image, height); the @State isFullScreen flag is a remember { mutableStateOf(false) }.

.fullScreenCover maps to a Dialog with DialogProperties(usePlatformDefaultWidth = false) whose content button dismisses the overlay.

Text("") used as a flexible divider is translated to Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f)) inside the Row, which reproduces the right-alignment behaviour of the SwiftUI layouts.

Row adds verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically to match SwiftUI's default HStack alignment.
The Swift views were structs with only stored properties but produce UI, so they stay @Composable functions instead of data classes.
No navigation, sheets or platform pickers in this file, so no navigation callback parameter is required.
No TODO() placeholders were needed; every view maps directly onto Compose.
@EnvironmentObject model becomes a parameter defaulted to LocalModel.current, @Environment(\.dismiss) becomes rememberDismiss().
@State var selectedId is never read in the Swift body, so it stays an unused String parameter (the parent supplies the current id, as in the Swift memberwise init).
model.bluetoothAllowed is read as a StateFlow and collected, like every @Published property of Model.

navigationTitle("Device") becomes Form(title = "Device"), which provides the NavigationStack.

Orientation and VideoPreviewProvider exposed @Published properties are StateFlow in the Kotlin port, so body reads use collectAsState() and the resulting Boolean/List values.
The Swift 'private func height()' helpers are kept as local functions inside the composables so names match the Swift source.

@ObservedObject parameters keep their names; their StateFlow properties are read with collectAsState() and written through .value (the ported settings classes expose MutableStateFlow).

The failable Swift initialisers MpegTsVideoConfigAvc/Hevc(formatDescription:) are called as fromFormatDescription(formatDescription), which is assumed to return null on failure - adjust to whatever the sibling avc/hevc files expose.
