FilesLocationView receives 'text: Text' in Swift; it is translated as a String parameter rendered with Text(localized(text)), so call sites pass the raw literal.
FilesLocationView's 'path: URL' becomes 'path: java.net.URI' and path.path() becomes the URI's path property, matching the hand-written platform note for this screen.
The struct's private methods makeSharedUrl/openInFilesApp/openInFinder/copyPathToClipboard became private top-level functions; model is threaded through the ones that need it.
UIPasteboard.general.string is translated to ClipboardManager.setPrimaryClip with AppDelegate.context, and UIApplication.shared.open uses the java.net.URI overload with its success completion.
RecordingsSettingsView collects model.stream with collectAsState before reading stream.recording.recordingPath, since model.stream is a StateFlow.
The Swift .sheet modifier on TextButtonView is translated to Sheet placed inside the same Section, next to TextButtonView, so it can animate in and out.
The multi-line ffmpeg string literals and the long Help paragraphs were joined into single-line Kotlin strings with escaped quotes.
Text is androidx.compose.material3.Text so it picks up the app's LocalTextStyle (17.sp body by default).

The SwiftUI struct became one @Composable fun StreamOpenStreamingPlatformSettingsView(model, stream) with the same name; the model and stream are plain parameters instead of @EnvironmentObject and a stored property.
The Swift methods submitUrl and submitRoom cannot be members of a composable, so they are top-level functions with explicit model and stream parameters and identical names.
Form/Section became a LazyColumn with one item per TextEditNavigationView row; .navigationTitle became the title of a Material 3 TopAppBar inside a Scaffold.
String(localized:) calls use the shared localized(...) helper from package com.moblin.android.
guard isValidWebSocketUrl(url: value) == nil else { return } became an early return when isValidWebSocketUrl(value) is non-nil.
onChange: isValidWebSocketUrl is passed as a lambda { value -> isValidWebSocketUrl(value) } because the Kotlin TextEditNavigationView takes a function-typed onChange parameter.
TextEditNavigationView is imported from com.moblin.android.view.utils with the same title/value/onChange/onSubmit/placeholder argument names as in the Swift call site.
No declared Kotlin types: the file only declares the composable and two top-level helper functions.
Swift @State var bitrate is filled by the SwiftUI memberwise initializer, so the Composable takes it as an initialBitrate parameter and mirrors it with remember { mutableStateOf() }.
model.isRecording is a StateFlow on Model and is read with collectAsState().
Slider step 32 over 0...320 becomes steps = 9 (Compose counts the values between the endpoints); onEditingChanged's end-of-drag branch becomes onValueChangeFinished.
.disabled(stream.enabled && model.isRecording) is applied to the whole HStack in Swift; in Compose only the Slider supports an enabled flag, so the Text keeps its normal colour.
The empty Text("") spacer line in the footer is rendered as Spacer(Modifier.height(16.dp)) to reproduce the line break.
.navigationTitle("Audio") is rendered by a Scaffold TopAppBar inside the same composable.
calcBitrate keeps its name as a private top-level function and returns Int (the Swift UInt32 maps to Int outside wire-format code).
Form/Section are translated to a LazyColumn with a header Text item, the bitrate row item and a footer item.
Adds the new SettingsStreamColorRange enum between SettingsStreamH264Profile and SettingsStreamRateControl, serialized with the Swift raw values "Full"/"Limited".

pixelFormatType() returns the OSType as an Int, calling the com.moblin.android.platform.video constants kCVPixelFormatType_420YpCbCr8BiPlanarFullRange and kCVPixelFormatType_420YpCbCr8BiPlanarVideoRange (with the CoreVideo shim every buffer is RGBA8, so the constant is only a tag).
toString() uses localized() for the two display strings, as everywhere else in this file.
SettingsStream gains a colorRange constructor parameter plus a Published(colorRange) property so Compose observes changes exactly like @Published.
colorRange is added to encode(), decode() (default .full) and clone() at the same positions as in the Swift container and clone body.
The two new imports are placed with the other com.moblin.android.platform imports, keeping the rest of the file byte-identical.
A companion fromRawValue is provided, matching the convention of the neighbouring enums in this file.
Nothing else in the file changed.
Form is rendered as a LazyColumn inside a Scaffold whose TopAppBar title is the Swift navigationTitle "Audio".
The Picker becomes an ExposedDropdownMenuBox; SettingsStreamAudioCodec.allCases maps to the Kotlin enum .entries and $0.toString() maps to .toString().
@State bitrate becomes remember { mutableStateOf(...) } seeded from stream.audioBitrate (converted from bps to Mbps).
Slider onEditingChanged(begin) is mapped to onValueChangeFinished so the new bitrate is only committed when the drag ends.
onChange(of: stream.audioCodec) becomes LaunchedEffect(audioCodec).
.disabled(stream.enabled && model.isLive) becomes enabled = !locked on the codec field and slider.
@ObservedObject/@EnvironmentObject properties are assumed to be MutableStateFlow and are read with collectAsState(); writes go through .value.
calcBitrate is translated as a private top-level function using kotlin.math.ceil to match rounded(.up).
PostView lost its size parameter and the red placeholder rectangle; the deleted-or-visible check is now the outermost branch.

The Kotlin BoxWithConstraints wrapper in MessagesView remains (it stands in for Swift's GeometryReader) but its unused size value and the now-unused IntSize, LocalDensity and layout.size imports were dropped.
state.deleted is still read through collectAsState so the row recomposes when the post is deleted.
Everything else in the file is unchanged.
The SwiftUI views became @Composable functions with identical names; @EnvironmentObject/SettingsStream model objects are now explicit parameters.
Model.objectWillChange.send() calls were dropped: Compose recomposes from the model's StateFlow updates, so no manual invalidation is needed.
Form/Section/footer became a Column with verticalScroll; section headers are plain Texts and blank separator lines are 8.dp Spacers.
ForEach + .onDelete + .contextMenuDeleteButton became one per-row delete IconButton that uses makeOffsets(...) and the private deletePriority helper.
Slider's onEditingChanged(begin) maps to onValueChangeFinished, which commits the clamped priority and calls model.updateSrtlaPriorities().
.navigationTitle became a Scaffold with a Material 3 TopAppBar (hence @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)).
Verify the Kotlin enum constant used in the when-branch: SettingsStreamDetailedProtocol.SRTLA (Swift case .srtla).
deletePriority expects a List<Int>, so makeOffsets(...)'s result is converted with toList(); adapt if it already returns List<Int>.
final class AnamorphicLensEffect -> plain class AnamorphicLensEffect, since VideoEffect is an open class and this is the leaf.
The Swift init(settings:) becomes the primary constructor with a private var property; the base VideoEffect takes no constructor arguments so it is called as VideoEffect().
setSettings hops to processorPipelineQueue with launch, matching Swift's processorPipelineQueue.async; this@AnamorphicLensEffect disambiguates the property from the parameter.
executeEarly keeps the Swift two-parameter shape (image, info) so it overrides VideoEffect.executeEarly.
The stretch crop filter is the CIFilter.stretchCrop() shim (CIStretchCrop) with inputImage, centerStretchAmount as Float and size as CGPoint.
filter.outputImage ?? image keeps the Apple fallback through the Kotlin elvis operator.
settings.scale is read inside the pipeline hop, so the latest settings value applies as on iOS.
@unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped.
Swift `deinit { stop() }` has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped; stop() must be called by the caller (VideoEffect.removed() is the natural hook).
The device-motion handler drops `[weak self]` and uses a WeakReference so the CMMotionManager does not keep the effect alive.
`minimalBoundingRectWithAspect` stays a file-private top-level function, with CGFloat mapped to Double throughout.
execute/executeMetalPetal override VideoEffect with the base parameter names; Swift's unnamed second argument becomes `info`.
CMMotionManager, OperationQueue and CMDeviceMotion come from com.moblin.android.platform.coremotion; operationQueue.underlyingQueue is assigned the processorPipelineQueue scope in the init block.
MTILayer is constructed with named arguments (content, position, size, rotation) matching Swift's .init(content:position:size:rotation:), and filter.outputImage keeps the `?: image` fallback.
The CIImage chain keeps Swift's translated/transformed/scaled/cropped calls from the Core Image shim.
`operationQueue` is declared after the other properties so its initializer runs before the init block, as the Swift `override init()` did.
Only the audio bitrate block changed: the nested `if let audio` / `if let bitrate` is merged into one condition in Kotlin, as it already was for the video blocks.
All other Kotlin code, including Android-specific Uri handling, `.value` flow writes and the `importSettingsFromFile(url = url.path ?: return)` hook, is untouched.
Swift's `self.handleSettingsFileImport(url: url.url)` already maps to the kept Android form `handleSettingsFileImport(url = url)`.
attach() now picks one photo shoot device (scene device or first device) and passes `device.id == photoShootDevice?.id` to attachDevice, so only that device gets a photo output.
takePhoto() now uses a single photo output taken from the first device that has one, instead of looping over all devices.
Swift's `params.devices.devices.first` is written as firstOrNull() to avoid an index crash; the Swift code crashes on an empty list anyway.
The photo codec selection (AVVideoCodecType.jpeg/hevc) and the IPTC metadata dictionary have no Kotlin shim, so they stay dropped as Unit markers, as in the previous translation.
The `photoOutput.supportedFlashModes.contains(.on)` check still has no shim; the Kotlin keeps setting flashMode whenever `flash` is true.
devices.compactMap(\.photoOutput).first is devices.mapNotNull { it.photoOutput }.firstOrNull().
The JPEG fallback branch (no photo output) still calls streamPhotoTaken() and returns early.
The Swift diff only merges two guard clauses in tagNameAndValue; behaviour is unchanged.
The Kotlin version folds the size check and the empty-value check into one early return, mirroring the merged guard.
Every other line of the file is kept byte-identical, including the hand-written Android WebSocketClient, MainTimer and AppDelegate.context calls.
No API or signature changes, so callers of tagNameAndValue and TwitchChatMessage need no updates.
@main MoblinApp becomes object MoblinApp (holding globalModel) plus a top-level @Composable MoblinApp() that creates the Model once with remember and stores it in globalModel.
Android has no App/Scene entry point, so MainActivity is added at the end to host MoblinApp(); it and AppDelegate must be registered in AndroidManifest.xml.

AppDelegate maps to android.app.Application, using Application.registerActivityLifecycleCallbacks to track the current activity so orientationLock can call Activity.requestedOrientation like the Swift didSet did.
Sub-views (StreamView, CameraPreviewView, StreamPreviewView) are passed to MainView as @Composable lambdas, which is the Compose equivalent of the SwiftUI view parameters.
Model @Published state (show, toast, orientation, database) is read with collectAsState(); controllers (webBrowserController, createStreamWizard) stay plain properties.

SceneDelegate is not used on Android: settings URLs come through platform/AndroidHost, and the external display scene is platform/uikit/ExternalDisplay (DisplayManager presentation displays shown with android.app.Presentation), installed from MainActivity by a hook.
.background(.black) becomes a Box with Modifier.background(Color.Black); .ignoresSafeArea() is a no-op because nothing applies window insets here.
targetEnvironment(macCatalyst) branches (storeSettings, replaysStorage.store, exit(EXIT_SUCCESS)) are not part of the Android build and were dropped.
BingoView stays a private @Composable function; since it is no longer a type, its private squareSize helper becomes a private top-level function and the local val keeps Swift's name.
BingoCardEffect's constructor takes a Compose Size (E6 convention, ModelScene passes one) and converts it once with toCGSize().
ImageRenderer<BingoView> becomes the non-generic ImageRenderer; the Swift arguments are copied into settings0/sceneWidget0/canvasSize0 locals before the content lambda captures them, never this.
@MainActor on setSettings and setup is dropped: both are called on the main thread as on iOS.
The sink's [weak self] is a java.lang.ref.WeakReference to the effect, so the renderer never keeps the effect alive.
minimumScaleFactor(0.4) plus lineLimit(3) is a Text whose onTextLayout lowers the font size while hasVisualOverflow, down to 0.4 times the requested size.
SettingsWidgetBingoCard and SettingsSceneWidget are settings classes, so their properties are read directly (no collectAsState) and the renderer's objectWillChange drives re-rendering.
.foregroundStyle on the ZStack is applied by passing foregroundColorColor explicitly to each Text; the cell and grid outlines use Modifier.background plus Modifier.border.

The only Swift change merges two guards in processMessageAudio; the existing Kotlin already checks the client first and then the body size in the same order, so no behavioural change is needed and the file stays as is.
All other members are unchanged and were carried over byte-identically, including the Android hooks (makePcmFormat, AVAudioConverter, MediaSample-based sample buffer creation).
processMessageAudioTypeSeq builds the MediaFormat via MpegTsAudioConfig.audioStreamBasicDescription() and attaches csd-0 from config.encode() for the AAC decoder, as before.
Only the chat-bot guard changed: the message-count limit moved into the outer condition and the inner if was removed.
The printChatMessage guards were already merged in Kotlin because CIImage(cgImage:) returns a non-null Bitmap, so no code changed there.
Everything else stays byte-identical, including the hand-written Android clipboard, coroutine delay and CacheAsyncImage calls.
The Swift diff only merges two guard statements into one; the Kotlin loadImage now combines the read and the CIImage construction into one expression with the same early return.
Everything else in the file is unchanged from the previous translation.
final class ImageEffect stays a plain Kotlin class; the DispatchQueue.global async stays CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Default).launch and the processorPipelineQueue.async hops stay as they were.
@MainActor dropped: MutableStateFlow assignments are thread safe and the effect methods are called from the same places as on iOS.
EmoteComboState's @Published properties become MutableStateFlow and are read with collectAsState (the emote URL is kept as a java.net.URI because CacheAsyncImage takes one).
ImageRenderer<EmoteComboView> becomes the non-generic ImageRenderer, and its content lambda captures local copies (state0, sceneWidget0, canvasSize0) instead of `this`.
The objectWillChange sink uses a java.lang.ref.WeakReference for self, as required; the sink fires only when comboCount > 0, exactly like the Swift closure.
SwiftUI's .stroke(color:width:) on Text has no Compose counterpart: it is drawn as an outline-only Text (TextStyle drawStyle = Stroke, black) layered under the white filled Text in a Box.
CacheAsyncImage has no modifier parameter, so the Swift .frame(width:height:) is applied by wrapping it in a Box(Modifier.size(size.dp)).
.resizable().scaledToFit() is Image(bitmap = image, contentScale = ContentScale.Fit, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize()).
post.segments.firstOrNull()?.url?.url(animated = false) yields a String in Kotlin, parsed once with URI inside runCatching before the combo counter is updated.

The iOS 26 scroll edge-effect block has no Android counterpart; the WKWebView shim's UIScrollViewFlags exposes no top/bottom/left/right edge effects, so those lines were dropped, matching how contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior was already dropped in this port.
Everything else is untouched: the Swift diff only added the iOS 26 availability block, so no other Kotlin line changed.
webView.scrollView.backgroundColor and showsVertical/HorizontalScrollIndicator still map onto the existing WKWebView/scrollView shim members.
DispatchQueue.main.async became CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main.immediate).launch { }, the main-thread form of the platform shims; the async block therefore returns with return@launch.
SwiftUI Canvas/Path/ImageRenderer are translated against the Compose-backed shims: the Canvas closures become Compose Canvas DrawScope lambdas and Path is androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Path.
In the Kotlin port DrawOnStreamLine.points are Compose Offsets, so each point is converted with toCGPoint() before being passed to transformPoint.
uiImage.cgImage is a non-null identity extension in the port, so Swift's optional chaining uiImage.cgImage?.toEffectImage() is written without the safe call.
SwiftUI .background(.clear).frame(w,h:) became Compose Modifier.size(w,h).background(Color.Transparent) so the modifier order matches SwiftUI's inside-out order.
path.addEllipse(in: CGRect(x:y:width:1,height:1)) is written as path.addOval(Rect(left, top, right, bottom)).
The class is a plain Kotlin class instead of Swift's final class, and @unchecked Sendable is dropped because Kotlin has no equivalent.
filter is left with an inferred CICompositeOperation type from CIFilter.sourceOverCompositing(), keeping the Swift property name.
makeFaceMask stays a file-private top-level function; FaceIconPlacement is a private data class replacing the Swift tuple return of calcIconPlacement.
FaceEffectPrivacyMode is a sealed class with nested Blur/Pixellate/BackgroundImage/Icon exactly as the platform layer expects (BackgroundImage holds CIImage?, Icon holds android.graphics.Bitmap?).

The detections-mode cases are referenced as the top-level Off and Now declarations in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.media.video, and sceneDetections() is imported as a VideoEffectInfo extension from that package.
setSettings uses processorPipelineQueue.launch and assigns through this@FaceEffect so the captured locals do not shadow the properties.
faceMasks keeps Swift's [Float: MTIMask?] cache semantics: presence is tested with containsKey so a cached nil mask is not recomputed.
UIImage(named: "AppIconNoBackground") becomes Bundle.image("AppIconNoBackground") and the cgImage identity property is kept.
rotation in the icon placement is Double because detection helpers keep Double math; it is converted with toFloat() only for MTILayer.rotation and negated for the counter-rotation.
FaceEffectSettings is a plain data class (not a settings-file class), so it has val fields and is replaced wholesale by setSettings.
The Swift diff only adds `font: settings.font` to makeChatLineStyle; the Kotlin ChatLineStyle call gains `font = settings.font` after `displayStyle`.
Everything else in ChatEffect.kt stays byte-identical, including the Android-only hooks (PipelineStats.increment, Dispatchers.Main.immediate, WeakReference, toBitmap/cgImage usage).
The settings.objectWillChange subscription of the Swift renderer stays dropped, as in the current Kotlin file: setSettings calls renderer.scheduleRender() instead.
`settings.font` is a settings value object passed straight through; no extra import is required because its type is inferred from ChatLineStyle's `font` parameter.

The Swift change merges the extent/size refresh check with the UTF-8 conversion check into a single guard; in Kotlin the message conversion cannot fail, so the guard simply stays a refresh check and the data is computed just before it, mirroring the merged guard.

Everything else in the file is unchanged and kept byte-identical: mapping to processorPipelineQueue via launch, the CIFilter.qrCodeGenerator() shim, and the Core Image scaled/toEffectImage rendering path.
iOS API usages (CIFilter, CIImage, MTIImage, CGSize) all go through the hand-written platform shims, so no TODO markers are required.
Swift Deque<CIImage> maps to kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque with popFirst() -> removeFirstOrNull().

processorPipelineQueue.async becomes processorPipelineQueue.launch, and property writes inside the lambda are qualified with this@SnapshotEffect to avoid shadowing by the constructor/setter parameters.

VideoEffectInfo.presentationTimeStamp is Long microseconds, so CMTime.seconds becomes / 1_000_000.0; the kCMTimeInvalidUs sentinel is turned into Double.NaN to preserve Swift's CMTime.invalid comparison semantics.
SnapshotEffect is a final class, so the Kotlin class is not open and its overrides still use override.
toEffectImage(isOpaque = true) is the existing extension from EffectUtils.kt in the same package, so no import is needed.
applyEffectsResizeMirrorMoveMetalPetal is called without widgetShape, using its declared default null.
showtime is the Swift stored property initialised in init(showtime: Int); it is a constructor parameter plus a body property in Kotlin.
PollState keeps its Swift shape: a private class whose @Published text is a MutableStateFlow, read in PollView with collectAsState like @ObservedObject.
PollView becomes a private @Composable function; scaledFontSize is a private top-level helper returning Float (CGFloat -> Float) computed from CGSize.maximum().

The Swift modifier chain is reversed: clip(RoundedCornerShape(10.dp)) then background(Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.75f)) then padding(end = 7.dp); the font goes through CompositionLocalProvider(LocalTextStyle provides ...) so it reaches both children.
ImageRenderer<PollView> becomes the non-generic ImageRenderer built from a lambda that captures only the local state copy; the objectWillChange.sink body uses a WeakReference in place of [weak self].
init(canvasSize: Size) takes the Compose Size ModelScene passes, converts it once with toCGSize(), and defers setup() onto the main thread as DispatchQueue.main.async did.
setOverlay hops onto processorPipelineQueue to publish the rendered bitmap, matching the Swift async block.
execute and executeMetalPetal keep the Swift logic: sourceOverCompositing filter with the overlay moved to the top-right, and positionComposited for the MetalPetal path.
@State presentingVersionHistory becomes remember { mutableStateOf(false) }.
SwiftUI Form/List is rendered as a LazyColumn inside a Scaffold so .navigationTitle 'About' maps to the TopAppBar title.

NavigationLink to AboutAttributionsSettingsView has no navigation-compose dependency here; it is exposed through the new onNavigate: (String) -> Unit parameter using the destination type name as the route.
.sheet(isPresented:) becomes a conditional ModalBottomSheet with onDismissRequest clearing the flag.
The ZStack containing AboutVersionHistorySettingsView and CloseButtonTopRightView maps to a Box with the close-button overlay emitted after the content.

Helper composables TextItemLocalizedView, TextButtonView, ExternalUrlButtonView and CloseButtonTopRightView are imported from their packages and called with named parameters (name/value, text/onClick, url/content, onClick).
Plain Swift Text literals are kept as plain strings; nothing in this file used String(localized:), so localized() is not called here.
No iOS-only framework APIs are used, so no TODO markers are required.
processorPipelineQueue.async becomes processorPipelineQueue.launch; property writes inside the lambda are qualified with this@VTuberEffect because launch's block has the CoroutineScope as receiver.
info.presentationTimeStamp is Long microseconds in the port, so Swift's .seconds becomes / 1_000_000.0.
VTuberFace is a data class with var fields; the value handed to the open updateModel is passed through structCopy to preserve Swift's value-type copy on hand-off.

Vision detection helpers calcFaceAngle/calcFaceAngleSide/isMouthOpen/isLeftEyeOpen/isRightEyeOpen are extension functions imported from com.moblin.android.platform.vision, and VideoEffectInfo.faceDetections is imported from com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.media.video.
.init(contentRegion:) becomes MetalPetalWidgetShape(contentRegion = renderedImage.extent), imported from com.moblin.android.videoeffects alongside resizeMirror/move/resizeMirrorMoveComposited.
VideoEffectDetectionsMode.Interval is a top-level class in com.moblin.android.media.haishinkit.media.video, so the returned mode is Interval(videoSourceId, 0.1).
The class is open because Swift's VTuberEffect is not final; @unchecked Sendable has no Kotlin counterpart and is dropped.
Unused Swift parameters (_ cameraFieldOfView, etc.) keep their names in the Kotlin signatures so call sites and overrides stay identical.

The Swift diff only merges two `guard` statements (size check + CGContext creation) into one; the Kotlin equivalents are expressed as a single `if (width > 0 && height > 0) { CGContext(...) } else { null } ?: return null` in makeCheckerboardImage and makeMaskCgImage.
Behaviour is unchanged: same early-return conditions, same order (points count check stays before the size/context guard in makeMaskCgImage).
Everything else in the file (Catmull-Rom path builder, colour converters, checkerboard painting, Core Image and MetalPetal caching) is left byte-identical.
CGRect has no value equality in Kotlin, so the file keeps its local `isSameRectAs` comparison helper for the Core Image cache, matching Swift's `cachedExtent == extent`.
Swift `processorPipelineQueue.async` stays `processorPipelineQueue.launch`; settings invalidation runs on the pipeline queue as before.
MTIBlendWithMaskFilter, MTIMask, MTIColor, CIFilter.checkerboardGenerator/blendWithMask and CGContext are all shim calls; no TODO() is needed in this file.
Replaced the inline scale min() computation with the shared layoutScale(layout, size, streamSize) helper from EffectUtils.kt.
Replaced the metalPetalLayerPosition call with the shared layoutCenter(layout, size, streamSize) helper, which returns a CGPoint widget centre.
Both helpers already live in the same package com.moblin.android.videoeffects, so no new imports are required.
Everything else in the file, including the hand-written PngCoordinate regex decoding, base64 image decoding and the face-detection pose logic, is unchanged.
Merged the two LUT-cube validation guards in lutEffectConvertLut into one condition, matching the new Swift guard with four clauses.
Merged the two guards in loadBundledPngLut into a single expression using ?.let, so a missing asset or unreadable PNG still returns silently.
Everything else is byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file, including the hand-written LUT data conversion helpers, the LoaderQueue coroutine scope and the processorPipelineQueue hand-off.
Bundle.url replaces Bundle.main.path(forResource:ofType:) and UIImage(contentsOfFile:) keeps the uikit shim shape.
SwiftCubeError cases and the SettingsColorLutType switch keep their previous mapping unchanged.

The Swift diff only merges the optional check and the change-detection guard into one statement; the Kotlin already performed the same two checks in sequence, so they are now fused into a single `if` with identical semantics and the rest of the file is untouched.
`guard let newLocation, ...` maps to `newLocation == null || !(changed)` with the local `val` smart-cast in the right-hand operand.
`size != self.size` is compared field by field because CoreGraphics sizes are value types (CGSize equality is width *and* height).
`isLocationUpdated` is still captured into a local before being reset, mirroring the Swift `defer` inside the immediately-invoked closure.
CLLocation is android.location.Location; missing bearing is -1.0 as on iOS and the `course` is converted through Math.toRadians.
Coordinates are translated with the CLLocationCoordinate2D.translateMeters extension from com.moblin.android.various.utils.
The snapshot completion runs on a background thread and hops back to processorPipelineQueue with a coroutine launch, as before.
No new iOS-only APIs appear in the diff, so nothing becomes TODO().
Removed the private SongRequestsView composable, matching the deleted Swift struct.
Removed its call site inside Form, so the PlaylistView now directly follows the add-song Section.
Dropped the imports that only the removed view used: Toggle, SettingsMoblinCloud and moblinCloudSendSongRequests.
Everything else, including all Android hand-written helpers (MusicPlayerState, MusicPlayerQueue, MusicControlButton), is unchanged.

stableBoundingBox comes from com.moblin.android.various, as in the previous port.

notes: @Published properties map to a private MutableStateFlow backing field plus a public read-only StateFlow, so the Compose/Wear UI can collect them.
StateFlow is not serializable, so each class is annotated @Serializable(with = ...) and carries a nested Serializer object with a private Snapshot data class that reproduces the Swift CodingKeys.
JSON keys and the missing-key fallbacks (17.0, true, false, 30, ...) are byte-identical to the Swift encode(to:)/init(from:) helpers.
The nested CodingKeys enums are kept from Swift for side-by-side reading; the actual element names are set with @SerialName.
chat and show stay plain mutable properties, matching Swift's non-@Published vars; the outer class encodes them through the nested serializers.
The app must serialize with Json { encodeDefaults = true } to match Swift, which always writes every key.
The types stay reference types (plain classes), so equality is identity based, exactly like the Swift classes.
Serializer and Snapshot are Kotlin-only additions required by kotlinx.serialization; no other API was invented.

FontFamilyPickerView and FontStylePickerView are private SwiftUI structs and become private @Composable functions; FontSettingsView stays public and emits its two NavigationLinks as siblings, exactly like the SwiftUI TupleView body.

@Binding var font: SettingsFont becomes font: MutableState<SettingsFont>; SettingsFont is an immutable data class, so font.style = s is font.value = font.value.copy(style = s) and FontSettingsView passes the same state down to both pickers.

The Swift List inside the Form Section is dropped: its rows are rows of the Section, and each row HStack becomes FormRow(onClick = ...) so the whole row is the button, with the checkmark drawn by SystemImage.
Form + navigationTitle is Form(title = "Family") / Form(title = "Style"); the FontStylePickerView List is wrapped in a Section so its rows keep iOS insets and separators.
.onAppear is DisposableEffect(Unit) with an empty onDispose, and it only loads the families when the remembered list is empty.
loadFontFamilies() (a static method of the struct) and fontStyles() (a private method of the second struct) exist as file-private top-level functions with the same names.

fontStyleName keeps Swift's grapheme-cluster semantics: hasPrefix/count/dropFirst are done with java.text.BreakIterator character instances instead of UTF-16 units, since the truncated suffix is displayed.

CoreText and UIFont come from the hand-written shims (CTFontCollectionCreateFromAvailableFonts/CreateMatchingFontDescriptors/CopyAttribute, UIFont.familyNames, UIFont.fontNames), and GrayTextView is imported from com.moblin.android.view.settings.streams.stream.
The Swift #if !targetEnvironment(macCatalyst) block is dropped: the whole file applies to Android, so both types are declared unconditionally.
LiveActionFunction is a Codable, Hashable struct, so it becomes @Serializable data class with the same property order (image, text).
LiveActivityAttributes conforms to ActivityAttributes, which is an Android interface without members, so the class header keeps the conformance and the nested ContentState stays nested.
ContentState is Codable, Hashable, so it is an @Serializable data class inside LiveActivityAttributes; 'functions' maps the Swift array to List<LiveActionFunction> and 'showEllipsis' to Boolean.
Section headers come from com.moblin.android.platform.activitykit, the shim that renders the Live Activity as Moblin's ongoing notification; never use NotificationManager for it.
The Swift property names become the JSON keys, so the activity content stays wire-compatible between the two apps.
The Swift labelled tuple (toLinear:toHlg:) becomes the file-private HlgKernels data class so the field labels survive side-by-side reading.
hlgKernels stays a file-private val evaluated with lazy, matching the one-shot Swift initializer.
Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:) plus Data(contentsOf:) collapse into Bundle.readBytes("default", "metallib").
try? CIColorKernel(functionName:fromMetalLibraryData:) becomes runCatching { ... }.getOrNull(), so a failing kernel leaves hlgKernels null as on iOS.
hlgToLinear() and linearToHlg() return the receiver when the kernels are unavailable, exactly like Swift's ?? self.
CIColorKernel.apply is called with named extent/arguments so it resolves to the shim member instead of Kotlin's stdlib apply.
The hlgToLinear and linearToHlg kernels must be registered in CIKernelLibrary (the GLSL port of default.metallib); otherwise the shim constructor throws and both functions pass the image through.
The Swift change only wraps the CIColor in `try`/`#require`, because the failable CIColor initialiser can return nil on iOS.
The platform CIColor constructor is non-failable in Kotlin, so no requireNotNull or try is needed and the existing Kotlin line already matches the new Swift intent.
The rest of the file is unchanged; the file is returned verbatim so all previous Android fixes, imports and helper implementations are preserved.

Only the waitUntil timeout in cleanupKeepsFilesOfKnownReplays changed from Duration.ofSeconds(2) to Duration.ofSeconds(10); the identical call in orphanedFileIsRemovedAsynchronously keeps Duration.ofSeconds(2).
Everything else in the Kotlin file is unchanged, including the Robolectric runner, the MutableStateFlow `.value` reads and the java.io.File writes that replace the Swift Data().write(to:) calls.
The @MainActor Swift suite becomes a JUnit 4 class; every test body runs inside runMainTest { } from com.moblin.android (TestUtils.kt).
posts, pausedPostsCount and paused are MutableStateFlow in the Kotlin ChatProvider, so they are read with .value; Swift's chat.posts.map(\.id) becomes chat.posts.value.map { it.id }.
RgbColor is imported from com.moblin.android.platform.swiftui because it is not listed in the glossary; move the import if the platform layer declares it in another package.
ChatPost.userId has no Swift default in the call site, so it is passed explicitly as userId = null.
Swift timestampTime .now becomes Instant.now() (java.time.Instant).
maximumNumberOfChatMessages is imported from com.moblin.android.various.model.
makePost is kept as a private method of the suite class, called inside runMainTest.
No ByteArray comparisons occur, so assertEquals on the mapped id lists is correct.
Merged the two focus guards into a single condition in claimFocus, as the Swift change does; the rest of the file is untouched.
reclaimFocusTimer still retries once per second while the view is detached or another view holds focus.
Swift's URLSession is replaced by OkHttp's OkHttpClient, the port's HTTP stack.
URLSession.shared is a process-wide singleton, so the Kotlin client is created once through a file-private lazy value.
The function keeps its Swift name and signature, returning the shared OkHttpClient.
No Apple-only frameworks are used, so the unsupported list is empty.
Added import for spokenEmoteNames from com.moblin.android (TestUtils.kt) and the new assertion in emoji()
Added the new emojiWithoutShortcutsHasNoName test right after emoji(), translated with runMainTest and assertTrue/assertEquals
assertTrue(cond) used for the Swift #expect(segments[0].url != nil) check
spokenEmoteNames returns List<String?> so the expected list is typed String? to keep assertEquals unambiguous
Swift ChatPostEmote is the Kotlin data class ChatPostUrl in com.moblin.android.various; it has the same moving/still fields and url(animated:) method, so the suite builds ChatPostUrl values.
Swift URL values become the URL strings, since ChatPostUrl stores String? fields.
#expect(a == b) is written as assertEquals(b, a), and #expect(x == nil) as assertNull(x).
The private stored let properties of the Swift struct become private val fields of the JUnit 4 test class.
No locale, time zone or main-queue dependency, so no @Config or runMainTest wrapper is needed.
ChatPostTextSuite is a plain JUnit 4 class; no main-looper work is needed because ChatPost construction and text() are pure.
The Kotlin ChatPost constructor has no default for userId, so the extra named argument userId = null is passed.
ChatPostEmote and ChatMessageEmote use String URLs instead of URL, so the Swift URL(string:)! values become string literals.
createTwitchSegments/createKickSegments take an AtomicInteger id in Kotlin, so Swift's inout id becomes a val id = AtomicInteger(0) passed by reference.
ChatMessageEmote lives in com.moblin.android.various (same package), so no import is needed for it.
makeEmotes and createTwitchSegments/createKickSegments are imported from com.moblin.android and com.moblin.android.streamingplatforms.twitch.
timestampTime: .now becomes Instant.now() since ChatPost stores a java.time.Instant.
RgbColor comes from com.moblin.android.common.various, not platform.swiftui.

HttpRequestParser and HttpRequestParseResult declarations were not supplied; their Swift shape (append(data:), parse() -> (Bool, HttpRequestParseResult?)) is translated positionally as append(ByteArray) and parse(): Pair<Boolean, HttpRequestParseResult?> and must be reconciled with the hand-written parser.
request.query is read as a Kotlin Map<String, String>, so dictionary literals become mapOf(...) and isEmpty() checks call query.isEmpty().
request.data is a ByteArray, so the Swift `request.data == "hello".utf8Data` becomes assertContentEquals("hello".toByteArray(), request.data).
The header check uses any { it.name == ... && it.value == ... } inside a lambda, so SettingsHttpHeader does not need to be imported here.
try #require(result) becomes val request = assertNotNull(result), which returns the non-null value; the Swift `throws` markers disappear.
#expect(!done) becomes assertFalse(done) and #expect(result == nil) becomes assertNull(result).
The suite has no Swift init, so there is no @Before setUp; no locale or time zone setup is needed because the suite only parses ASCII request strings.

Swift 'extension Model: HapticsDelegate' becomes a top-level extension function on Model; Kotlin has no way to add protocol conformance from another file, so Model itself must declare 'HapticsDelegate' in its own header (see Model.kt).
Model lives in the same package com.moblin.android.various.model, so no import for it is needed.
HapticsDelegate is not imported because the conformance is expressed in Model's class header, not in this file.

setAllowHapticsAndSystemSoundsDuringRecording() is a Model extension declared in the audio session file; it is called unchanged, matching the AVAudioSession shim's setAllowHapticsAndSystemSoundsDuringRecording(value).
No state, no coroutines and no Kotlin-specific workaround is required, the function is a one-line delegation.
CoreHaptics has no Android framework equivalent: CHHapticEngine is replaced by android.os.Vibrator, so start() plays a looping 30 s waveform at the given intensity and stop() cancels it.
sharpness has no Android counterpart and is ignored; intensity only maps to the vibration amplitude on devices that report hasAmplitudeControl().
The engine (CHHapticEngine) and player (CHHapticAdvancedPatternPlayer) properties both hold the same Vibrator instance, because Android vibrates directly instead of building a haptic pattern player.

engine.stoppedHandler, engine.resetHandler, engine.playsHapticsOnly, CHHapticTimeImmediate and CHHapticPattern/CHHapticEvent are dropped, so the generation-guarded private stop(generation:) is kept but never called.
The vibrator comes from AppDelegate.context (VibratorManager on API 31+, Vibrator below); android.permission.VIBRATE must be declared in AndroidManifest.xml outside this file.
delegate is a strong reference: Kotlin has no weak references, so an owner must clear the delegate when it goes away.
@MainActor is dropped; like the rest of the port this class is expected to be driven from the main thread.
start() restarts the vibration with the Swift shape: stop() first, then isActive/delegate notification and, when duration is non-null, a MainTimer single shot that calls stop().
The Swift suite is translated to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions; no @Before is needed because the tests have no shared state.
URL(string:) plus try #require becomes a plain String literal, since the three URLs are always valid and the Kotlin port of appleMusicSongId takes the URL as a String.
appleMusicSongId is called with the url argument; the glossary lists it without a parameter list, so if the Kotlin declaration is truly parameterless this call site must be adjusted.
#expect(x == nil) is asserted with assertNull, matching the nil result for an album URL without the ?i= query item.
The test results do not depend on locale or time zone, so no @Config or TimeZone setup is added.

Applied the diff: added the intro line, the three-step list and the guide link; renamed the alerts picker title to Message with a new footer; updated the wheel of luck footer; removed the Song requests section.
The numbered Swift multi-line string keeps its real newlines, translated as one localized string joined with \n.
Removed the now unused moblinCloudSendSongRequests import.
Everything else (Toggle, pickers, TextEditNavigationView, reloadMoblinCloud calls) is byte-identical to the previous Kotlin file.
The Swift diff only reformats the guard in moblinCloudTryNextEffect onto multiple lines; no behaviour changes, so the Kotlin file is unchanged.
makeMoblinCloudUrl stays as before: URI parsing plus percent-encoded path and scheme swap to ws/wss.
MoblinCloud keeps the RemoteControlStreamerDelegate overrides with empty bodies as in Swift.
remoteControlStreamerMusic still forwards to Model when the model reference is alive; the dead-branch result remains a TODO pending a RemoteControlResult error case.
The tip effect queue uses a Triple list and removeFirstOrNull, matching popFirst().
Renamed the tips view's Form title from "Tips" to "Message" to match the new navigationTitle.
Renamed the NavigationLink label from "Tips" to "Message".
Everything else is unchanged from the previous translation.
GeometryReader becomes BoxWithConstraints; the drag half-width is computed once in pixels so the gesture and the knob offset share a unit (the ratio passed to setZoomSpeed is unchanged).
The DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) is detectDragGestures; the offset accumulates drag deltas and is clamped with the existing Float.clamped helper.
The knob's animated return to 0 (`withAnimation(.spring)`) runs an `animate(...)` call in a remembered scope; the job is cancelled when a new drag starts or the view leaves composition.
Modifiers are reversed: bottom padding, 1dp rounded border (overlay stroke), clip, background, fixed 250x40 frame, then the inner horizontal/vertical padding.
`.foregroundStyle(.white)` only affected the two SF Symbols, so each SystemImage gets tint = Color.White at the default 17.sp body size.
`onDisappear { model.stopZoomSpeed() }` is a DisposableEffect that also cancels the pending spring animation.
The Capsule/Circle shapes are plain Boxes with RoundedCornerShape(percent = 50) / CircleShape backgrounds and a 2dp shadow on the knob.
model.setZoomSpeed / model.stopZoomSpeed are called as Model extensions from com.moblin.android.various.model; the model defaults to LocalModel.current.

The AVSpeechSynthesizer shim has no `write(utterance:)` buffer callback, so the AVAudioFile/AVAudioPlayer PCM capture path is replaced by speaking the utterance directly and passing the volume through the shim's `AVSpeechUtterance.volume`.
AVAudioFile, FileManager temp-file handling and AudioPlayer are no longer used, because there is no synthesized PCM buffer to write and replay on Android.
The DispatchQueue parameter becomes a CoroutineScope (`queue`); delegate callbacks hop onto it with `queue.launch { }`, matching the Swift `queue.async { }`.
`generation` is expressed through the identity of the last utterance (`current`), so late didFinish/didCancel callbacks for a stopped utterance do not fire the new `onFinished`.
`usesApplicationAudioSession = false` is set once in init so speech does not fight the capture audio session, as intended on iOS.
No TODO() markers are needed; the only iOS-only parts (buffer write, temp CAF file) are dropped rather than stubbed.
Swift enum with associated values becomes a sealed class with nested data classes Apple, TtsMonster and ElevenLabs.
The static find(voices:language:) moves to the sealed class companion object, keeping the same name and parameter order.
The Swift if/else-if chain is written as a when over the selected voice type with an else branch that falls through to the AVSpeechSynthesisVoice lookup, matching the original fall-through behaviour.
Only SettingsVoice, SettingsVoiceType and AVSpeechSynthesisVoice are imported; the settings types come from com.moblin.android.various.settings as declared.
AVSpeechSynthesisVoice(identifier) resolves to the identifier overload of the shim's companion invoke because a non-null String is preferred over String?.
Swift's URLRequest/URLSession is replaced by OkHttp's Request plus the existing suspend httpGet(request) helper, so failures use runCatching(...).getOrNull() to mirror try?.
baseUrl is a private top-level String constant; paths are built by concatenation like URL.appending(components:).
The Codable structs become @Serializable data classes keeping the Swift snake_case property names, so the JSON keys stay byte-identical.
JSON decoding uses codableJson and strips a leading UTF-8 BOM, matching String(data:encoding:.utf8) behaviour.
ElevenLabsVoice.countryCode uses java.util.Locale.forLanguageTag with '_' normalised to '-', and maps an empty country back to null like Swift's Locale.region?.identifier.
createRequest returns an OkHttp Request.Builder so the POST body and Accept header can be added afterwards, as Swift mutates its URLRequest.
The request always carries the xi-api-key header, exactly as createRequest did.
Text() comes from Material 3 (there is no SwiftUI Text shim) with the default 17.sp body size.
SettingsMicsMic.gainDb is exposed as a StateFlow over the internal _gainDb, so the slider writes mic._gainDb.value and reads it with collectAsState().
SwiftUI Slider step: 1.0 has no FormSlider counterpart; the value is rounded with roundToInt() inside onValueChange.
The .onChange(of: mic.gainDb) side effect becomes a call to model.updateAudioGain() right after the write in onValueChange, so it never runs on first composition.
SettingsMics.mics is a StateFlow, collected at the top of MicsGainSettingsView (the whole list) and inside MicGainView (the single mic's gain).
Form provides the NavigationStack and the navigation title "Gains"; Section carries the footer text through footerContent.
ForEach keys on SettingsMicsMic.id so rows keep identity across list updates.
Swift Testing suite ported to a JUnit 4 class with kotlin.test assertions; every async @MainActor test runs inside runMainTest so the Robolectric main looper is advanced.
Task.sleep becomes delay(); the reconnect-delay check uses ContinuousClock.now and kotlin.time.Duration from the platform layer.

WebSocketServerMock now stands on the platform NWListener/NWConnection shims. Those shims serve plain TCP only, so inserting the NWProtocolWebSocket options, building frame metadata and reading protocolMetadata are TODO.

WebSocketClient.stop(closeCode:) is not part of the platform shim (only stop() is declared), so the close-code argument is dropped and the client always sends the default normal closure; the privateCode expectations in the close tests only hold once that overload exists.
UInt16 ports are Int in Kotlin; url() returns the "ws://127.0.0.1:<port>" String that WebSocketClient takes instead of a URL.
WebSocketClient needs a Context, so every construction passes AppDelegate.context.
MessageQueue.get() times out after 10 s, so a missing callback fails the test instead of hanging the run.
The Swift deinit of the mock server is dropped; stop() cancels the listener.
unsupported: NWProtocolWebSocket.Metadata / NWConnection.ContentContext (WebSocket frames on NWConnection) -> TODO
